headline: LGH forms vigilance committee to improve patient care, monitoring
description: LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) constituted a high-level vigilance committee to ensure a patient-friendly environment, improve healthcare
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) constituted a high-level vigilance committee to ensure a patient-friendly environment, improve healthcare services and strengthen the hospital’s monitoring system.

Amiruddin Medical College Principal Prof Dr Jodat Saleem has formed the three-member committee, headed by Prof of Paediatric Gastroenterology Dr Hassan Suleman, while Associate Prof of Pathology Dr Amna Asif and Senior Registrar of Orthopaedic Surgery Dr Mubashar Farhan will serve as its members.

The committee will conduct regular and surprise inspections of hospital wards, emergency, outpatient departments (OPDs) and other units to monitor staff attendance, discipline, quality of patient care, medical records and availability of stock. It will also oversee the attendance and performance of janitorial staff, cleanliness arrangements, waste disposal, sanitation, infection-control measures and the presence of security personnel. Special attention will be given to maintaining cleanliness round the clock and ensuring alertness of security staff. In coordination with administrative doctors, the committee will take necessary measures to improve patient care, safety and facilities for attendants. It will submit weekly reports to the principal, highlighting observations, actions taken and recommendations, while cases of serious negligence will be reported immediately.

Prof Dr Jodat Saleem said effective monitoring was essential for improving institutional performance and ensuring quality healthcare facilities in line with the health vision of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif. He directed all relevant departments and administrative doctors to extend full cooperation to the committee and ensure timely implementation of its instructions.

headline: ACS orders faster execution of development schemes, improved public service delivery
description: LAHORE - Additional Chief Secretary Punjab Iftikhar Ali Sahoo visited the Commissioner’s Office in Gujranwala and chaired an important meeting of
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Additional Chief Secretary Punjab Iftikhar Ali Sahoo visited the Commissioner’s Office in Gujranwala and chaired an important meeting of divisional and district officers to review progress on ongoing administrative, development and public welfare initiatives across the division.

Commissioner Gujranwala and Gujrat divisions Muhammad Ali, Deputy Commissioner Gujranwala Naveed Ahmed, deputy commissioners of other districts and officers from various departments attended the meeting, said a handout issued here on Sunday.

The meeting reviewed the implementation of government policies, public welfare initiatives of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, progress on development projects, improvement of civic amenities and performance across various governance sectors. Additional Chief Secretary Iftikhar Ali Sahoo directed the officers to ensure effective implementation of government priorities and emphasised that no negligence or unnecessary delay in providing relief to the public would be tolerated. He said that the fundamental responsibility of administrative officers was to resolve public issues promptly, improve the delivery of public services and complete development projects within stipulated timelines. All departments were directed to achieve their targets through effective coordination, an integrated strategy and robust monitoring. He stressed the need to ensure transparency, merit and accountability in official affairs, directing officers to increase their field presence instead of remaining confined to their offices. They were instructed to personally inspect ongoing projects, public facilities and the performance of government institutions.

He further emphasised that quality must not be compromised in projects of public importance, available resources must be utilised efficiently, and practical measures must be taken to ensure that the benefits of development schemes reach ordinary citizens. During the meeting, Commissioner Muhammad Ali gave a detailed briefing to the ACS Punjab on ongoing administrative and development activities, departmental performance and implementation of government initiatives across the division.

He informed the meeting that work was underway on various initiatives, including the Suthra Punjab Programme, Punjab Development Programme (PDP), WASA and Local Government projects, Mass Transit Corridor, OSR schemes, improvement of urban infrastructure and provision of public amenities. Highlighting key development projects, the commissioner briefed the meeting on progress regarding the establishment of a library, construction and improvement of Classke Road, Lady Park Kamoke, Eminabad Family Park, Saroke Family Park, Nawaz Sharif Family Park Gujrat, upgradation of General Bus Stand Gujrat, Dak Khana Road Mandi Bahauddin, Sublime Chowk Sialkot, upgradation of Iqbal Manzil, Khayaban-e-Iqbal Park and Sagar Road Hafizabad, among other schemes. He also briefed the meeting on Narowal Public School, various beautification schemes and projects aimed at improving basic civic facilities in urban areas.

The meeting was further informed about the Chief Minister Punjab’s Apni Chhat Apna Ghar Programme and ongoing initiatives in the agriculture sector, including agricultural extension services, Kisan Card, Green Tractor Scheme and the establishment of model farms.

The implementation status of other public welfare initiatives was also reviewed, including measures against hoarding and profiteering, the Chief Minister Punjab’s Electric Green Buses, the Clean Water Programme and other public facilitation projects.

Regarding governance and administrative reforms, the Commissioner highlighted various initiatives, including the Governance Initiative, e-Foas, e-Biz, Apna Khet Apna Rozgar, digitisation of revenue estates and computerisation of revenue records, including Khewat and Intiqalat.

He said that these initiatives aimed to promote transparency in the government system, facilitate public service delivery, ensure effective redressal of public grievances and modernise administrative processes.

Reviewing the progress of ongoing projects and departmental performance across Gujranwala and Gujrat divisions, Additional Chief Secretary Iftikhar Ali Sahoo directed the concerned departments to accelerate work on all development schemes, strengthen monitoring mechanisms to achieve stipulated targets and immediately remove bottlenecks hindering project completion. He made it clear that delays in projects of public importance would not be tolerated and directed officers at all levels to demonstrate responsibility and ensure that the benefits of government initiatives reached the people.

Officers from various departments also presented updates on ongoing projects, departmental performance and future action plans.

The ACS directed all relevant institutions to work in close coordination to achieve administrative and development targets, reiterating that public relief, improved governance and continuity of the development process must remain their foremost priorities.

headline: Lahore ranks as most polluted city in world as AQI reaches hazardous 448
description: LAHORE - Air pollution in the provincial capital has reached dangerous levels due to severe smog, with the city’s overall Air Quality Index (AQI)
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Air pollution in the provincial capital has reached dangerous levels due to severe smog, with the city’s overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at a hazardous 448, making Lahore the most polluted city in the world, according to Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) sources on Sunday.

Statistical data revealed severe pollution levels across various localities of the city, with Iqbal Town recording a peak AQI of 617, followed by Paragon City at 513, Model Town at 453, Chaman Park at 430, Barki Road at 427, and DHA Phase 5 at 324. Health and environmental experts have advised citizens to strictly adhere to preventive measures, urging them to wear face masks when stepping outdoors and to avoid unnecessary travel, particularly during early morning and late evening hours.

Residents have been further cautioned to limit outdoor activities and minimise prolonged exposure to polluted ambient air. Experts warned that high smog levels can lead to eye irritation, nasal and throat discomfort, breathing difficulties, and severe lung-related illnesses, advising children, the elderly, and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions to exercise extra caution.

In view of the worsening air quality, authorities have urged the public to remain indoors unless necessary and follow official safety guidelines to protect against health hazards.

headline: Punjab IGP declares violence against women, children ‘red line’
description: LAHORE - Punab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Karim on Sunday declared that incidents of abuse and violence against women and children are a
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Punab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Karim on Sunday declared that incidents of abuse and violence against women and children are a “red line” under Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s “Safe Punjab Vision”, directing officers to prioritise the timely resolution of such cases.

According to a spokesperson, presiding over a review meeting on investigation affairs, serious crimes, and prosecution progress, the IGP instructed police commanders to accelerate efforts for the swift logical conclusion of heinous offenses, including murder and kidnapping.

IGP Abdul Karim ordered all district police officers (DPOs) to update data regarding challans (charge sheets) and proclaimed offenders from 2024 to date on the Police Record Management System (PRMS) by November 15, categorised region-wise.

He directed DPOs to assign specific targets to sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and station house officers (SHOs) within set timeframes, while personally reviewing first information reports (FIRs) of serious crimes and evaluating officer performance through regular inspections.

To ensure effective court proceedings, the provincial police chief instructed investigation officers to brief their respective DPOs before appearing in court and to present complete records during hearings. He further directed regional police officers (RPOs) to enhance coordination between investigation officers and prosecutors to streamline the case submission mechanism.

Reiterating his zero-tolerance policy on discipline, Abdul Karim emphasised that strict accountability will continue for personnel found involved in corruption, abuse of power, or breach of official code of conduct.

The meeting also reviewed measures and a strategy to improve coordination between investigation officers and the prosecution. The IGP directed the RPOs to set targets aimed at making the investigation and ‘challaning’ (case submission) mechanisms more effective. Abdul Karim made it clear that strict accountability will continue for personnel involved in corruption, abuse of authority, or violations of the code of conduct.

headline: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in India’s Manipur state
description: Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India’s northeastern state of Manipur, police said on Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India’s northeastern state of Manipur, police said on Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in the conflict-hit region. Three men from the Kuki tribal group were killed in an exchange of gunfire between “unidentified armed miscreants” in the state’s Noney district on Saturday, according to a police statement.

The bodies of two other men from the same community, who had gone missing earlier this week, were recovered in Kangpokpi district on Sunday morning after security personnel launched a search operation, a second police statement said.

A top Kuki tribal body blamed Naga separatist outfits for the killings, describing them as a “direct unprovoked assault . . . in their homeland.” The killings came amid mass protests attended by hundreds of thousands of people in the state capital Imphal and other areas, demanding the abrogation of a ceasefire arrangement between Kuki armed groups and the Indian state. The predominantly Christian Kuki and Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state. The latest fighting erupted after a Naga man was allegedly assaulted by men from the Kuki community in February this year.

The killing of three Kuki pastors in May, allegedly by Naga armed groups, triggered a series of retaliatory abductions and killings by both sides. The latest Kuki-Naga clashes have added to tensions in Manipur, where the Kuki community is also embroiled in a bloody ethnic conflict with the mainly Hindu Meitei community that began in May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas. More than 60,000 people displaced by the conflict, which has claimed more than 300 lives, continue to live in temporary shelters.

headline: One killed, eight injured in factory cylinder blast
description: LAHORE - A worker was killed while eight others sustained injuries after a massive gas cylinder explosion occurred at the Shezan Bakers factory on Guru Mangat
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - A worker was killed while eight others sustained injuries after a massive gas cylinder explosion occurred at the Shezan Bakers factory on Guru Mangat Road in Gulberg here on Sunday. According to Rescue 1122, the explosion, triggered by a gas leak in the baking section on the first floor of the factory, was so intense that it shook nearby buildings and caused a portion of the floor to collapse, sparking a fire. More than 40 employees were working in the building at the time of the blast.

Upon receiving information, police and Rescue 1122 teams reached the spot, cordoned off the area, and launched a rescue operation to evacuate trapped workers from the affected section.

Rescue authorities confirmed that 35-year-old worker Sajid, son of Fareed, succumbed to his injuries during the incident, while eight others suffered injuries due to the impact of the blast and falling debris. The injured, identified as Saleem, Hanif, Nawaz, Munir, Ishtiaq, and three others, were shifted to a nearby hospital for emergency medical treatment.

Police secured the site and initiated an investigation into the cause of the gas leak.

headline: Israeli leader warns Netanyahu can use new attack on Iran to stay in power
description: Yarusalem - Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan warned Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could exploit a potential new military attack on Iran to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Yarusalem - Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan warned Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could exploit a potential new military attack on Iran to remain in power amid political uncertainty following last week’s elections. “The likelihood of another round of fighting with Iran is growing,” Golan wrote on United States social media platform X. “We have reached a point of repeated rounds of fighting with Iran, and this shows just how much Netanyahu has failed,” he added.

His remarks came amid Israeli and US media reports suggesting that Israel and Washington could launch another attack on Iran after the US midterm elections scheduled for Tuesday, November 3. Golan said Netanyahu “lacks the moral legitimacy, and even the basic capacity” to manage another conflict with Iran. He called for the formation of an alternative government, warning that Israel’s security could be endangered under Netanyahu’s leadership. Golan said forming a new government as soon as possible was “of utmost importance, as Israel’s security and the safety of its citizens are at stake.” The warning came after neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition parties secured enough seats to form a government in last Tuesday’s parliamentary elections.

Preliminary results showed Netanyahu’s bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Jewish opposition parties and 19 for Palestinian parties. The results left all blocs short of the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority. The inconclusive election results have raised several possible scenarios, including a government backed by Palestinian parties, a unity government or another election. Netanyahu, 76, faces an ongoing corruption trial involving charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, which could result in imprisonment if he is convicted. He has also been wanted by the International Criminal Court since 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians during Israel’s war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

headline: Man stabs wife, five children over domestic dispute
description: LAHORE - A man allegedly attacked his wife and five children with a knife following a domestic dispute near Hakim Chowk in the Nishtar Colony area here
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - A man allegedly attacked his wife and five children with a knife following a domestic dispute near Hakim Chowk in the Nishtar Colony area here on Sunday. According to a spokesperson, the suspect, identified as Arshad, went to his in-laws’ residence to reconcile with his estranged wife, but she refused to return home with him. Enraged by her refusal, the suspect launched a violent knife attack on his wife. Police stated that the five children intervened in an attempt to save their mother, resulting in all of them sustaining knife injuries during the scuffle. Following the incident, police and rescue teams reached the spot and shifted the injured woman and her five children to General Hospital for emergency medical treatment.

headline: French protest violence eases, scattered riots hit Germany
description: PARIS - French authorities expressed relief Sunday after mass protests over rising living costs resulted in less violence than previous weekends. But police
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
PARIS - French authorities expressed relief Sunday after mass protests over rising living costs resulted in less violence than previous weekends. But police expect new demonstrations as high schools at the heart of the movement reopen Monday after their autumn break. Germany faced its own challenges after nationwide protests Saturday ended with rioters attacking police and looting stores in some cities. Around Europe, hundreds of thousands joined overwhelmingly peaceful marches Saturday inspired by young people, despite scattered unrest. In Paris, rioters targeted police with Molotov cocktails at the end of Saturday’s march on the city’s eastern edge, injuring three officers and setting a car ablaze, police said. Across town, masked groups hurled fireworks at officers at a viewpoint across from the Eiffel Tower, and police charged repeatedly, sending panicked tourists fleeing the area. Overall, however, the violence was less severe than on Oct. 17, when a city hall was torched and more than 2,000 stores were looted in hours of violence that authorities seemed unprepared to control, or during follow-up protests Oct. 24.

Police had arrested 779 people as of Saturday night, compared with 2,628 on Oct. 17 and 1,314 last weekend. Paris and Marseille police said a handful of shops were targeted but no major damage was reported. A national police official said Sunday authorities had prepared for a larger turnout of both peaceful marchers and troublemakers. About 70,000 police were deployed around the country. Police are preparing for more tensions as schools reopen Monday and as student groups and labor unions call for new nationwide protests on Tuesday and Thursday, the official saod. The official spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to be publicly named according to police policy.

More than 100,000 mostly young people protested peacefully across Germany on Saturday, demanding that the government invest more money in education, housing, climate protection and make daily life more affordable. In some cities the protests turned violent at night. Following a demonstration in Frankfurt, rioters attacked police downtown and looted stores. More than 100 officers were injured and 54 people — aged 13 to 29 — were detained. It wasn’t clear how many of the protesters were injured. Police said 17 stores were damaged and five of those were looted. After police cordoned off an area in the city center, the situation calmed down by early Sunday morning. “I am shocked by the violent excesses in Frankfurt, which will not go unpunished,” said Boris Rhein, the governor of Hesse, where Frankfurt is located. “Anyone who behaves like the attackers in downtown Frankfurt places themselves outside our society.’’

Violence also broke out Saturday night in Cologne, where police used water cannons to disperse the crowd. In Berlin, protesters attacked police with bottles and pyrotechnics.

The organizers of Saturday’s protests, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z’s got this” — posted a statement on Instagram distancing itself from “any form of violence, as well as violent acts by other groups or individuals” who were not part of the demonstrations. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt accused “violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the immigrant community’’ of hijacking peaceful demonstrations. “The rioters and looters will be identified and held accountable,’’ Dobrindt told daily paper Bild on Sunday.

In Portugal, riot police overnight removed protesters by force from a square in Lisbon following protests for more affordable housing. Thousands of people marched through the city during the day and at the end a few hundred camped out in Rossio, an iconic square in downtown Lisbon. Police intervened early Sunday, removing tents and pushing people away, and a few were detained.

Portuguese demonstrators have been protesting for weeks following inspiration from the Spanish movement to call out rising living costs, especially housing costs.

headline: Somali pirates seize Iranian fishing vessel, raising fears of attacks on cargo ships
description: MOGADISHU, Somalia - Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Center Indian Ocean said, warning that the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MOGADISHU, Somalia - Somali pirates have seized an Iranian fishing vessel carrying 23 people, the Maritime Security Center Indian Ocean said, warning that the ship was approaching a commercial shipping lane and could become a floating base for further attacks. The Azini was hijacked Thursday between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, a maritime security officer with the Puntland Maritime Police Force said Sunday. The officer said that 12 pirates seized the vessel, which was carrying 21 Iranian crew members and two Somali security guards. He spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to speak with the media. The crew’s safety was unknown, the center said in an alert dated Saturday. In an updated warning, it said that pirates could use the vessel as a “mother ship” to support attacks on commercial vessels. The European Union’s naval Operation Atalanta was investigating. The center urged ships in the area to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity. The seizure follows a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. By August, pirates had hijacked six commercial vessels since April, with some attacks taking place far from Somalia’s coastline. The captures included the oil products tanker Sibu 1, seized about 136 nautical miles (252 kilometers) east of al-Mukalla, Yemen.

headline: NCCIA arrests three suspects for blackmailing women through social media
description: LAHORE - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested three suspects for allegedly harassing, blackmailing and defaming women through social
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested three suspects for allegedly harassing, blackmailing and defaming women through social media in separate incidents, including two arrests in Lahore and one in Faisalabad. NCCIA Lahore Zone Additional Director Atif Ameer told media on Sunday that a suspect was arrested from Engineering Town, Lahore, for allegedly blackmailing a woman from Multan Cantt after obtaining her private pictures and videos on the pretext of marriage.

The suspect had also allegedly gained unauthorized access to her Snapchat account and demanded money from her. He also created a fake TikTok account in her name and shared her pictures.

The victim’s private data was recovered from the mobile phone seized from the suspect, who belongs to Arifwala, Pakpattan district. In another operation, an accused was arrested from Lahore for allegedly sharing a Multan-based woman’s pictures and videos through fake channels without her consent, damaging her reputation.

An Infinix Smart 8 mobile phone containing the victim’s pictures and videos was recovered from his possession.

In a separate case, a suspect was arrested near Faisalabad Toll Plaza for allegedly blackmailing a woman from Vehari through WhatsApp and threatening to share her private pictures on social media. An Oppo F19 mobile phone containing WhatsApp accounts allegedly used for blackmailing and related evidence was recovered from him.

Atif Ameer said the NCCIA has taken all three mobile phones into custody and initiated further investigation and legal proceedings against the suspects. He mentioned the agency was taking effective measures to protect women from online harassment and blackmailing, adding that strict legal action would be taken against those involved in such offences.

headline: Yotova to become Bulgaria’s first elected female president
description: SOFIA, Bulgaria - Exit polls in Bulgaria suggest that incumbent President Iliana Yotova is the apparent winner in the country’s presidential runoff.
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SOFIA, Bulgaria - Exit polls in Bulgaria suggest that incumbent President Iliana Yotova is the apparent winner in the country’s presidential runoff. Partial official results are expected later Sunday. Surveys by several polling organizations give Yotova about 52% of the vote. If confirmed by official results, she would become Bulgaria’s first elected female head of state. Former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, backed by reformist pro-Western opposition parties, is said to be trailing with around 44%. The vote was the first major test for Prime Minister Rumen Radev’s Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party, which has endorsed Yotova. In April’s parliamentary vote, the party won 131 of the 240 seats in Parliament, securing an outright majority. Observers say that a victory for Yotova will keep the presidency in the hands of the governing majority. Such a concentration of power could prevent the effective maintenance of checks and balances on policy decisions by institutions, they say. Yotova, 62, took over the presidency in January, when Radev stepped down to run for parliament, and was seeking her own elected mandate. She’s expected to continue Radev’s policy of keeping Bulgaria on its European path, while also supporting better relations with Russia and the lifting of sanctions.

After casting her vote on Sunday, Yotova said that she voted for a Bulgaria that makes its own decisions and maintains a strong voice on the international stage.

“I voted for national consensus through dialogue, for institutions that work for citizens, for a strong state with its own foreign policy in a strong Europe,” she told reporters.

The Balkan country joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. While there is a broad consensus among the parties in parliament on the country’s pro-Western path, widespread pro-Russia sentiments based on traditional historical and cultural ties with Russia have divided society, particularly since the start of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Both Yotova and Radev have called for a diplomatic solution to end the war in Ukraine but remain evasive about possible Russian involvement in drone attacks in the Black Sea region.

During a television debate between the two presidential contenders, Yotova advocated for a settlement involving both Ukraine and Russia, saying that “peace could come only through negotiations.” She also proposed a security meeting involving all six Black Sea countries to sign a moratorium on hostilities.

Bulgaria’s presidency is primarily ceremonial. Although the head of state has no executive powers, and all major policies must be approved by parliament, direct election gives the president greater political authority. The president leads the armed forces and can veto legislation, signs international treaties and appoints ambassadors.

Presidents in Bulgaria are elected directly for a five-year term and can serve no more than two terms.

SOFIA, Bulgaria - Exit polls in Bulgaria suggest that incumbent President Iliana Yotova is the apparent winner in the country’s presidential runoff. Partial official results are expected later Sunday. Surveys by several polling organizations give Yotova about 52% of the vote. If confirmed by official results, she would become Bulgaria’s first elected female head of state. Former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, backed by reformist pro-Western opposition parties, is said to be trailing with around 44%. The vote was the first major test for Prime Minister Rumen Radev’s Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party, which has endorsed Yotova. In April’s parliamentary vote, the party won 131 of the 240 seats in Parliament, securing an outright majority. Observers say that a victory for Yotova will keep the presidency in the hands of the governing majority. Such a concentration of power could prevent the effective maintenance of checks and balances on policy decisions by institutions, they say. Yotova, 62, took over the presidency in January, when Radev stepped down to run for parliament, and was seeking her own elected mandate. She’s expected to continue Radev’s policy of keeping Bulgaria on its European path, while also supporting better relations with Russia and the lifting of sanctions.

The Balkan country joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. While there is a broad consensus among the parties in parliament on the country’s pro-Western path, widespread pro-Russia sentiments based on traditional historical and cultural ties with Russia have divided society, particularly since the start of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Bulgaria’s presidency is primarily ceremonial. Although the head of state has no executive powers, and all major policies must be approved by parliament, direct election gives the president greater political authority. The president leads the armed forces and can veto legislation, signs international treaties and appoints ambassadors.

description: LAHORE - The working hours of subordinate courts across Punjab will be revised with effect from today (Monday), with the new schedule applicable to both
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - The working hours of subordinate courts across Punjab will be revised with effect from today (Monday), with the new schedule applicable to both Sessions and Civil courts. According to the revised schedule, hearings in Sessions and Civil courts will be held from 9:00am to 4:00pm from Monday to Thursday and on Saturdays. A break for prayers and lunch will be observed from 1:00pm to 1:30pm. However, on Fridays, the subordinate courts will continue to hear cases from 9:00am to 1:00pm under the revised judicial schedule.

headline: Punjab approves 149 new posts in 3 departments
description: LAHORE - The Punjab government has approved the creation of more than 149 new positions across three departments, paving the way for fresh recruitment in
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - The Punjab government has approved the creation of more than 149 new positions across three departments, paving the way for fresh recruitment in the Youth Affairs and Sports Department, Provincial Intelligence Fusion Centre (PIFC) and Special Branch.

According to details, approval has been granted for 70 new positions in the Project Management Unit (PMU) of the Youth Affairs and Sports Department and 79 positions in the Provincial Intelligence Fusion Centre. Recruitment will also be carried out in the intelligence cadre of the Special Branch. The recruitment drive is aimed at strengthening the province’s intelligence and security capabilities. The additional staff at the Provincial Intelligence Fusion Centre is expected to improve information sharing, threat identification and intelligence analysis. Meanwhile, new appointments in the Special Branch will enhance field monitoring and support efforts to maintain law and order and prevent crime. The 70 positions in the Youth Affairs and Sports Department’s PMU will help improve the monitoring and management of sports projects, as well as departmental administrative affairs.

headline: CM Maryam felicitates GB people on 79th Liberation Day
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday extended heartfelt felicitations to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on the 79th anniversary
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday extended heartfelt felicitations to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on the 79th anniversary of their liberation from Dogra rule and accession to Pakistan.

In her message, she described November 1, 1947, as a landmark day in the region’s history, paying tribute to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan for their courage, sacrifices and struggle for freedom. She said the day symbolised the bravery, determination and unwavering resolve of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan, adding that their sacrifices would always be remembered and honoured. Maryam Nawaz said Gilgit-Baltistan was an integral and valuable part of Pakistan and a symbol of national unity. She stressed that ensuring the region’s development, prosperity and public welfare was a shared national responsibility.

Describing Gilgit-Baltistan as one of Pakistan’s most beautiful regions, she said its courageous people were a source of national pride, while its rich cultural heritage and traditions continued to attract tourists from across the country and abroad. The chief minister also paid tribute to the freedom fighters, veterans and martyrs whose sacrifices had shaped the region’s history. She prayed that Allah Almighty would bless Gilgit-Baltistan and the entire country with lasting peace, progress and prosperity.

headline: Punjab sets target to train one million youth in skills over 3 years
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday set a target of imparting skills training to one million young people over the next three years,
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Sunday set a target of imparting skills training to one million young people over the next three years, approving a range of initiatives to expand technical and vocational education and improve employment opportunities across the province. The decisions were taken at a special meeting chaired by the chief minister, which reviewed ongoing skills development programmes and considered new projects aimed at equipping young people with market-oriented and internationally recognised skills.

The meeting approved the establishment of Punjab’s first modern Woodworking Centre of Excellence, along with centres of excellence for electrical work, vehicle technology and digital marketing. It also approved certification programmes for agriculture and heavy machinery operators. Maryam Nawaz also approved the launch of a CM Language Learning Programme, offering courses in 13 languages for the first time in Punjab. The province’s first Cleaning and Cleaner Academy will also be established to provide professional training in cleaning support, healthcare, hospitality and domestic services. The meeting was informed that 400,000 young people had so far completed skills training in Punjab, with more than 45 per cent securing employment, while a number of others had opted to continue their education. Under the Skills Development and Entrepreneurship Department, nearly 175,000 trained young people had secured jobs, including more than 38,000 who had found employment abroad. Sector-wise figures showed that 113,333 individuals had completed training in manufacturing, with more than 50,000 securing immediate employment. In the information technology sector, 111,607 young people had received training, of whom 49,588 were earning through employment.

Similarly, 23,269 people completed training in agriculture and livestock, with 10,033 securing jobs. In construction, 27,069 received training and 12,026 found employment, while 35,227 were trained in the energy sector, of whom 15,651 secured jobs. A total of 15,319 trainees completed courses in hospitality and tourism, with 6,807 securing immediate employment. The briefing further revealed that 90,029 trained individuals had found jobs in local industries, 53,509 had opted for self-employment and 38,557 had secured employment abroad. Another 39,325 had chosen to pursue further education.

Under the Empowering Women through Information Technology programme, 3,000 women from rural areas were earning from home after completing training. The department had also provided industry-related, management, teaching and skills-upgradation training to 15,065 teachers and staff members. The meeting was informed that 220 computer laboratories, 100 industrial stitching labs, 70 solar labs and 27 healthcare labs had been upgraded. Virtual reality welding and electric vehicle laboratories had also been established. Under the ‘Mahir’ programme, 25,000 young people will receive training in industrial clusters in Lahore, Faisalabad, Sialkot, Gujranwala and Multan.

The ‘Global Rozgar’ programme aims to train another 25,000 young people for the business process outsourcing (BPO) sector, while the Advance Tech programme will provide international certifications in emerging technologies to 7,500 individuals.

The Rs2.6 billion ‘Haryali’ programme will impart training to 20,000 young people in agriculture and green environment-related fields. The ‘Pahchaan’ and ‘Umeed’ programmes have so far provided training to 2,474 transgender people, while the ‘Umeed’ initiative aims to equip 10,000 persons with disabilities with employable skills.

Under another initiative, 69 Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (TEVTA) institutions will train 45,700 young people annually in line with the European Qualifications Framework. The meeting was also informed that a trainee electrician from a technical college in Punjab had secured fourth position at the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai.

headline: Punjab to launch polio eradication campaign from today
description: LAHORE - The Punjab Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) will launch a polio eradication campaign in 13 districts from Monday (today), November 2, to
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - The Punjab Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) will launch a polio eradication campaign in 13 districts from Monday (today), November 2, to vaccinate more than 9.3 million children under the age of five against the poliovirus. This will be the fifth polio vaccination campaign in Punjab this year and the third Sub-National Immunization Days (SNIDs) campaign, following two National Immunization Days (NIDs) and two earlier SNIDs rounds. These repeated vaccination drives are part of an intensive national strategy to interrupt poliovirus transmission and eradicate polio from Pakistan.

With 2027 widely viewed by public health experts as a potentially decisive year for Pakistan’s polio eradication efforts, extensive vaccination campaigns are also being planned for the coming year, continuing through June, to sustain immunity, close vaccination gaps and prevent the virus from spreading.

During the November campaign, more than 77,000 frontline workers will go door to door to administer polio vaccine drops to children, ensuring that every eligible child is protected against the crippling disease.

According to Punjab EOC Coordinator Khalid Parvaiz, the November campaign will continue for seven days in Lahore, while the remaining 12 districts will observe a four-day campaign. Lahore has set a target of vaccinating more than 2.285 million children, while 990,000 children will be reached in Rawalpindi. In Multan, the campaign aims to vaccinate more than one million children, while the target for Rahim Yar Khan stands at over 1.142 million. “Every campaign is an important opportunity to protect children against polio. Parents must ensure that all children under five receive polio drops during every campaign, even if they have been vaccinated in previous rounds,” said Khalid Parvaiz.

He emphasised that polio is an incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis, but timely vaccination can protect children against this preventable illness. He urged parents to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure their children are available when frontline workers visit their homes.

The EOC Coordinator said that follow-up activities would also be undertaken to reach children who may have been missed during the initial household visits. He stressed that no child in any of the targeted districts should be left without vaccination.

He also called upon local leaders, religious scholars and community influencers to play their role in raising awareness about the importance of polio vaccination and encouraging parents to ensure that their children receive the vaccine during the campaign. “Protecting every child requires collective responsibility. The cooperation of parents and communities, alongside the dedicated efforts of frontline workers, is essential to ensure that no child is left vulnerable to polio,” he added. The Punjab Emergency Operations Centre is mobilising all available resources and strengthening field-level coordination to ensure the successful implementation of the campaign and protect every child against the poliovirus.

headline: MQM-P demands new administrative units, announces Nov 29 procession
description: KARACHI - Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan Chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Sunday called for new administrative units across the country and announced
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan Chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Sunday called for new administrative units across the country and announced a procession towards Karachi’s Sharea Faisal on November 29 to press the demand.

Addressing a general workers’ meeting of the party’s District East chapter at PIB Ground in KMC Park, Siddiqui said Pakistan needed a political system that devolved power and resources to ordinary citizens. “There is no room left in Pakistan for feudal democracy,” he said, arguing that dynastic politics and the concentration of authority had deprived people of meaningful representation. Siddiqui said democracy could not serve its purpose if its benefits failed to reach ordinary Pakistanis. Workers, he argued, could not be adequately represented by wealthy industrialists, while the middle class needed representatives drawn from its own ranks.

The MQM-P chairman said a demand for a separate province, first raised by a student movement more than four decades ago, had gained support, particularly in Sindh’s urban areas. He pledged that his party would lead the campaign for new provinces and administrative units. Responding to questions about the proposed province’s territory, Siddiqui invoked the sacrifices of families who migrated to Pakistan at Partition, saying they had left their land and property in India for the new country. He urged supporters to prepare for the November 29 procession, saying the mobilisation would mark a new phase in the party’s campaign. He predicted that the turnout would fill roads leading to Sharea Faisal.

headline: Wafi Energy Pakistan announces Q3 2026 results
description: KARACHI - The board of directors of Wafi Energy Pakistan Limited (WEPL) has announced its financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. WEPL
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: KARACHI - The board of directors of Wafi Energy Pakistan Limited (WEPL) has announced its financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. WEPL reported a profit after tax of Rs 6,558 million for the first nine months of the year, compared with Rs 3,030 million in the same period last year. The results were announced amid continued volatility in global oil markets, supply-side pressures and a challenging operating environment. WEPL also announced a dividend of Rs 4 per share. During this period, WEPL continued to expand its retail network, adding 54 new Shell retail sites, 26 Shell Select stores and 9 Shell Recharge electric vehicle charging locations. WEPL continued to serve customers across its consumer and industrial lubricants businesses through product offerings and customer engagement. New alliances and partnerships further supported the growth of its retail business and customer offering. As part of its community initiatives, WEPL supported children’s education through its partnership with The Dawood Foundation’s MagnifiScience Centre. WEPL also secured first place in IFC–Pakistan Business Council’s Climate2Equal initiative for work carried out through WEPL’s Access to Energy programme, which supports women and rural communities. During period, Shell recognized Wafi Energy Pakistan Limited as Shell Licensee of Year 2025, among Shell licensees worldwide. The recognition reflects WEPL’s work across its business and its commitment to operational standards, safety and customer service.

headline: Handmade Carpet Exhibition delivered results beyond expectations: PCMEA
description: LAHORE - Chairman of the Pakistan Carpet Manufacturers and Exporters Association (PCMEA) Naeem Khokhar and Senior Vice Chairman Khawaja Mir Mudassar have
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - Chairman of the Pakistan Carpet Manufacturers and Exporters Association (PCMEA) Naeem Khokhar and Senior Vice Chairman Khawaja Mir Mudassar have expressed satisfaction over the successful conclusion of the three-day 42nd International Handmade Carpet Exhibition held recently in Lahore, saying that despite visa-related challenges, the exhibition achieved results beyond expectations. They said that the participation of a large number of foreign buyers was highly encouraging, while figures relating to export orders secured during the exhibition were currently being compiled. They also expressed gratitude to the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) for its valuable support and cooperation.

They expressed these views while addressing a review meeting held to assess the outcomes of the recently concluded three-day international exhibition in Lahore. The meeting was attended by Patron-in-Chief Abdul Latif Malik, Carpet Training Institute Chairman Ijaz-ur-Rehman, Senior Central Leader Riaz Ahmed, Usman Ashraf, Major (Retd.) Akhtar Nazir, Saeed Khan, Qamar Zia, Sheikh Aamir Khalid, Kamran Razi, Mrs. Sikanderin, Waseem Mukhtar Awan and other participants. The participants also paid tribute to all members of the organising team, led by Exhibition Chairman Riaz Ahmed, for making excellent arrangements and ensuring the successful conduct of the event.

Naeem Khokhar and Khawaja Mir Mudassar said that the successful organisation of the international exhibition under the prevailing circumstances was a welcome development for Pakistan’s handmade carpet industry and had significantly boosted the confidence of manufacturers and exporters. They added that the participation of serious international buyers had resulted in substantial export orders, the official figures for which would be compiled and shared in due course. They further said that several international events were scheduled to take place in the coming months, and the association would ensure active participation in these opportunities to strengthen Pakistan’s presence in global markets. They urged TDAP to extend maximum possible support in this regard so that the country’s exports could be enhanced and valuable foreign exchange earned.

The meeting also agreed on a proposal to send goodwill letters to foreign companies that participated in the exhibition. The initiative is aimed at strengthening business relations, maintaining regular communication with international buyers and developing long-term trade partnerships.

headline: Pakistan, Maldives reaffirm commitment to strengthen bilateral coop
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan and the Maldives yesterday reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations and advancing cooperation in diverse
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan and the Maldives yesterday reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations and advancing cooperation in diverse areas following a telephone conversation between Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Maldivian Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam. During the conversation, Foreign Minister Adam, who is currently in Antigua and Barbuda to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), expressed appreciation for the warm hospitality extended by Pakistan during the recent visit of Maldivian President Mohamed Muizzu and his delegation to Islamabad, the Foreign Office said.

Both foreign ministers underscored the importance of building on the understandings reached during the presidential visit and maintaining close engagement to translate the agreed areas of cooperation into tangible progress. They also exchanged views on the agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting and discussed matters relating to multilateral cooperation. The conversation reflected the two countries’ shared resolve to maintain close diplomatic engagement and further strengthen their longstanding bilateral ties, the FO said.

headline: North Korea tests cluster-bomb warheads: KCNA
description: Pyongyang - North Korea conducted a test of a cluster warhead for a tactical ballistic missile to assess its combat applicability and destructive power, state
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Pyongyang - North Korea conducted a test of a cluster warhead for a tactical ballistic missile to assess its combat applicability and destructive power, state media reported Sunday. The Missile Administration carried out the test Saturday, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

The test was overseen by Gen Kim Jong Sik, a member of the Central Military Commission of the ruling Workers’ Party of Korea and first deputy director of a department of the party’s Central Committee. North Korea’s Ballistic Missile Systems Research Institute and Warhead Research Institute said the test confirmed that the country’s “Type-2 standard cluster warhead” could devastate a target area of about 12 to 13 hectares (29 to 32 acres) at what they described as an “ultra-high density.” The head of the Missile Administration said North Korea classifies its cluster warheads into four categories, including special-purpose and standard types. He said Pyongyang plans to make all four types available to military units by the end of this year, allowing them to select warheads according to operational objectives and the characteristics of targets.

The Missile Administration described the test as part of regular scientific research aimed at increasing the destructive power of its weapons systems. Pyongyang has ramped up its show of force in recent weeks with multiple missile tests and holding a drone exhibition.

Analysts said the tests could be part of efforts to modernise the military. North Korea gained experience in modern warfare, sending troops to the war in Ukraine for its ally Moscow. North Korea test-fired around 10 ballistic missiles from its east coast towards the sea on Thursday, when German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited South Korea for a summit.

headline: Province advances NDC 3.0 plan and digital climate registry
description: KARACHI - The provincial government has prepared recommendations for the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0), while work is also underway on a
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - The provincial government has prepared recommendations for the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0), while work is also underway on a digital climate registry and dashboard to monitor carbon emissions and assess the performance of climate projects. Sindh Environment Secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili said this at a workshop held on Saturday to explore new investment opportunities to mitigate the effects of climate change and protect the environment ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Karachi Centre for Climate Change (K4C) and the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (Kati) jointly organised the workshop. Participants held detailed discussions on various environmental initiatives, including access to clean water, restoration of agricultural land and orchards, reduction of industrial pollution and carbon emissions, promotion of electric vehicles and transparency in carbon projects.

Opening the dialogue, K4C founding director Bilal Sohail stressed the need to translate Pakistan’s climate commitments into practical projects and investment opportunities.

He said effective measures in the water, energy and carbon sectors, along with private-sector participation, were essential for an industrial and coastal city like Karachi.

Lahore High Court Justice Jawad Hassan highlighted the importance of effective environmental legislation, protection of public interest and a clear regulatory framework to address climate change.

He said legal certainty was essential to encourage private-sector investment, adding that laws and policies must ensure environmental protection while providing investors with clear guidance and confidence.

Speaking on the occasion, Sindh Environment Secretary Uqaili outlined the provincial government’s initiatives to address climate change, protect the environment and strengthen policymaking, institutional reforms and practical interventions.

He said the government had approved 13 carbon-market projects and forwarded them to the federal ministry of climate change. These projects had the potential to reduce emissions equivalent to 330.13 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

The projects included wind power, emission reductions in the energy sector, production of biochar from agricultural waste, reduction of methane emissions and sustainable forestry initiatives.

He added that the Sindh government had also prepared six priority climate projects worth $62.15m. These included biogas projects in five districts, floating agriculture in lower Sindh, reduction of carbon emissions from brick kilns and capacity-building initiatives in climate finance.

Mr Uqaili said Sindh faced serious climate-related threats, including extreme heat, floods, water scarcity, rising sea levels and seawater intrusion into coastal areas. Addressing these challenges required joint efforts by the government, private sector and international development partners.

He said Sindh’s provincial recommendations for the NDC 3.0 had been prepared, while work was also underway on a digital climate registry and dashboard to monitor carbon emissions and assess the performance of climate projects.

He added that the provincial government believed in guiding and supporting industrial development alongside enforcing environmental laws. In this regard, memorandums of understanding had also been signed with various educational institutions to promote research and collaboration.

The COP31 will be held in Antalya, Turkiye, from Nov 9 to 20, 2026. Heads of state, government representatives, experts and officials from relevant institutions from across the world are expected to attend.

headline: KP seeks CCI nod for 500pc increase in FED on indigenous natural gas
description: ISLAMABAD - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has approached the Council of Common Interests (CCI) seeking a 500 percent increase in the federal excise duty (FED) on
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has approached the Council of Common Interests (CCI) seeking a 500 percent increase in the federal excise duty (FED) on indigenous natural gas, it has been learnt reliably. The KP government has sought CCI nod for increasing FED on natural gas from the existing Rs10 per MMBTU to Rs60 per MMBTU, official documents revealed.

“The federal duty of excise on natural gas was last fixed at Rs10 per MMBTU through Finance Act 2010 in accordance with the provision of Article 161(1)(a) of the Constitution. At that time the federal duty of excise was 2.6% of the industrial gas tariff which was Rs382 per MMBTU. As of today, the industrial gas tariff has jacked up to Rs2700 per MMBTU which translates that the federal duty of excise on natural gas shall be Rs60 per MMBTU at the same proportion as determined in 2010 i.e. 2.6%,” said a summary moved by the former PTI-led KP government to CCI.

According to the summary available with The Nation, the KP government said that under Article 161(1)(a) - “the net proceeds of the federal duty of excise on natural gas levied at well-head and collected by the federal government and of the royalty collected by the federal government, shall not form part of the Federal Consolidated Fund and shall be paid to the province in which the well-head of natural gas is situated;” Article 161(1)(a) of the Constitution stipulates levy and collection of federal duty of excise on natural gas, the receipts so collected shall be paid to the province in which the well-head of natural gas is situated.

According to the summary, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has limited avenues to mobilize its revenue resources. The province solely depends on its share in the federally collected receipts to discharge its constitutional role and responsibilities for the welfare of the people. Freezing of federal duty of excise on natural gas has been badly affecting provincial revenue resources. Since “Mineral Oil and Natural Gas”, falls at Entry 2, Part-II of Federal Legislative List, therefore, in light of Article 154 of the Constitution, the matter is within the exclusive jurisdiction of CCI to decide. “The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa therefore respectfully submits the matter for consideration of the CCI and requests for upward revision in the rate of federal duty of excise on natural gas from the existing rate of Rs.10 per MMBTU to Rs. 60 per MMBTU. Moreover, the specific rate of federal duty of excise on natural gas may be linked with the Cost Performance Index (CPI) in future annual budgets.”

headline: Chinese Communist Party’s minister Liu Haixing in Pakistan for talks
description: ISLAMABAD - Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC), Liu Haixing, arrived in Islamabad yesterday on his first official
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC), Liu Haixing, arrived in Islamabad yesterday on his first official visit to Pakistan, marking another significant development in the high-level political and party-to-party engagement between the two close allies. Liu is visiting Pakistan at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, the Foreign Office said. During his stay, the Chinese minister will call on Pakistan’s leadership and co-chair a high-level event with Ishaq Dar on November 2, the Foreign Office said on Sunday. The visit reflects the longstanding close ties between Pakistan and China and underscores their shared resolve to further strengthen the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership. It also forms part of the continuing high-level exchanges and institutional engagement between the ruling parties of the two countries, which have remained an important pillar of bilateral relations alongside government-to-government cooperation.

The Foreign Office said the visit would provide another opportunity to reinforce political understanding and deepen cooperation between Pakistan and China.

headline: NCCIA arrests man for harassing, blackmailing woman
description: KARACHI - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Saturday arrested a man for his alleged involvement in harassing and blackmailing a woman
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Saturday arrested a man for his alleged involvement in harassing and blackmailing a woman through objectionable videos, WhatsApp messages and threatening voice messages. A spokesperson said that the suspect was arrested in a raid conducted in the Badar Commercial area of the Defence Housing Authority. He said the suspect allegedly subjected the complainant to online harassment, intimidation, and blackmail through digital communication platforms. In this regard, a case had been registered against him under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). Earlier on Friday, the NCCIA arrested a man for allegedly depriving a woman of approximately Rs4.45 million by making empty promises of marriage on a matrimonial app. The agency said that the suspect had allegedly obtained the money through online bank transfers and subsequently threatened the woman to circulate her doctored photographs on social media to extort further money.

headline: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 8, including 4-year-old boy
description: Gaza City - Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Sunday, according
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: Gaza City - Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Sunday, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry. Medics said three people were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City. The interior ministry said the five police officers were killed in another strike in western Khan Younis, in the south of the enclave. The Israeli military said it struck several militants in Khan Younis, without giving further information. It did not immediately comment on the Gaza City strike. Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of a year-old ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal. Last year’s US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel to withdraw its troops, who control about two-thirds of the territory where they have ordered residents out. Nearly all of the more than 2 million residents live in the remaining third of the enclave among war ruins, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, still under effective control of Hamas. At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory’s health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel’s assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

headline: RLNG price hike to further burden industry: PIAF
description: LAHORE - Pakistan Industrial and Traders Associations Front (PIAF) has strongly criticised the increase of 13.89% to 15.27% in regasified liquefied natural gas
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan Industrial and Traders Associations Front (PIAF) has strongly criticised the increase of 13.89% to 15.27% in regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) prices for October 2026, warning that the latest revision will further increase industrial energy costs, raise production expenses and undermine the competitiveness of Pakistani products in international markets. PIAF Chairman Faheemur Rehman Saigol, Senior Vice Chairman Nasrullah Mughal and Vice Chairman Tahir Manzoor Chaudhary, in a joint statement, said the increase had come at a time when industries were already struggling with high electricity and gas tariffs, heavy taxation, expensive financing and rising operational costs. Repeated adjustments in energy prices were making it increasingly difficult for manufacturers to plan production, manage expenses and compete with regional rivals.

They said the latest OGRA notification, which raised RLNG prices for SNGPL and SSGCL transmission and distribution networks by up to 15.27%, had reversed the 20% reduction allowed in September, creating fresh uncertainty for businesses already facing considerable financial pressure. Faheemur Rehman Saigol said energy was among the most important components of industrial production costs, and any increase in gas prices directly affected manufacturing expenses, particularly in energy-intensive sectors. He warned that higher energy costs would eventually be passed on to consumers through increased prices of locally manufactured products, adding to inflationary pressures and weakening purchasing power.

He pointed out that the average delivered ex-ship price of LNG had increased to $10.75 per MMBtu in October from $10.06 in September, while the RLNG sale price for SNGPL’s distribution network had risen by 14.01% to $17.3259 per MMBtu. The increase in SSGCL’s distribution network price was even higher at 15.27%, taking the rate to $16.3959 per MMBtu. Saigol said the government needed to develop a balanced energy pricing mechanism that protected industrial consumers from sudden and excessive cost fluctuations. While acknowledging the impact of international energy prices on domestic fuel costs, he stressed that the entire burden should not be passed on to productive sectors without considering their ability to absorb additional expenses. He said Pakistan’s manufacturers were already facing intense competition from regional economies where relatively affordable energy, efficient infrastructure and business-friendly policies provided industries with a competitive advantage.

headline: Week long polio eradication campaign starts in Hyderabad
description: HYDERABAD - The National Polio Eradication Campaign will continue from November 2 to November 8 in Hyderabad with a target of immunizing around 490,000
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
HYDERABAD - The National Polio Eradication Campaign will continue from November 2 to November 8 in Hyderabad with a target of immunizing around 490,000 children of under 5 years age in the district. In this connection, the campaign was inaugurated at the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) on Sunday by Deputy Commissioner Hyderabad Zain-ul-Abideen, Memon. District Health Officer Hyderabad Dr Pir Ghulam Hussain and Additional Deputy Commissioner-II, Mehwish Ejaz, administered polio drops to children on the occasion. Addressing the event the DHO apprised that all necessary arrangements for the campaign had been completed. He stated that approximately 490,000 children would be administered polio drops during the campaign. The DHO appealed to the public to cooperate with polio vaccination teams to protect children from that crippling disease. The inauguration ceremony was attended by the NSTOP Officer Hyderabad, District Polio Officers (DPOs) of the World Health Organization (WHO), Chief Communication Officer (CCO), DFP SIA representatives, TMC focal persons and Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs). The participants reaffirmed their commitment to joint efforts for the eradication of polio and pledged to make the November 2026 campaign successful.The cooperation of parents, religious scholars, social leaders, and all segments of society was also essential for the complete eradication of polio, they said.

They urged the parents to ensure that their children received polio drops during every single campaign so that Pakistan could be made polio-free.

headline: Pakistan set to host 23rd Asian Team Squash C’ships in Islamabad
description: LAHORE - Pakistan is set to host the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championships 2026 at the Mushaf Squash Complex from November 3 to 7, with six nations competing
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan is set to host the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championships 2026 at the Mushaf Squash Complex from November 3 to 7, with six nations competing for continental honours. A total of 44 players from Pakistan, Hong Kong China, Malaysia, Korea, Iran and Uzbekistan will participate in the five-day championship.

Pakistan’s men’s team, seeded No. 1 in Pool A, comprises Noor Zaman, M Ashab Irfan, M Asim Khan and Nasir Iqbal, with Tahir Iqbal as coach. The women’s team, seeded fourth, features Sana Bahadar, Mehwish Ali, Mahnoor Ali and Sehrish Ali, coached by Sadia Gul. Group Captain (retd) Irfan Asghar will oversee the team management.

headline: Lahore Blues and Whites reach National U19 C’ship semis
description: LAHORE - Lahore Region Blues and Whites qualified for the semifinals of the National U-19 Three-Day Championship after quarterfinal performances. Lahore
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Lahore Region Blues and Whites qualified for the semifinals of the National U-19 Three-Day Championship after quarterfinal performances. Lahore Whites defeated Faisalabad Region by six wickets, chasing a target of 219. Ahmed Khawaja led the pursuit with an unbeaten 98, while Ali Khokhar scored 49. Earlier, Naveed Ayub made an unbeaten 64. Lahore Blues advanced on the basis of a 45-run first-innings lead against Peshawar Blues. They posted 262 and dismissed Peshawar for 217. Ibtisam Azhar starred with seven match wickets and an unbeaten century, earning player-of-the-match honours. LRCA president Khawaja Nadeem Ahmed congratulated both teams.

headline: Thousands protest in India’s capital against voter roll revision
description: New Delhi - Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India’s capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country’s election
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: New Delhi - Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India’s capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country’s election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party. The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world’s largest democracy over the last month. The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the accusations. On Sunday, protesters led by opposition Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi chanted “vote thief, leave your seat” and beat drums while marching from central parts of New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan, a large outdoor venue. “I have been a voter since I was 18 and now I find myself struck off the list,” protester Nandita, 46, told news wire, giving only one name. “It’s important to be here because of the way things are going. The cost of living is going up… The only option is to take to the streets peacefully.” The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the campaign against the voter-roll revision. The overhaul of India’s voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings. Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims. Members of Hindu-nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls. Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll. Human Rights Watch has said the removal of voters was “arbitrary and deeply flawed”. “The authorities should immediately scrap the voter roll revision process that has denied India’s most marginalised people their right to vote and other government services,” it said in a statement this week. The Cockroach movement has been heavily involved in the pushback to the voter-roll revision and several of its leaders were temporarily detained by police during protests last month. The CJP has gained millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May. Earlier protests organised by the CJP in July over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi’s administration.

headline: DC Hyderabad for intensifying action against artificial price hikes, profiteering
description: HYDERABAD - Deputy Commissioner Hyderabad Zain ul Aabdeen Memon has issued strict directives to take action against artificial price hikes, profiteering
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
HYDERABAD - Deputy Commissioner Hyderabad Zain ul Aabdeen Memon has issued strict directives to take action against artificial price hikes, profiteering across district. According to a handout issued on Sunday in this regard monitoring will be maintained over the prices and availability of LPG, milk, flour, wheat, and other food items.

Severe legal action—including the imposition of heavy fines and arrests—will be taken against those who charge arbitrary prices by creating artificial shortages (or using the pretext of a shortage) and those who sell goods at prices illegally exceeding the government-fixed rates.

All Assistant Commissioners, Mukhtiarkars, and relevant officials have been instructed to remain active in the field starting tomorrow and to ensure that action is taken against violators without any discrimination

headline: Shehbaz FC, Lahore City FC win 12th Fame Sports Floodlight openers
description: LAHORE - The 12th Fame Sports Floodlight Football Tournament opened in thrilling fashion at Fame Football Club Ground, Model Town, with Shehbaz FC and Lahore
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The 12th Fame Sports Floodlight Football Tournament opened in thrilling fashion at Fame Football Club Ground, Model Town, with Shehbaz FC and Lahore City FC recording victories in two exciting opening-day encounters. The tournament was formally inaugurated by Zia Arif Dogar, President of District Football Association Lahore and Fame Sports Football Club. Shehbaz FC began their campaign with a convincing 3-1 victory over Cantt United, while Lahore City FC edged Shahdara United 8-7 in a penalty shootout after the teams finished regulation time at 1-1. Dogar said the competition had become one of Pakistan’s leading club-level football events. He revealed that more than 60 registered Lahore clubs were taking part in the two-and-a-half-month tournament, which provides local players with a valuable platform to showcase their talent and gain competitive experience.

headline: Sukkur Commissioner pledges improved sports facilities for Sindh Games
description: LAHORE - Sukkur Commissioner Abid Saleem Qureshi has announced that the renovation of the Sukkur basketball court will be completed before the Sindh
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Sukkur Commissioner Abid Saleem Qureshi has announced that the renovation of the Sukkur basketball court will be completed before the Sindh Games, promising improved facilities for athletes across the city. He made the announcement during a meeting with a delegation led by Sindh Basketball Association (SBBA) patron Ghulam Muhammad Khan. Qureshi also announced an Ali Naqvi Memorial Hockey Match between Commissioner Sukkur and Commissioner Karachi teams in November. Meanwhile, Lok Sahita Trust has sponsored kits for Sukkur’s girls’ basketball team. The trust’s Sports Chief Agha Haroon Khan presented tracksuits to the commissioner and team kits alongside Berger Paints Manager Abdul Samad Sheikh.

headline: Governor felicitates people of GB on 79th Independence Day
description: KARACHI - Governor of Sindh Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi has extended heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on their 79th Independence
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Governor of Sindh Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi has extended heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on their 79th Independence Day. According to a Governor House communique on Sunday, he said that the people of Gilgit-Baltistan won freedom through a historic struggle against Dogra rule and subsequently acceded to Pakistan. The Governor said that former Prime Minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif laid the foundation for the region’s development through landmark projects including the expansion of Karakoram Highway, Gilgit-Skardu Road and CPEC.

Hashmi said that several development projects in energy, education and employment are underway in Gilgit-Baltistan under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif.

The 16-megawatt Naltar hydropower project, 100-megawatt solar energy project and four Daanish Schools are important initiatives for the development of Gilgit-Baltistan.

The sacrifices, patriotism and unwavering commitment of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan to Pakistan are a source of pride for the nation, he said, adding that the development, prosperity and welfare of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan are a national responsibility.
