headline: Pakistan Police edge Guangdong 7-6 in thrilling hockey friendly
description: LAHORE - Pakistan Police hockey team edged China’s Guangdong provincial side 7-6 in an exciting friendly match at the Manzoor-ul-Hassan Hockey Stadium,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan Police hockey team edged China’s Guangdong provincial side 7-6 in an exciting friendly match at the Manzoor-ul-Hassan Hockey Stadium, Lahore, under the auspices of the Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF). Punjab Inspector General of Police and Pakistan Police Sports Board President Abdul Karim attended as chief guest, while DIG Athar Ismail, Chief Sports Officer of Pakistan Police, was also present. Abdul Karim congratulated the Pakistan Police players, coach and officials on their hard-fought victory and appreciated both teams for their spirited performance. Several hockey legends, including Olympians Manzoor-ul-Hassan, Shahbaz Ahmed Senior, Tahir Zaman and Khawaja Junaid, attended the match alongside Chinese Consulate officials and a large number of spectators. At the conclusion, Athar Ismail distributed medals among players and presented shields to team officials and hockey legends. The Punjab Police musical band added to the occasion with its performances.

headline: Consumers getting Rs14.71 relief as govt orders refineries to surrender extra war-time premium on petrol
description: ISLAMABAD - Petrol consumers in Pakistan have started receiving a relief of Rs14.71 per litre after the federal government directed refineries to surrender the
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Petrol consumers in Pakistan have started receiving a relief of Rs14.71 per litre after the federal government directed refineries to surrender the extra war-time premium, which was being charged on imported petrol but was also being applied to locally produced fuel.

Despite strong resistance from refineries, the Federal Cabinet approved a revised pricing mechanism for motor spirit (MS) during the Iran-US war, directing all refineries to surrender the difference between the import price of petrol — inclusive of the extra war-time premium — and the ex-refinery price under petroleum levy head.

A letter written by OGRA to the Petroleum Division said, “Refineries shall surrender Rs. 49.02 per litre in PL Account, representing the differential between the notified import price/ex-refinery price (calculated on the basis of the prevailing PSO cargo premium, customs duty and incidentals) and the corresponding entitled ex-refinery price determined on the basis of the premium, customs duty and incidentals prevailing as of March 7, 2026. The amount so surrendered shall translate into a contribution equivalent to Rs. 14.71 per litre towards the overall Petroleum Levy (PL) of Rs. 80 per litre, calculated on the countrywide volume.” It is worth noting that while common people reel under high fuel prices, the US-Iran war has become a goldmine for Pakistan’s refineries and E&P companies. In reports filed with the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), the country’s oil refineries have reported a whopping 1,860% surge in profit to Rs57 billion during the first quarter (July–September) of FY2026-27, compared to Rs2.9 billion in the same period last fiscal year.

Till October 30, OGRA was calculating petrol prices on import parity basis and was allowing local refineries to apply PSO premium to locally produced petrol, which means even if petrol is produced in Rawalpindi or Karachi from crude, it is priced as if a ship brought it from Gulf or any anywhere else.

However, when Iran-US war pushed PSO Premium to 25.52 USD/BBL, as of October 30, local refineries automatically got that high price too without any extra cost, creating a windfall. However, the price mechanism was changed from October 31, and the government capped the premium at March 7 (pre-war) level and took the difference as PL. The surrendered amount will be used to provide relief to petrol consumers. According to a letter issued by Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division) to all the six local refineries, i.e. Pak-Arab Refinery Limited, , Pakistan Refinery Limited, Attock Refinery Limited, ,National Refinery Limited, Cnergyico Refinery Limited, and ENAR, it was informed that the Federal Cabinet has approved a revised pricing mechanism for motor spirit (MS) during the Iran-US war period to insulate consumers from volatile premiums and route delays. The new mechanism will remain in place for the next 30 days.

In order to implement the decision, all refineries have been advised to deposit the differential petroleum levy as specified in the OGRA price notification and PL notification issued from time to time into the head of account C03901. The refineries shall also furnish the reporting of domestic sales of MS along with CPRs/challans to Petroleum Division and OGRA on daily basis for necessary verification and reconciliation, the letter said. On October 30, while announcing the daily price mechanism, the government kept the petroleum levy (PL) on petrol at Rs80 per litre, however, after applying Rs14.71 per liter to be surrendered to the PL account, the government charged Rs65.29 per liter levy from OMCs.

A letter written by OGRA to the Petroleum Division said, “Refineries shall surrender Rs. 49.02 per litre in PL Account, representing the differential between the notified import price/ex-refinery price (calculated on the basis of the prevailing PSO cargo premium, customs duty and incidentals) and the corresponding entitled ex-refinery price determined on the basis of the premium, customs duty and incidentals prevailing as of March 7, 2026. The amount so surrendered shall translate into a contribution equivalent to Rs. 14.71 per litre towards the overall Petroleum Levy (PL) of Rs. 80 per litre, calculated on the countrywide volume.” It is worth noting that while common people reel under high fuel prices, the US-Iran war has become a goldmine for Pakistan’s refineries and E&P companies. In reports filed with the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), the country’s oil refineries have reported a whopping 1,860% surge in profit to Rs57 billion during the first quarter (July–September) of FY2026-27, compared to Rs2.9 billion in the same period last fiscal year.

Till October 30, OGRA was calculating petrol prices on import parity basis and was allowing local refineries to apply PSO premium to locally produced petrol, which means even if petrol is produced in Rawalpindi or Karachi from crude, it is priced as if a ship brought it from Gulf or any anywhere else.

However, when Iran-US war pushed PSO Premium to 25.52 USD/BBL, as of October 30, local refineries automatically got that high price too without any extra cost, creating a windfall. However, the price mechanism was changed from October 31, and the government capped the premium at March 7 (pre-war) level and took the difference as PL. The surrendered amount will be used to provide relief to petrol consumers. According to a letter issued by Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division) to all the six local refineries, i.e. Pak-Arab Refinery Limited, , Pakistan Refinery Limited, Attock Refinery Limited, ,National Refinery Limited, Cnergyico Refinery Limited, and ENAR, it was informed that the Federal Cabinet has approved a revised pricing mechanism for motor spirit (MS) during the Iran-US war period to insulate consumers from volatile premiums and route delays. The new mechanism will remain in place for the next 30 days.

In order to implement the decision, all refineries have been advised to deposit the differential petroleum levy as specified in the OGRA price notification and PL notification issued from time to time into the head of account C03901. The refineries shall also furnish the reporting of domestic sales of MS along with CPRs/challans to Petroleum Division and OGRA on daily basis for necessary verification and reconciliation, the letter said. On October 30, while announcing the daily price mechanism, the government kept the petroleum levy (PL) on petrol at Rs80 per litre, however, after applying Rs14.71 per liter to be surrendered to the PL account, the government charged Rs65.29 per liter levy from OMCs.

headline: Sindh tourism resorts face Rs22.3m loss despite strong tourist footfall
description: KARACHI - Despite Sindh’s rich cultural heritage and numerous tourist attractions, several resorts and hotels operated by the Sindh Tourism Development
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Despite Sindh’s rich cultural heritage and numerous tourist attractions, several resorts and hotels operated by the Sindh Tourism Development Corporation (STDC) are reportedly running at a loss, raising questions about whether these facilities are generating revenue for the provincial government or placing an additional burden on the public exchequer. According to the Auditor General of Pakistan’s audit report for 2024-25, seven hotels and resorts managed by the STDC incurred total expenses of Rs42.1 million during the year, while their combined revenue stood at just Rs19.7 million. The resulting loss to the Sindh government amounted to Rs22.3 million. The highest loss was recorded at the resorts located near Keenjhar Lake in Thatta district. According to the report, the facilities generated Rs9.073 million in revenue against expenses of Rs22 million, leaving a substantial gap between earnings and operating costs.

The disparity is particularly striking given the popularity of Keenjhar Lake as a recreational destination. An estimated 10,000 to 12,000 people visit the lake every week, the majority of them from Karachi. Despite this steady flow of visitors, the resorts have reportedly struggled to generate sufficient revenue to cover their expenses. The audit report also identified losses at several other facilities managed by the corporation, including Rooplo Kolhi Resort, Marvi Rest House, Haleji Lake Resort, Baqar Lake Resort, Ranikot Resort and Lal Shahbaz Resort in Sehwan. Other properties operated by the STDC include Sambar Inn Hotel in Larkana and a motel in Garhi Khuda Bakhsh. However, details of their annual expenses and revenues were not available in the report cited.

The findings have raised questions about the commercial performance of tourism facilities that are intended to serve visitors while also generating income for the provincial government. Although these properties operate on commercial lines, the audit figures suggest that their earnings have not been sufficient to meet operating costs.

However, the STDC has disputed the claim that its resorts and hotels are still operating at a loss. Speaking to media STDC Managing Director Syed Fayyaz Shah said the facilities had previously faced financial difficulties, but the situation had changed after the introduction of a computerised management system. He said room bookings were now handled online, helping increase the corporation’s revenue. Shah did not, however, provide figures to substantiate the claim that the facilities were no longer running at a loss, leaving the corporation’s current financial position unclear. Sindh has considerable potential for tourism, with a wide range of historical, cultural and recreational destinations spread across the province. The performance of publicly managed resorts is therefore significant not only for the provincial exchequer but also for efforts to develop tourism and create employment.

The STDC was established in August 1991 and operates under the provincial tourism department. Following the 18th Constitutional Amendment in 2010, the management of several historical, cultural and tourist sites was transferred from the federal government to the provinces. The transfer also included properties associated with these sites, placing them under the Sindh government’s administration.

The corporation’s website states that it has around 100 registered tour operators working with it to promote tourism across the province. Yet the audit findings highlight a persistent question: why are publicly managed tourism facilities failing to generate enough revenue to cover their costs, despite the province’s tourism potential and the popularity of destinations such as Keenjhar Lake?

The absence of updated financial figures from the corporation makes it difficult to determine whether online booking and other administrative changes have improved profitability or whether the facilities continue to depend on public funds to meet their operating expenses.

headline: Osairm springs surprise to secure Governor’s Cup Golf title
description: LAHORE - Osairm Nasir emerged as the champion of the 43rd Millat Tractors Governor’s Cup Golf Tournament, overturning the overnight standings and leaving
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Osairm Nasir emerged as the champion of the 43rd Millat Tractors Governor’s Cup Golf Tournament, overturning the overnight standings and leaving his rivals trailing in a memorable finish. Displaying impressive golfing skills, composure and determination, Osairm rose to the occasion when it mattered most, delivering a decisive net score of 67 in the final round to finish with an aggregate net score of 209 and secure the coveted championship trophy. The triumph was particularly special for the young golfer, who comes from a golfing family and carried forward his passion for the sport with an impressive display of talent and consistency. In the net category, Dr Hamza Asif secured the runner-up position with an aggregate score of 211, while Omer Farooq finished third with 215. The final results brought a dramatic shift in the leaderboard, as the overnight leaders were unable to maintain their advantage, paving the way for Osairm’s remarkable ascent to the top. In the gross category, Qasim Ali Khan emerged as the leading performer and claimed the title with an aggregate score of 216. Mohammed Shoaib secured second place with 219, while Zayd Omer finished third. The closing ceremony was attended by distinguished guests, including chief guest Sikandar Mustafa Khan and Salman Siddique, Chairman of Lahore Gymkhana.

headline: Gilgit-Baltistan vital part of Pakistan, beautiful symbol of national unity: CM Murad
description: KARACHI - Chief Minister (CM) of Sindh Syed Murad Ali Shah has congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on Independence Day. He said that November 1,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Chief Minister (CM) of Sindh Syed Murad Ali Shah has congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on Independence Day. He said that November 1, 1947, is a significant and memorable day in the history of Gilgit-Baltistan. The sacrifices, courage and determination of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan are a proud chapter in our national history.

Syed Murad Ali Shah said that the people of Gilgit-Baltistan made history through their remarkable struggle and sacrifices for freedom.

Gilgit-Baltistan is an important part of Pakistan and a beautiful symbol of our national unity and solidarity, he said, adding that the culture, traditions and natural beauty of Gilgit-Baltistan are a valuable asset of Pakistan’s national identity. Chief Minister Sindh said that the role of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan’s development, stability and prosperity is commendable. He prayed that Gilgit-Baltistan continues to progress on the path to peace, development, prosperity and stability.

headline: 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis begins
description: LAHORE - The 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 officially got underway on Sunday at the Sports Board Punjab Tennis Academy,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 officially got underway on Sunday at the Sports Board Punjab Tennis Academy, Nishtar Park, Lahore. The national-level championship is being organised by Punjab Lawn Tennis Association. The championship holds special significance as it commemorates the services and contributions of the late Sheheryar Malik towards the promotion and development of tennis in Pakistan. The formal opening ceremony of the championship will be held on November 3 at 3:00 PM at the Sports Board Punjab Tennis Academy, Nishtar Park, Lahore. Dr. Asif Tufail, Secretary Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Punjab, and Mr. Fazal-ur-Rehman, Member Planning and Development Board, Punjab, will grace the occasion as chief guests. Meanwhile in the men’s singles first qualifying round, Asad Ullah, Abdullah Zeeshan, Rayn Noor Malik, Aliyan Ali, M Junaid, Aalay Husnain, Khurram Imtiaz, M Mohsin Hassan, Omer Babar and Ahmad Raza were victorious. In the men’s singles second qualifying round, the winners were Asad Ullah, Ibrahim Ahmad, M Waleed, M Junaid, Haider Ahmad, Khurram Imtiaz, Shamoon Jutt, Omer Babar, Shawal Azeem, Ismail Ahmad, Mubeen Akram and Kamran Khan. In the men’s singles third round, Omer Babar beat Shahmoon Jutt 6-0, Ahmad Raza beat Ismail Ahmad 6-0, Kamran Khan beat Mubeen Akram 6-3, Asad Ullah beat Ibrahim Ahmad 6-0, M Waleed beat Aliyan Ali 6-3, Khurram Imtiaz beat Abubakar 6-3.

headline: ECP launches pilot project for women’s voter registration in Qambar-Shahdadkot
description: KARACHI - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has launched a special pilot project for women’s voter registration in District
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has launched a special pilot project for women’s voter registration in District Qambar-Shahdadkot. Director General Gender and Training Nighat Siddique formally inaugurated the pilot project, ECP Sindh communique said on Sunday. Under the pilot project, 49,156 women in District Qambar Shahdadkot will be facilitated in obtaining Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs) and completing voter registration. The primary objective of the pilot project is to increase women’s voter registration and reduce the gender gap.

Joint Provincial Election Commissioner Sindh Tahir Mansoor Khan also attended the inauguration ceremony.

Regional Election Commissioner Larkana Abdul Waheed Baloch and the Deputy Commissioner Qambar-Shahdadkot were also present at the ceremony. District Election Commissioner Qambar Shahdadkot, Inayatullah Jamali, and Assistant Election Commissioner Kashif Inayat Soomro also attended the event. Priority will be given to women’s voter registration in statistical blocks with a higher gender gap. During November, Election Commission representatives will conduct door-to-door visits to identify eligible women and complete their voter registration.

A door-to-door survey will be conducted across the district to identify eligible women. NADRA’s mobile registration vans will provide women with the facility to obtain CNICs at their doorsteps. Women will also be able to obtain CNICs and register as voters at registration centres established in government buildings. “A total of 49,156 women in District Qambar Shahdadkot will be facilitated in obtaining CNICs and completing voter registration,” Nighat Siddique said.

“Increasing women’s voter registration and eliminating the gender gap are the primary objectives of the pilot project,” she said adding that im light of the results of this pilot project, similar initiatives will also be undertaken in other districts to improve women’s voter registration.

headline: Pakistan team to face world’s best at MMA World C’ships
description: LAHORE - More than 1,000 elite MMA fighters from over 70 countries are gathering in Tbilisi, Georgia, for the prestigious IMMAF World Championships, taking
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - More than 1,000 elite MMA fighters from over 70 countries are gathering in Tbilisi, Georgia, for the prestigious IMMAF World Championships, taking place from November 1 to 7. One of the largest international competitions in mixed martial arts, the championship brings together the world’s top emerging fighters in a major showdown for world titles and international recognition. Pakistan has sent a formidable seven-member national contingent, representing the country’s diverse sporting talent from Karachi, Lahore, Rawalakot, Poonch and Hunza in Gilgit-Baltistan. The squad includes Shayan Mehdi (Karachi – Strawweight 52.2kg), Shams Ur Rehman (Karachi – Bantamweight 61.2kg), Syed M Qaim Abass (Lahore – Super Lightweight 74.8kg), Saria Khan (Rawalakot/Poonch – Atomweight 47.6kg), Maliha Ali (Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan Featherweight 65.8kg), Manisha Ali (Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan – Lightweight 70.3kg) and Hamood Ali Wajid (Lahore – Junior Super Lightweight 74.8kg). The geographically diverse team reflects the rapid growth of MMA across Pakistan and the emergence of exceptional talent from every corner of the country. The IMMAF World Championships represent far more than an opportunity to win medals. They provide a recognised pathway towards the world’s leading professional MMA organisations, including the UFC and BRAVE Combat Federation. Numerous internationally recognised fighters have progressed through the IMMAF system before establishing successful professional careers, demonstrating how this platform can transform young athletes into global sporting stars. For Pakistan, the opportunity is significant: developing a generation of fighters capable of winning world titles, securing international contracts and representing the country on the biggest sporting platforms.

The Pakistan MMA Federation has established a clear, merit-based athlete development pathway, beginning with the Pakistan Open Championships, progressing through national trials and elite selection, and culminating in Asian and World Championships. The ultimate objective is to connect international sporting success with professional careers, creating a sustainable system that identifies talent, develops champions and produces global sporting icons.

This structured approach offers a potential blueprint for other sporting federations in Pakistan, demonstrating how transparent selection, competitive opportunities and long-term athlete development can deliver measurable results and lasting social impact.

Pakistan MMA Federation President Omar Ahmed described the squad as the strongest contingent Pakistan has ever assembled for the World Championships. “This is the best contingent we have ever sent to the World Championships. We have tremendous confidence in our athletes and expect them to challenge for medals against the world’s finest. Pakistan is no longer simply participating. We are competing amongst the best.”

Ahmed also highlighted the importance of private-sector support in making international participation possible. “I am deeply grateful to all our sponsors and supporters, who have stepped forward to back these young athletes. Their support is not simply funding a sporting event. It is investing in Pakistan’s future champions, the superstars of tomorrow and a generation that can inspire millions of young Pakistanis.”

He added: “Sport has the power to transform lives, create opportunities and deliver enormous social impact. These young fighters can become role models for an entire generation. Our sponsors are helping make that future possible, and their contribution deserves genuine recognition and appreciation.”

headline: DP/Imperial clinch 14th Maj Gen Saeed Uz Zaman Janjua Memorial Polo Cup trophy
description: LAHORE - Diamond Paints/Imperial defeated FG/Din/Sheikhoo 10–8 to lift the 14th Maj Gen Saeed Uz Zaman Janjua Memorial Polo Cup 2026 trophy at Fortress
author: The Nation
article_text: LAHORE - Diamond Paints/Imperial defeated FG/Din/Sheikhoo 10–8 to lift the 14th Maj Gen Saeed Uz Zaman Janjua Memorial Polo Cup 2026 trophy at Fortress Stadium on Sunday. The tournament, organised under the auspices of Lahore Garrison Polo Grounds and sponsored by JS Bank, concluded with an exciting final that kept spectators on the edge of their seats. Diamond Paints/Imperial demonstrated impressive coordination and attacking prowess throughout the encounter. Leading the charge was Raja Jalal Arslan, who smashes superb six goals while Bilal Haye and Ibrahim Naveed Sheikh thrashed in two goals apiece. For FG/Din/Sheikhoo, Hamza Mawaz Khan led their scoring effort with five goals, combining skilful field play with successful penalty conversions, while Abbas Mukhtar added three goals. Despite their determined comeback efforts, the runners-up finished the contest at 8–10. The prestigious occasion was attended by several distinguished personalities, including Dr Rashid Latif, Chairman of Rashid Latif University; Brig Mukhtiar; Brig Badar Uz Zaman, son of late Maj Gen Saeed Uz Zaman Janjua; and Maj Babar Mahboob Awan, Secretary of Lahore Garrison Polo Grounds. Prominent polo players and a large number of spectators also attended the final. Speaking after the triumph, Diamond Paints/Imperial captain Mir Shoaib Ahmad expressed satisfaction with his team’s performance, acknowledging the players’ dedication, teamwork and consistent efforts throughout the tournament. He particularly praised Raja Jalal Arslan and Bilal Haye for their exceptional contributions that led the team to title triumph. The concluding ceremony brought the tournament to a memorable close, with Club Secretary Maj Babar Mahboob Awan extending a special vote of thanks to Brig Badar Uz Zaman and his family for honouring the occasion with their presence and for their continued support of polo.

headline: KU offers free oral health screening for staff
description: KARACHI - The University of Karachi has launched what it described as a major staff welfare initiative to address the growing health risks associated with the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - The University of Karachi has launched what it described as a major staff welfare initiative to address the growing health risks associated with the use of gutka, paan and chhalia among its non-teaching employees. According to a press release, an estimated 70 per cent of the 1,575 non-teaching staff members are reported to use one or more of these hazardous substances, exposing themselves to serious oral health complications and an increased risk of oral cancer. On the directives of Vice Chancellor Dr Wasim Qazi, the KU has initiated awareness and free dental screening and treatment for affected employees through the recently rehabilitated Dental Outpatient Department of Karachi Metropolitan University.

It said that the VC believed that institutional responsibility extended beyond administrative oversight and disciplinary measures to include the health, dignity and well-being of employees.

Rather than initially resorting to disciplinary action against employees for these habits, the VC has prioritised awareness, counselling, early detection and access to treatment. “The objective is to encourage behavioural change through education, compassion and institutional support,” the statement added.

headline: Abbas Afridi’s fireworks power Pakistan to Hong Kong Sixes Plate title
description: MONG KOK - Pakistan ended their Hong Kong Sixes 2026 campaign on a winning note, defeating Oman by 18 runs in the Plate final to claim the second-tier title at
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MONG KOK - Pakistan ended their Hong Kong Sixes 2026 campaign on a winning note, defeating Oman by 18 runs in the Plate final to claim the second-tier title at Mission Road Ground on Sunday. Led by an explosive batting display from captain Abbas Afridi, Pakistan posted a formidable 154-4 in their allotted six overs. Afridi smashed 73 off just 16 deliveries, hitting 11 sixes and a four, to headline the innings. Abdul Samad provided further impetus with 26 off five balls, while Ahmed Daniyal contributed 25 from five deliveries, including four sixes. M Shahzad added 13 off four balls as Pakistan finished with a commanding total. Oman responded aggressively but could manage 136-4 in six overs. Openers Usman Ali and Zohaib Amanat kept their side in contention with spectacular half-centuries. Usman hammered 67 off 17 balls, including eight sixes, while Amanat struck 61 from 18 deliveries, also clearing the boundary eight times. Despite their impressive partnership, Oman’s batting effort fell short of Pakistan’s imposing target, handing the Green Shirts an 18-run victory. The Plate triumph helped Pakistan finish fifth overall after missing out on the main championship, which they had won previously. Their campaign began with a defeat against the UAE, but they bounced back with an emphatic victory over arch-rivals India. However, the UAE’s subsequent win over India secured its place in the main trophy competition, leaving Pakistan in the Plate category. Pakistan then overwhelmed hosts Hong Kong in the Plate semifinal, chasing 107 without losing a wicket, with Afridi smashing an unbeaten 55 off 13 balls. headline: Sindhi Adabi Sangat reviews multiple genres of literature
description: HYDERABAD - The meeting of Sindhi Adabi Sangat Hyderabad was held at Khana Badosh Writers Cafe, under the chairmanship of Professor Madad Ali Jhitial. Moula
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: HYDERABAD - The meeting of Sindhi Adabi Sangat Hyderabad was held at Khana Badosh Writers Cafe, under the chairmanship of Professor Madad Ali Jhitial. Moula Bakhsh Mohabati presented ‘Wai’, Mukesh Barthani read essay ‘My Mother’, Noor Hussain Kalhoro read Auto Biography, Imran Soomro ‘Yaadgiriyon’ and Madad Jhitial presnted ‘Kalam’ for review. Commenting on Mukesh’s article, it was said that this novel can be a piece. Talking about a character in Noor Hussain’s autobiography, it was said that in the past, the role of Bodhiri is going to be big. The ritual of giving chicken is important in this festival. The memoirs are not complete, read Madh Jhatial column without criticism. Prof. Dr. Qazi Khadim, Syed Zowar Naqvi, Nazeer Malkani, Wahid Kandhro, Gul Sindhi, Salim Chana, Imran Soomro, Waheed Ghaho, Abdul Latif Malah, Mukesh Barthani, Mola Bakhsh Mohabati, Noor Hussain Kalhoro, Gul Munir Valhari and Abuzar Malah participated in the gathering. In the end, Prof. Madad Ali Jhatial said that creative writings are paramount, on which all corrections and criticisms were given. Creative, literary, scientific and research writings were presented in literary session.

headline: Qist Bazaar celebrating five years of operations
description: KARACHI - Qist Bazaar is celebrating five years of operations, having grown from a startup into one of Pakistan’s leading Shariah-compliant installment
author: PR
article_text:
KARACHI - Qist Bazaar is celebrating five years of operations, having grown from a startup into one of Pakistan’s leading Shariah-compliant installment financing platforms. With over 100 branches across more than 18 cities, the company has made essential household products accessible to hundreds of thousands of Pakistani families while maintaining profitability since day one.

Founded in 2021, Qist Bazaar has financed more than Rs 15 billion worth of products, including smartphones, laptops, refrigerators, washing machines, motorcycles, and solar solutions. Backed by Bank Alfalah and leading venture capital firms, including Indus Valley Capital and Gobi Partners, the company has processed over one million applications nationwide. Unlike conventional Buy Now, Pay Later models that often encourage discretionary spending, Qist Bazaar focuses on necessities rather than luxuries.

This disciplined product selection, combined with its community-based approach to customer relationships and credit assessment, has helped the company maintain bad debt below 4%, despite financing customers largely underserved by traditional financial institutions. The results challenge the perception that serving grassroots communities necessarily means accepting higher credit risk. Qist Bazaar’s distinctive strength lies in its physical presence within the communities it serves. From the historic streets of Androon-e-Lahore to the busy neighborhoods of Korangi, its branches and weekend mohalla exhibitions bring financing directly to customers.

Local branch managers play a central role, combining neighborhood knowledge and personal relationships with technology to build trust, assess customers, and support responsible repayments.

Building on its established branch network and customer data, Qist Bazaar is now expanding its Point-of-Sale (POS) partnerships with independent retailers and distributors.

Beginning with smartphones and laptops, the initiative will make Qist Bazaar’s financing available directly at participating retail outlets, creating a new distribution channel without relying exclusively on branch expansion.

Arif Lakhani, Co-Founder of Qist Bazaar, said: “You cannot understand a household’s financial reality sitting in a boardroom. You have to be in the neighborhoods, understand the people, and earn their trust. We made a conscious decision five years ago to finance necessities, not luxuries. Combined with our community-driven model, this has helped us keep bad debt below 4%, proving that financial inclusion and commercial discipline can go hand in hand. I am incredibly proud of what our team has achieved, but it feels like we are only getting started. Necessities First, Payments Later. That’s not just our tagline. It’s how we do business.”

Combined with our community-driven model, this has helped us keep bad debt below 4%, proving that financial inclusion and commercial discipline can go hand in hand. I am incredibly proud of what our team has achieved, but it feels like we are only getting started. Necessities First, Payments Later. That’s not just our tagline. It’s how we do business.”

With over 100 branches across more than 18 cities, the company has made essential household products accessible to hundreds of thousands of Pakistani families while maintaining profitability since day one.

Founded in 2021, Qist Bazaar has financed more than Rs 15 billion worth of products, including smartphones, laptops, refrigerators, washing machines, motorcycles, and solar solutions. Backed by Bank Alfalah and leading venture capital firms, including Indus Valley Capital and Gobi Partners, the company has processed over one million applications nationwide. Unlike conventional Buy Now, Pay Later models that often encourage discretionary spending, Qist Bazaar focuses on necessities rather than luxuries.

This disciplined product selection, combined with its community-based approach to customer relationships and credit assessment, has helped the company maintain bad debt below 4%, despite financing customers largely underserved by traditional financial institutions. The results challenge the perception that serving grassroots communities necessarily means accepting higher credit risk. Qist Bazaar’s distinctive strength lies in its physical presence within the communities it serves. From the historic streets of Androon-e-Lahore to the busy neighborhoods of Korangi, its branches and weekend mohalla exhibitions bring financing directly to customers.
Local branch managers play a central role, combining neighborhood knowledge and personal relationships with technology to build trust, assess customers, and support responsible repayments.

headline: HCSTSI seeks extension in gas supply hours for hotels, restaurants
description: HYDERABAD - President of the Hyderabad Chamber of Small Traders & Small Industry (HCSTSI), Nadeem Ahmed Siddiqui, has said that hotels and restaurants
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
HYDERABAD - President of the Hyderabad Chamber of Small Traders & Small Industry (HCSTSI), Nadeem Ahmed Siddiqui, has said that hotels and restaurants in Hyderabad are facing serious difficulties due to limited gas supply and rising LNG prices. HCSTSI President expressed these views during the inauguration of Haji Mehfooz Sheermal in Latifabad, Hyderabad, on the invitation of Muhammad Fahad Mian, the proprietor of Delhi Mehfooz Sheermal and Senior Vice President of HCSTSI President stated that the duration of gas supply by Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) is insufficient to meet the operational requirements of the hospitality sector, while, according to some business operators, gas is available for barely six hours a day. Meanwhile, the supply of LNG is also facing difficulties, and business circles have complained that they are being compelled to obtain it at prices considerably higher than the prescribed rates, highlighting the need for effective monitoring and regulatory oversight. The Chamber President further stated that the recent increase in LNG prices, coupled with limited gas supply, was placing additional financial pressure on hotels and restaurants. He attended the ceremony as the chief guest along with a delegation. He urged the government and relevant authorities to take immediate measures to extend gas supply duration for the hotel and restaurant sector, ensure the uninterrupted availability of LNG, and introduce effective monitoring of its pricing and distribution system. The Chamber President specifically demanded that SSGC provide special relief to hotels, restaurants, and other related businesses by introducing a suitable supply schedule that ensures at least 16 hours of gas supply daily.

Siddiqui also welcomed the expansion of business activities in Hyderabad, stating that the continuity and growth of trade and industry were essential for keeping the wheel of the national economy moving.

The ceremony was attended by HCSTSI Vice President Irfan Arbiani, former presidents, members of the Executive Committee, senior members, as well as political, social and business leaders of Hyderabad and other distinguished guests.

headline: NDF conducts community accountability forum in Nawabshah
description: NAWABSHAH - National Disability and Development Forum (NDF) with collaboration of Citizen Network for Budget Accountability (CNBA) and CPDI conducted a
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
NAWABSHAH - National Disability and Development Forum (NDF) with collaboration of Citizen Network for Budget Accountability (CNBA) and CPDI conducted a Community Accountability Forum to discuss citizens’ experiences and perceptions of public service delivery in health, education and municipal services.

CNBA is a nationwide network of civil society organizations managed by the Centre for Peace and Development Initiatives (CPDI). CPDI conducts research and provides technical support and guidance, while partner CSOs engage local communities and relevant stakeholders through the network. The forum brought together participants, including relevant stakeholders, community members, teachers, health professionals, local government representatives and civil society members. Participants openly shared their experiences, identified service delivery challenges and discussed areas requiring government attention.

The discussion covered the availability and quality of healthcare services, the presence of teachers and basic facilities in government schools, and access to clean drinking water, sanitation, drainage and waste management services. Based on the discussion, participants assessed these services through a Community Score Card, recording their collective perceptions on a scale of 1 to 5.

The exercise aims to bring citizens’ experiences into discussions on public service delivery and strengthen accountability by highlighting issues that require the attention of relevant government departments.

headline: Four killed in exchange of fire between two groups
description: LARKANA - At least four people, including two women, were killed in an exchange of fire between two rival groups in Larkana on Sunday, according to rescue
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LARKANA - At least four people, including two women, were killed in an exchange of fire between two rival groups in Larkana on Sunday, according to rescue sources quoted by a private TV channel.

Initial reports indicated that the exchange of fire continued for nearly five hours, resulting in the deaths of four people. Rescue teams rushed to the scene and shifted the bodies to a nearby hospital.

headline: Two boys killed as tractor trolley hits motorbike
description: HYDERABAD - Two boys lost their lives while a child was injured in an accident between motorbike and a tractor trolley on Thandi Sarak road here on
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
HYDERABAD - Two boys lost their lives while a child was injured in an accident between motorbike and a tractor trolley on Thandi Sarak road here on Sunday.

According to the GOR police, the deceased have been identified as 14 years old Rayan Hussain Chandio and 9 years old Faheem Chandio. The police informed that the tractor’s driver Jahanzeb Kandhro was captured by the people who later handed him over to the police. The police also impounded his vehicle. Azaan Chandio, the injured child, and the deceased were shifted to Liaquat University Hospital.

headline: Nestlé Pakistan to participate in 29th Sustainable Development Conference
description: ISLAMABAD - Nestlé Pakistan is set to participate in the 29th Sustainable Development Conference (SDC) and Sustainability Investment Expo (SIE), hosted
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Nestlé Pakistan is set to participate in the 29th Sustainable Development Conference (SDC) and Sustainability Investment Expo (SIE), hosted by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) from November 2 to 5, 2026, bringing to the forum its efforts to advance regenerative agriculture through food systems, climate action and water stewardship, better systems and packaging, and circular economy.

Building on its recognition at last year’s conference, where Nestlé Pakistan secured 1st Position in Renewable Energy & Low-Carbon Transitions at the SDC Sustainability Awards 2025 and received the Best Pavilion Award at the Sustainability Investment Expo, Nestlé Pakistan will return this year to demonstrate how sustainability is being embedded across its value chain, from farms and factories to communities and ecosystems.

Under the theme “Advancing Regenerative Food Systems at Scale,” Nestlé Pakistan’s presence at the Sustainability Investment Expo will offer visitors an immersive view of interventions being undertaken across its sustainability pillars. Artfully rendered models and interactive displays at the Nestlé pavilion will demonstrate Nestlé Pakistan’s sustainable practices and its partner farmers, helping visitors experience how renewable energy, regenerative farming, water stewardship and packaging circularity come together to strengthen the resilience of Pakistan’s food systems.

“At Nestlé, we believe building more resilient food systems starts with supporting farmer livelihoods and healthier ecosystems, while strengthening the value chain. Meaningful collaborations such as these help protect, renew, and restore the environment, while also paving the way for better systems that promote responsible packaging, and improved waste management for circular economy. We remain fully committed to scaling these efforts and creating lasting impact for people and the planet,” said Sheikh Waqar Ahmad, Head of Corporate Affairs & Sustainability, Nestlé Pakistan & Afghanistan.

Nestlé Pakistan’s participation will extend beyond the exhibition floor to the conference’s policy dialogue. The high-level joint plenary titled “Transforming Pakistan’s Agriculture and Food Systems in an Age of Disruption: AI for Regenerative and Climate-Smart Agriculture,” will bring the conversation around agriculture, climate resilience and emerging technologies into the wider SDC discourse.

“Pakistan’s development challenges require us to rethink how we produce food, manage natural resources and build resilience to climate change. The transition towards regenerative and climate-smart food systems is both environmentally as well as economically imperative to build a more sustainable and food-secure Pakistan,” said Dr Abid Qaiyum Suleri, Executive Director, Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI).

The showcase comes as Nestlé Pakistan continues to make advance its sustainability ambitions. Recording more than 48% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 compared with its 2018 baseline, Nestlé Pakistan is working towards halving emissions by 2030 and achieving net zero by 2050. Its interventions include 9.6 MW of solar power capacity across manufacturing sites, a 20 ton/hour biomass boiler at Kabirwala Factory, and renewable energy and energy-optimization initiatives comprising 135 solar plants and 25 biogas plants at farms.

Regenerative agriculture and circular ecosystem remain central to this journey. Nestlé aims to source 50% of its key ingredients from farmers adopting regenerative agriculture practices by 2030, while 40% of its fresh milk is already sourced through regenerative agriculture. On the circular economy front, Nestlé’s efforts are in-line with its vision that none of its packaging ends up in landfills or as litter. These efforts include packaging innovation and collection and recycling partnerships designed to support better packaging and better systems.

Nestlé Pakistan’s participation at SDC and SIE reflects its Creating Shared Value approach, which seeks to align long-term business success with meaningful impact for people, communities and the planet.

headline: PPP to continue struggle for the rights of Gilgit-Baltistan’s people
description: KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur has extended her heartiest congratulations to the people of
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur has extended her heartiest congratulations to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on the region’s 79th Independence Day, saying November 1 is a memorable day in our history when the brave people of Gilgit-Baltistan raised the banner of revolt against the oppressive rule of the Dogra regime and lit the flame of freedom. Their courage, sacrifices and resolve, she said, are an unforgettable treasure of our national history. In her message, Faryal Talpur said that Quaid-e-Awam Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto laid the foundation for freeing the people of Gilgit-Baltistan from an exploitative system through historic reforms, including the abolition of the FCR and the feudal order. Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto carried forward the journey of political representation and empowerment in the region in 1994 by establishing the Legislative Council.

President Asif Ali Zardari, during his first term, gave Gilgit-Baltistan a new political identity, an elected assembly and an empowered, province-style administrative structure through the 2009 reforms package. She added that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, carrying forward the same pro-people vision, is continuously raising his voice for the democratic, constitutional and fundamental rights of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan, their political autonomy, and equal development opportunities. Faryal Talpur said the love and attachment of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan for Pakistan is an unbreakable bond that endures from generation to generation. Fulfilling their dreams, securing a bright future for the youth, and ensuring that the fruits of development reach every citizen is our collective responsibility. She reaffirmed that the PPP will continue its struggle to protect the rights of the people of Gilgit-Baltistan and to secure a better future for them.

headline: Pakistan needs unified body to protect digital asset investors: AWAJ president
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan needs a unified industry representative body to safeguard digital asset investors and improve coordination with international
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan needs a unified industry representative body to safeguard digital asset investors and improve coordination with international cryptocurrency exchanges, President of Asia Web3 Alliance Japan (AWAJ) Hinza Asif has said.

The country’s growing cryptocurrency market faced significant challenges in the absence of verified investor data and an organised mechanism to represent industry stakeholders, particularly in the event of major cybersecurity or financial incidents involving international exchanges, Hinza Asif said in a statement.

She pointed out that Pakistan ranked third in the 2025 Global Crypto Adoption Index compiled by Chainalysis. Estimates suggesting around 40 million crypto-linked accounts and digital asset exposure ranging between $10 billion and $20 billion indicated the potential scale of the market, although these figures had not been officially verified as individual investor numbers.

Referring to reports of a multibillion-dollar cybersecurity incident involving Binance, Hinza said security breaches at major exchanges could result in financial losses, unauthorised transactions and disruptions to withdrawals, potentially undermining investor confidence.

She added that the extent of the reported incident and its potential impact on Pakistani investors remained unclear and required independent verification. “The question is who will represent and protect Pakistani investors if an international exchange faces a major cybersecurity or financial crisis,” she said, adding that the country lacked an established mechanism to coordinate investor complaints and engage with international exchanges in such circumstances.

Hinza, who has more than 11 years of international market experience in Japan, said Pakistan needed to develop institutional structures alongside its expanding digital finance sector. Through AWAJ, she has been involved in technology partnerships, startup development and engagement with Japanese corporations, financial institutions and venture capital firms. Welcoming the government’s regulatory initiatives through the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), she said the regulator and an independent industry association would have complementary roles.

While PVARA would oversee regulatory matters within its legal mandate, an industry representative body could provide a platform for FinTech companies, blockchain businesses, technology professionals and investors to raise concerns and engage with policymakers, she said.

Hinza Asif called for the establishment of a national digital finance platform, supported by reliable market research, coordinated investor grievance mechanisms, cybersecurity awareness and formal partnerships with international industry organisations.

She said Pakistan’s digital finance potential extended beyond cryptocurrency trading to include blockchain applications, digital payments, financial technology entrepreneurship and international investment.

“Pakistan cannot afford to wait for a major financial crisis before establishing the necessary mechanisms for investor protection and institutional coordination,” she said.

The country’s growing cryptocurrency market faced significant challenges in the absence of verified investor data and an organised mechanism to represent industry stakeholders, particularly in the event of major cybersecurity or financial incidents involving international exchanges, Hinza Asif said in a statement.

She pointed out that Pakistan ranked third in the 2025 Global Crypto Adoption Index compiled by Chainalysis. Estimates suggesting around 40 million crypto-linked accounts and digital asset exposure ranging between $10 billion and $20 billion indicated the potential scale of the market, although these figures had not been officially verified as individual investor numbers.

Referring to reports of a multibillion-dollar cybersecurity incident involving Binance, Hinza said security breaches at major exchanges could result in financial losses, unauthorised transactions and disruptions to withdrawals, potentially undermining investor confidence.

Welcoming the government’s regulatory initiatives through the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), she said the regulator and an independent industry association would have complementary roles.

While PVARA would oversee regulatory matters within its legal mandate, an industry representative body could provide a platform for FinTech companies, blockchain businesses, technology professionals and investors to raise concerns and engage with policymakers, she said.

Hinza Asif called for the establishment of a national digital finance platform, supported by reliable market research, coordinated investor grievance mechanisms, cybersecurity awareness and formal partnerships with international industry organisations.

“Pakistan cannot afford to wait for a major financial crisis before establishing the necessary mechanisms for investor protection and institutional coordination,” she said.

headline: Pakistan reports eighth polio case
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has reported its eighth polio case of 2026, involving a 13-month-old girl from Khyber district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.According to the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has reported its eighth polio case of 2026, involving a 13-month-old girl from Khyber district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), the affected child belongs to Union Council Janbaz-B in Tehsil Bara. This is the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year and the sixth from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, highlighting the continued threat of poliovirus transmission in the province. Although overall wild poliovirus transmission has declined in Pakistan this year, positive environmental samples from the Peshawar block, comprising Peshawar and Khyber districts, indicate continued virus circulation and a risk to unvaccinated children. The Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) has launched a comprehensive investigation into the latest case and is assessing science-based measures to prevent further transmission, including targeted vaccination activities and strengthening routine immunisation. Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns so far in 2026, protecting more than 45 million children multiple times. Additional targeted campaigns have also been carried out in high-risk areas, including the Peshawar block, using oral and injectable vaccines. During the September subnational campaign, more than 29.3 million children were vaccinated across the country. The next campaign, scheduled for November 2 to 8, aims to protect nearly 24 million children in 97 districts, including Khyber. According to the PEI, Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8 percent, from an estimated 20,000 cases in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025. However, eight cases have been reported so far in 2026, including six from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, four of them from southern districts, and two from Sindh. Polio is a highly contagious viral disease that has no cure and can cause permanent paralysis and, in severe cases, death. However, it is preventable through safe and effective vaccination, which has been used in 195 countries, including Muslim-majority nations. The PEI has urged parents and caregivers to ensure that every child under five receives oral polio vaccine during every campaign, alongside completing routine immunisation schedules. It urged parents to ensure vaccination of all children under five during the upcoming nationwide subnational campaign scheduled for November 2 to 8. It emphasized that frontline vaccination workers continued to visit households to administer vaccines, while parents and caregivers remained essential partners in protecting children against the potentially crippling disease. Communities, religious leaders and the media have been asked to play an active role in promoting vaccination, countering misinformation and ensuring that no child was missed during the upcoming campaign. The PEI stressed that polio eradication was a collective responsibility, calling for sustained public cooperation to protect children and achieve a polio-free Pakistan.

headline: ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise Rs2-3b through IPO
description: LAHORE - ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) of 132 million ordinary shares on
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - ABHI Microfinance Bank plans to raise between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) of 132 million ordinary shares on the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX), with a floor price of Rs15 per share. According to details disclosed to the PSX, the book-building process will take place on November 5 and 6, while the retail subscription period is scheduled for November 12 and 13. The book-building portion comprises 99 million ordinary shares, representing 75% of the total issue, at a floor price of Rs15 per share, including a premium of Rs5 per share. The price band allows a maximum increase of 50%, taking the upper price limit to Rs22.50 per share.

The general public portion of the offering will be fully underwritten by Arif Habib Limited, Topline Securities Limited, Growth Securities (Private) Limited and Dawood Equities Limited. At the floor price, the bank expects to raise gross proceeds of Rs1.98 billion, which will primarily be used to expand its loan portfolio and strengthen its capital base. The proposed equity injection is expected to improve the bank’s capital adequacy ratio (CAR), support balance-sheet growth and help it meet the minimum regulatory capital requirements prescribed by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) for microfinance banks.

According to the bank’s projections, the IPO proceeds will help address its capital shortfall and bring its CAR closer to the regulatory threshold. The bank’s projected profitability over the following two years is expected to further strengthen its capital position and support compliance with regulatory requirements. The bank has continued to report profits in 2026 as the management estimates a profit of approximately Rs1.5 billion in the second half of calendar year 2026, taking the projected full-year profit to around Rs3 billion. The bank’s forecast puts its 2026 profit at Rs2.927 billion. The bank expects its CAR to turn positive and reach approximately 4.3% by the end of 2026, following the addition of IPO proceeds and projected earnings, before accounting for other capital adjustments. Profitability is projected to improve further in 2027, adding to retained earnings.

headline: CDA appoints 3 retired military officers as DGs
description: ISLAMABAD - The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has posted three senior officers as Directors General (DGs) against key positions in the authority
author: Our Staff Reporter

headline: Serena Hotels celebrates 5 years of Mehfil-e-Sukhan
description: ISLAMABAD - Serena Hotels hosted the fifth edition of Mehfil-e-Sukhan on Saturday evening, bringing together some of Pakistan’s most distinguished
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Serena Hotels hosted the fifth edition of Mehfil-e-Sukhan on Saturday evening, bringing together some of Pakistan’s most distinguished poets for its annual mushaira at the Islamabad Serena Hotel. Held under Serena’s Cultural Diplomacy Initiative, the evening honoured one of the region’s oldest literary traditions, and the enduring power of Urdu verse to bring people together across generations, regions and backgrounds. Presided over by Abbas Naqvi and Shakeel Jazaib, the mehfil featured Kishwar Naheed, Iftikhar Arif, Anwar Shaoor, Abbas Tabish, Izhar ul Haq, Hamid Ateeq Sarwar, Haris Khaleeq, Ahmed Salman, Wasi Shah, Adnan Baig, Shakeel Jazib, Ashfaq Nasir, Saima Aftab, Rehman Faris, Zarnigar Abbas and Saba Uddin Hunzai. Spanning the classical and the contemporary, their readings reflected the range of Urdu poetry and its continuing ability to speak to the present.

“Poetry has always been a meeting place. For five years, Mehfil-e-Sukhan has opened Serena’s doors to the poets who give voice to Pakistan, and to the audiences, from Pakistan and beyond, who come to listen. At its heart, cultural diplomacy is simply that: an invitation to sit together and share in something enduring,” said Mr. Aziz Boolani, Global CEO of Serena Hotels. Since its first edition in 2022, Mehfil-e-Sukhan has become a fixture of the capital’s cultural calendar: a setting in which celebrated poets and appreciative audiences meet in the spirit of the traditional mushaira. Its fifth edition reaffirms Serena’s commitment to keeping Urdu’s literary heritage alive. Mehfil-e-Sukhan forms part of Serena’s wider support for literature and the arts across Pakistan, including the Lahore Literary Festival and the Quetta Literary Festival, which give writers, poets and thinkers a platform to share ideas with wider audiences.

Through its Cultural Diplomacy Initiative, Serena opens its spaces to Pakistan’s artists, writers and thinkers, and to the communities, at home and abroad, who come to meet them. It reflects a belief that understanding between people often begins with shared culture, and that Pakistan’s rich and plural heritage deserves to be celebrated, preserved and heard.

headline: Iran, US continue Doha talks as Tehran warns of wider war
description: TEHRAN - Iran and the United States continued diplomatic efforts to end their eight-month-old conflict on Sunday, as Iranian negotiators held a third
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: TEHRAN - Iran and the United States continued diplomatic efforts to end their eight-month-old conflict on Sunday, as Iranian negotiators held a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha amid growing threats of renewed military confrontation. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said consultations with Qatari officials were ongoing but no final agreement had been reached, stressing that Tehran was prepared for both diplomacy and defence. Speaking to state media, Araghchi said the outcome of the discussions depended on Washington’s response to Iran’s proposals and questions. He maintained that there was no plan to hold direct negotiations with American officials during his latest visit. Iran has insisted on seven conditions for any agreement, with National Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei reiterating that diplomacy would remain an option if Tehran’s demands were met. He warned, however, that any fresh attack on Iran would invite devastating retaliation using new weapons. An official briefed on the discussions told a news wire that Iranian negotiators had been engaged in talks with Qatari mediators for three consecutive days to advance an understanding aimed at ending the US-Israeli war against Iran. Araghchi also indicated that Tehran and Doha had developed a proposal for reopening the strategically important Strait of Hormuz within two days of a potential agreement with Washington. However, diplomatic efforts have been accompanied by increasingly hardline statements from both sides. US President Donald Trump said Washington could strike Iran’s remaining suspected nuclear facilities within minutes, despite describing negotiations as progressing. Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that American military operations had severely weakened Iran’s armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only one or two targets requiring further action. He specifically mentioned the suspected underground nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain, saying the United States could deal with the remaining sites quickly. Iran has denied conducting nuclear activities at the facility. Trump said Washington was not in a hurry to reach an agreement but reiterated that Iran would never be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons. He also declined to rule out renewed military action, saying he could not disclose whether strikes might resume in the coming days. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not made a decision about further attacks and preferred a diplomatic settlement. Meanwhile, US Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs Donald Blome warned that Washington was prepared to consider other options if normal navigation through the Strait of Hormuz was not restored. Speaking at the Manama Dialogue security forum in Bahrain, Blome said diplomatic channels remained open but stressed that the United States would not allow Iran to hold the region and global economy hostage. Iran, meanwhile, has stepped up military preparedness. Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said Tehran was rapidly enhancing its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond without geographical limitations. He said the military was strengthening its smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, warning that any attack would receive an appropriate and decisive response. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier General Yadollah Javani said Iranian forces were operating on the assumption that the United States or Israel could launch an attack at any moment. He claimed Iran’s military capabilities allowed it to respond through defensive, pre-emptive and offensive operations, warning that any area entered by enemy forces could become a “killing ground”. Iranian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia also warned that any renewed US aggression would trigger an immediate and decisive response on a larger scale than before. He cautioned that a future conflict would not necessarily remain confined to West Asia. In another development, Iran designated Britain’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organisations and its intelligence agency MI6 as a hostile group, according to the Iranian Foreign Ministry. The decision was announced in response to Britain’s designation of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organisation under the State Threats Act 2026 on July 13. Tehran also accused London of supporting the US-Israeli military campaign by providing access to military and logistical facilities under British jurisdiction. Iran has separately submitted documents and photographic evidence of alleged US and Israeli attacks on its ports, civilian vessels and maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation, warning that damage to navigation and rescue systems could endanger shipping and seafarers across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Sea of Oman. Regional countries have expressed concern over the possibility of another escalation. UAE presidential diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash said Abu Dhabi hoped negotiations would produce a diplomatic breakthrough but was prepared for the worst. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah television reported that two air raids had targeted an oil facility in the Bajil district of western Hodeidah governorate, wounding at least three civilians. There was no immediate comment from the Saudi-led coalition. The diplomatic efforts come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the November 3 US midterm elections. Trump has indicated that Washington would refrain from launching fresh attacks before the vote, while Tehran has warned that any new confrontation could be longer and more extensive than the previous conflict. The continuing tensions have disrupted global oil supplies and raised fears of a wider regional crisis, with the future of the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a central issue in negotiations.

However, diplomatic efforts have been accompanied by increasingly hardline statements from both sides. US President Donald Trump said Washington could strike Iran’s remaining suspected nuclear facilities within minutes, despite describing negotiations as progressing.
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that American military operations had severely weakened Iran’s armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only one or two targets requiring further action.
He specifically mentioned the suspected underground nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain, saying the United States could deal with the remaining sites quickly. Iran has denied conducting nuclear activities at the facility.
Trump said Washington was not in a hurry to reach an agreement but reiterated that Iran would never be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons. He also declined to rule out renewed military action, saying he could not disclose whether strikes might resume in the coming days.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not made a decision about further attacks and preferred a diplomatic settlement.
Meanwhile, US Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs Donald Blome warned that Washington was prepared to consider other options if normal navigation through the Strait of Hormuz was not restored.
Speaking at the Manama Dialogue security forum in Bahrain, Blome said diplomatic channels remained open but stressed that the United States would not allow Iran to hold the region and global economy hostage.
Iran, meanwhile, has stepped up military preparedness. Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said Tehran was rapidly enhancing its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond without geographical limitations.
He said the military was strengthening its smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, warning that any attack would receive an appropriate and decisive response.
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier General Yadollah Javani said Iranian forces were operating on the assumption that the United States or Israel could launch an attack at any moment.
He claimed Iran’s military capabilities allowed it to respond through defensive, pre-emptive and offensive operations, warning that any area entered by enemy forces could become a “killing ground”.

headline: Saudi-led coalition launches operation to ‘neutralise’ Houthi military resources
description: RIYADH - The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it had carried out a military operation to “neutralise vital resources” used by the Houthi
author: News Source
article_text: RIYADH - The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it had carried out a military operation to “neutralise vital resources” used by the Houthi group to support its war effort and strengthen its military capabilities, particularly ballistic missiles and drones. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that the operation took place on Sunday morning following continued Houthi attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The coalition’s joint forces command had monitored the Houthis’ “continued use of vital resources to support their war effort and bolster their military capabilities, especially ballistic missiles and drones,” he said. Al-Maliki said the continued attacks posed a direct threat to civilian lives and the safety of civilian infrastructure. The operation sought to “neutralise” resources used by the group to carry out repeated attacks and threaten the security of Saudi Arabia and Yemen, as well as shipping lanes in the southern Red Sea, he added. The statement did not identify the targeted locations or specify the nature of the resources it said had been neutralised. It also provided no details on casualties or material damage. There was no immediate comment from the Houthis. Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa. Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports. The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement. Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government. A strike at an industrial complex in Saudi Arabia’s Dammam caused a huge fire on Sunday, Iran’s state-run IRNA Nerecognisedws Agency reported. “A Yemeni strike hit an industrial complex in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, sparking a large fire at the facility,” IRNA said in a post on X. A drone belonging to Yemen’s Houthi group struck a family home in the Old Airport neighbourhood in western Taiz city, according to Al Jazeera, reportedly killing a mother and daughter. The development comes amid escalating hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government. The two sides have exchanged daily attacks since a fragile truce collapsed over the summer. The Houthis on Thursday reported that 12 people had been killed and three others critically injured in what they described as Saudi strikes on residential areas in western Yemen. The group’s health ministry said the casualties occurred when homes belonging to two families were targeted in Al-Barah, in Maqbana district. The claims could not be independently verified. The Houthis had reported at least 14 deaths in Saudi strikes on a petrol station and market on Wednesday, while the group also targeted the airport in Aden, a stronghold of Yemen’s internationally recognised government, wounding civilians. The latest escalation follows a breakdown of the 2022 truce in July, after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace. The move triggered renewed attacks, with the rebels subsequently targeting Saudi territory, shipping and oil facilities. The Houthis have also intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and prompted the cancellation of major events, threatening the kingdom’s economic diversification plans. Yemen has endured conflict since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year in support of the government. More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since hostilities resumed, according to United Nations figures. Separately, Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council issued two decrees on Sunday appointing new governors for al-Bayda in central Yemen and al-Jawf in the north, two provinces partially controlled by the Houthis. The government-run version of Saba News Agency said that Major General Hussein al-Ajji Ali al-Awadhi was appointed as governor of al-Bayda. Major General Amin Ali al-Akimi was also named as governor of al-Jawf and commander of its military axis, the agency added. Al-Awadhi replaces former al-Bayda governor Nasser al-Sawadi, while al-Akimi takes over al-Jawf from al-Awadhi, who had served as the province’s governor. The appointments come as both provinces face a complex military situation, with clashes continuing between government forces and the Houthi group over control of strategic positions. The Houthis control most areas of al-Bayda, while control of al-Jawf is divided between the group and government forces. Al-Bayda holds strategic importance because of its central location in Yemen and its borders with eight other provinces, four in the north and four in the south. Al-Jawf is also of military and geographic significance because it shares a land border with Saudi Arabia and lies near the Houthi-controlled provinces of Saada, Amran and Sanaa. It also borders Marib and Hadhramaut, which are under government control. Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa. Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports. The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement. Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Preparations have been completed for the 6th Pakistan Water Week 2026, which will kick off in Islamabad on November 2 to bring national and international stakeholders together to advance water security and climate-resilient food systems. The five-day international conference, themed “Commitments to Action: Advancing Water Security and Achieving Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Pakistan,” will continue until November 6. The event is being organised by the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), in collaboration with the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) and the Ministry of Water Resources. The conference will bring together policymakers, parliamentarians, researchers, development partners, youth leaders, civil society representatives and media professionals, with participation available both in person and online.

It will feature two parallel thematic tracks, each comprising 13 sessions, focusing on strengthening water, agriculture and food systems through effective policy implementation and scaling up inclusive innovations for climate resilience. Key topics to be discussed include groundwater management, irrigation reforms, drought and health, climate financing, Pakistan’s preparations for COP31, the water-energy-food-environment nexus, artificial intelligence, digital twins, cryosphere risks in the Upper Indus Basin, and women’s and youth leadership in water security. Three plenary sessions will focus on development partners’ priorities in water and climate, water governance in the Indus Basin, and Australian water innovations for the basin. IWMI Director General Dr. Mark Smith will join the second-day plenary panel online alongside national and international experts. International participants will also visit a water body during a study tour scheduled for the final day of the conference. Dr. Mohsin Hafeez, Strategic Program Director for Water, Food and Ecosystems at IWMI said that Pakistan already has many of the policies, laws and plans it needs. The real challenge is implementation.

He said the conference aimed to bridge the gap between evidence and decision-making by linking policy commitments with practical action on the ground. IWMI Country Representative for Pakistan Dr. Muhammad Ashraf told APP that water security had become central to Pakistan’s food security, economy and climate resilience. He said the conference would bring science, policy and practice together to identify priorities, determine responsibilities and establish mechanisms to track progress. The event is supported by PCRWR through the Ministry of The event is supported by PCRWR through the Ministry of Water Resources, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR), the CGIAR Policy Innovations Science Program, and the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).
