headline: Dishonesty’s Short Life
description: Man is born honest. Every newborn is blessed with a minuscule of divine traits. The purity of the soul is pristine and clear. Man suffers from no ailments of
author: Sirajuddin Aziz
article_text:
Man is born honest. Every newborn is blessed with a minuscule of divine traits. The purity of the soul is pristine and clear. Man suffers from no ailments of attitude and behaviour until he comes into contact with the environment outside himself: society. If humans were to live in isolation, they would most likely retain their original purity. Robinson Crusoe had no complexes of inferiority or superiority. He had no one to compare himself with and no sense of competition.

Regrettably, a sense of competition is induced in children at a very young age, when parents and family begin comparing them with others. The indirect message is to excel over fellow children. This malaise begins at home and continues through school, college, university and the professional world. The spirit of beating others is given respect by calling it “competitiveness”.

Students are encouraged to be competitive, while teachers guide them towards noble achievements. Yet, negative human instincts can drive individuals beyond accepted norms of behaviour. Consequently, success through ignoble means gradually becomes acceptable.

There is a need to ponder this dilemma. The curriculum, teacher, and environment may be the same, yet in a class of 25 students, one secures the first position while another ranks last. Nature is not unkind or injudicious, so what explains these different results? The answer lies in applying one’s natural endowment of intelligence with hard work and focus. Those who endeavour with intellect achieve sustainable success. The intentionality behind every action determines the nobility of its objective. Those who seek to achieve their goals at “any cost” may experience sudden success, but it rarely lasts. Human history is replete with such examples.

In Japan, I believe, children are not graded until Class 5, whether in sports or academics.

As a member of an interview panel for senior executive positions, I was once given an assessment form by the HR division to evaluate candidates. It listed ten or so personality traits against which we were expected to assign scores from 1 to 10, with 10 being the highest. To my chagrin, the first trait was “honesty and integrity”. How can one assign numerical ratings to subjective, non-quantifiable traits? I questioned how we could hire anyone scoring less than 10 on honesty and integrity. These qualities are either present or absent. There is no middle ground. A person is either honest or dishonest. The notion of someone being honest between 10 and 11 am but dishonest by 3 or 4 pm is ridiculous.

The line between honesty and dishonesty is as thin as a cat’s whiskers and as fragile as a spider’s web. They are separate domains. The dividing line between white and black is strong, yet actions often smudge it, giving rise to the “grey area”. This growing ocean of grey unleashes a tsunami of moral decline upon the shores of truth and honesty.

When a society honours the dishonourable, moral decay begins. When justice is traded for gold and silver, a virtuous society approaches its end. If a noble profession becomes ignoble through its practitioners’ waywardness, little hope remains for future generations. Every individual is guilty of dishonesty, either through unlawful gains or complicity through tolerance. The power of silence mutes the weapon of speech.

Even religious understanding is corrupted, whether through ignorance or deliberate intent to weaken social structures. A parable tells of a milkman who, after adulterating pure milk with water, quenched his thirst with the remaining water. Sitting by the roadside, he explained that it was a Sunnah to drink water while seated. How much further can we descend in thought, understanding and behaviour? Sinning has become acceptable.

The Sultans of Delhi and the subcontinent were dishonest. To protect their power and wealth, they betrayed the population by facilitating British rule. A handful subjugated millions, and the orders of General Dyer were carried out by Indians. Prince Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia, who spent years in exile in Beijing, remarked: “Time will eventually uncover dishonesty and lies; history has no place for them.”

Dishonesty has no relationship with the amount involved. A single paisa can corrupt. Even a cent of corruption constitutes dishonesty. The office boy in my civil servant father’s office would cycle five kilometres to return a five-rupee note, saying, “Sir, you left this on the table.” Father would ask why he had not returned it the next day. The reply was, “How could I keep it overnight? Life is uncertain.” Honesty and its principles are universal yet easy to practise for those committed to it.

Since dishonesty is rampant, it is no longer abhorred as a social evil. Shopkeepers and buyers alike accept it as a norm of business. When moral uprightness ceases to be a value, it reveals the depth of corruption. We willingly offer bribes for legitimate or otherwise objectives. Forget the taker; the strike must begin with the giver.

Corruption is only one segment of dishonesty. When it permeates every sector, nations ingloriously occupy the lowest rungs of global corruption indices. We are not known for our honesty. That is a reality.

At school, we were taught that “honesty is the best policy”. Why have we consigned this dictum to forgotten memories? Honesty is a principle: it is either present or absent. There is no middle ground. The blurred lines must be clearly delineated, with a China wall between white and black. The grey area must be narrowed through a firm pledge of action.

Sirajuddin Aziz The writer is a Senior Banker & Freelance Columnist.

article_html:
Man is born honest. Every newborn is blessed with a minuscule of divine traits. The purity of the soul is pristine and clear. Man suffers from no ailments of attitude and behaviour until he comes into contact with the environment outside himself: society. If humans were to live in isolation, they would most likely retain their original purity. Robinson Crusoe had no complexes of inferiority or superiority. He had no one to compare himself with and no sense of competition.

Regrettably, a sense of competition is induced in children at a very young age, when parents and family begin comparing them with others. The indirect message is to excel over fellow children. This malaise begins at home and continues through school, college, university and the professional world. The spirit of beating others is given respect by calling it “competitiveness”.

False rape cases emerge as new challenge for south Punjab police

Students are encouraged to be competitive, while teachers guide them towards noble achievements. Yet, negative human instincts can drive individuals beyond accepted norms of behaviour. Consequently, success through ignoble means gradually becomes acceptable.

There is a need to ponder this dilemma. The curriculum, teacher, and environment may be the same, yet in a class of 25 students, one secures the first position while another ranks last. Nature is not unkind or injudicious, so what explains these different results? The answer lies in applying one’s natural endowment of intelligence with hard work and focus. Those who endeavour with intellect achieve sustainable success. The intentionality behind every action determines the nobility of its objective. Those who seek to achieve their goals at “any cost” may experience sudden success, but it rarely lasts. Human history is replete with such examples.

DIG Prisons inspects Bahawalnagar District Jail

In Japan, I believe, children are not graded until Class 5, whether in sports or academics.

As a member of an interview panel for senior executive positions, I was once given an assessment form by the HR division to evaluate candidates. It listed ten or so personality traits against which we were expected to assign scores from 1 to 10, with 10 being the highest. To my chagrin, the first trait was “honesty and integrity”. How can one assign numerical ratings to subjective, non-quantifiable traits? I questioned how we could hire anyone scoring less than 10 on honesty and integrity. These qualities are either present or absent. There is no middle ground. A person is either honest or dishonest. The notion of someone being honest between 10 and 11 am but dishonest by 3 or 4 pm is ridiculous.

Man kills former mother-in-law over divorce dispute

The line between honesty and dishonesty is as thin as a cat’s whiskers and as fragile as a spider’s web. They are separate domains. The dividing line between white and black is strong, yet actions often smudge it, giving rise to the “grey area”. This growing ocean of grey unleashes a tsunami of moral decline upon the shores of truth and honesty.

When a society honours the dishonourable, moral decay begins. When justice is traded for gold and silver, a virtuous society approaches its end. If a noble profession becomes ignoble through its practitioners’ waywardness, little hope remains for future generations. Every individual is guilty of dishonesty, either through unlawful gains or complicity through tolerance. The power of silence mutes the weapon of speech.

FIC schedules live cardiac surgeries during PHC inspection

Even religious understanding is corrupted, whether through ignorance or deliberate intent to weaken social structures. A parable tells of a milkman who, after adulterating pure milk with water, quenched his thirst with the remaining water. Sitting by the roadside, he explained that it was a Sunnah to drink water while seated. How much further can we descend in thought, understanding and behaviour? Sinning has become acceptable.

The Sultans of Delhi and the subcontinent were dishonest. To protect their power and wealth, they betrayed the population by facilitating British rule. A handful subjugated millions, and the orders of General Dyer were carried out by Indians. Prince Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia, who spent years in exile in Beijing, remarked: “Time will eventually uncover dishonesty and lies; history has no place for them.”

Khawaja Farid University, college face decline amid mismanagement

Dishonesty has no relationship with the amount involved. A single paisa can corrupt. Even a cent of corruption constitutes dishonesty. The office boy in my civil servant father’s office would cycle five kilometres to return a five-rupee note, saying, “Sir, you left this on the table.” Father would ask why he had not returned it the next day. The reply was, “How could I keep it overnight? Life is uncertain.” Honesty and its principles are universal yet easy to practise for those committed to it.

Since dishonesty is rampant, it is no longer abhorred as a social evil. Shopkeepers and buyers alike accept it as a norm of business. When moral uprightness ceases to be a value, it reveals the depth of corruption. We willingly offer bribes for legitimate or otherwise objectives. Forget the taker; the strike must begin with the giver.

Corruption is only one segment of dishonesty. When it permeates every sector, nations ingloriously occupy the lowest rungs of global corruption indices. We are not known for our honesty. That is a reality.

At school, we were taught that “honesty is the best policy”. Why have we consigned this dictum to forgotten memories? Honesty is a principle: it is either present or absent. There is no middle ground. The blurred lines must be clearly delineated, with a China wall between white and black. The grey area must be narrowed through a firm pledge of action.

Sirajuddin Aziz
The writer is a Senior Banker & Freelance Columnist.

headline: Dangerous Border Conduct
description: The latest exchange of fire along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Lower South Waziristan, where Pakistani security forces responded to unprovoked firing
author: The Nation
article_text:
The latest exchange of fire along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Lower South Waziristan, where Pakistani security forces responded to unprovoked firing from Afghan posts, underscores the growing volatility on Pakistan’s western frontier. With repeated cross-border incidents, including attacks resulting in civilian casualties, Afghanistan’s conduct is becoming an increasingly serious concern for regional peace and stability.

Pakistan’s response to these provocations must be viewed within the context of its responsibility to protect its territorial integrity and citizens. No sovereign state can be expected to remain passive in the face of armed aggression, particularly when its border communities are repeatedly exposed to insecurity. A measured but firm response is therefore justified, especially when diplomatic assurances have failed to translate into tangible action on the ground.

The consequences extend beyond bilateral relations. South and Central Asia remain vulnerable to interconnected security threats, and instability in one country can quickly spill across borders. Afghanistan’s failure to address these concerns risks undermining regional connectivity, economic cooperation and efforts to establish lasting peace.

The international community must recognise that counterterrorism cannot remain a matter of selective concern. Pakistan’s security apprehensions warrant serious consideration, while Afghanistan must be held accountable for preventing its territory from becoming a source of cross-border violence. Lasting stability requires restraint, responsible state conduct and verifiable action against militant networks. Without these, recurring border clashes will continue to erode trust and threaten the wider region.

headline: Civic Heritage
description: Lahore Gymkhana’s colonial beginnings are part of its history, but reducing its present identity to that legacy is disingenuous. Since Partition, it has
author: The Nation
article_text:
Lahore Gymkhana’s colonial beginnings are part of its history, but reducing its present identity to that legacy is disingenuous. Since Partition, it has evolved into a civilian institution with thousands of members from varied professional backgrounds, including doctors, engineers, academics, journalists, public officials and businesspeople. Its member-led elections distinguish it from an establishment governed solely through official appointment. Its privileges merit scrutiny, but its evolution cannot simply be erased.

Nor is the club merely a collection of lawns and sporting facilities. For generations, it has served as a centre for sporting, literary, social and cultural activity. Its green grounds contribute to Lahore’s scarce open spaces, offering environmental and recreational value in a city burdened by pollution and unchecked development. Losing such an institution would carry consequences beyond its membership.

Questions about the lease, rent, construction approvals and tax obligations are legitimate and require transparent answers. Yet the same standards must apply to other institutions occupying valuable public land. Singling out a civilian institution while comparable arrangements escape scrutiny would make accountability appear selective. Reclaiming land is not, in itself, public service; what replaces it, who benefits, and whether citizens gain accessible facilities are the questions that matter.

Lahore’s heritage cannot be protected through slogans, nor can public interest be reduced to land value. The Punjab government must demonstrate that any action is lawful, consistent, and directed towards the city’s collective good and long-term wellbeing.

Lahore’s heritage cannot be protected through slogans, nor can public interest be reduced to land value. The Punjab government must demonstrate that any action is lawful, consistent, and directed towards the city’s collective good and long-term wellbeing.

headline: Shaping Financial Reform
description: Pakistan’s assumption of the chairmanship of the Group of 24 (G-24), a coalition of developing nations, marks a significant diplomatic and economic
author: The Nation
article_text:
Pakistan’s assumption of the chairmanship of the Group of 24 (G-24), a coalition of developing nations, marks a significant diplomatic and economic opportunity. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has pledged to strengthen the collective voice of emerging economies, advocate fairer representation in international financial institutions, and push for more accessible development financing. At a time when developing countries face mounting debt, climate-related pressures and economic uncertainty, Pakistan’s new position carries considerable significance.

The appointment offers Pakistan an opportunity to extend its influence beyond traditional diplomatic engagements and contribute to discussions that shape the global economic order. As chair, Islamabad can bring greater attention to the structural challenges confronting developing economies, particularly their limited influence over decisions made by institutions such as the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

For Pakistan, the chairmanship also has implications at home. Its own experience with economic stabilisation, debt management and climate vulnerability provides a relevant perspective on the difficulties faced by developing nations. By advancing these concerns internationally, Pakistan can strengthen its economic diplomacy, build partnerships with countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America, and create opportunities for greater cooperation in trade, investment and development financing.

The chairmanship should be treated as more than a ceremonial distinction. It presents Pakistan with a platform to influence international debate while advancing its own economic interests. Translating this position into meaningful outcomes would strengthen the country’s standing and give its voice greater weight in shaping a fairer global financial system.

headline: Governor Kundi calls peace key to KP’s progress
description: Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday described sustainable peace as essential for the province’s progress and
author: APP
article_text:
Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday described sustainable peace as essential for the province’s progress and prosperity, urging all sections of society to contribute to promoting harmony and projecting a positive image of the region.

Addressing the Urs ceremony at Darbar-e-Aalia Murshad Abad Sharif, the governor stressed the need for unity, lasting peace, development and the promotion of sports. He also called for the effective utilisation of the province’s natural resources and collective efforts to improve public welfare.

Former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, Adviser Tayab Qureshi and other guests attended the ceremony. Governor Kundi thanked the organisers for inviting him and welcomed visitors from outside the province.

He said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had endured decades of terrorism and made immense sacrifices in the fight against militancy. Religious scholars, security personnel, politicians and innocent students, including those martyred in the Army Public School (APS) attack, had laid down their lives for peace, he added.

The governor said peace was a fundamental prerequisite for development and that the province, known for its resilience in the face of terrorism, was determined to move towards lasting stability and progress.

Highlighting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s potential in sports, he said the province had produced outstanding athletes from Mardan, Dera Ismail Khan and Bannu who had earned international recognition. He stressed the need to provide young people with opportunities to excel in sports and other fields.

He said the province was blessed with abundant natural resources, including oil, gas and water, as well as considerable tourism potential. The Tarbela Dam was among its major assets, he added, saying that the effective utilisation of these resources could transform the provincial economy.

Recalling Peshawar’s former reputation as the “City of Flowers”, Governor Kundi said concerted efforts were needed to restore the province’s positive image. “The safety of our people comes first, followed by the development of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the progress of the country,” he remarked, expressing confidence that the province would witness significant positive change in the near future.

He also underscored the role of religious scholars in promoting peace, unity and interfaith and social harmony across the province. He urged the ulema to use their influence to promote tolerance, discourage extremism and support collective efforts to secure lasting peace.

At the conclusion of the ceremony, Governor Kundi congratulated newly graduated Huffaz and distributed certificates among them. He also visited the institution’s library and appreciated its educational services. The organisers presented him with a traditional shawl as a mark of respect.

headline: KP orders shifting of students from unsafe school buildings
description: PESHAWAR - The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elementary and Secondary Education Department has ordered the immediate relocation of students from dilapidated and dangerous
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR - The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elementary and Secondary Education Department has ordered the immediate relocation of students from dilapidated and dangerous school buildings and their unsafe sections to safer locations. In a letter issued to all District Education Officers (DEOs), the department directed that students studying in unsafe buildings be shifted immediately to secure classrooms.

According to the instructions, students should be accommodated in safe sections of the same school or nearby government schools. In case government school facilities are unavailable, rented buildings may be arranged to ensure the continuation of their education.

The department clarified that only unsafe portions and rooms of buildings declared dangerous would be vacated and sealed, rather than requiring the evacuation of entire buildings.

The letter stated that dangerous school buildings and their unsafe sections had been identified by the Communication and Works Department and technical experts.

All District Education Officers have been directed to take immediate measures to ensure students’ safety and make alternative arrangements to prevent any disruption to their education.

headline: PMDC clears 99pc of over 304,000 registration applications
description: ISLAMABAD - The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has issued 302,587 registrations and related services against 304,819 applications
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has issued 302,587 registrations and related services against 304,819 applications received, clearing nearly 99 per cent of the total caseload, according to the council’s registration portal statistics up to October 2026.

The figures reflect improvements in the council’s registration system, which has focused on expediting application processing, clearing pending cases and facilitating doctors and dental professionals through its online portal.

According to a press release issued on Sunday, the council has strengthened workflow management, introduced closer monitoring of applications and improved administrative coordination to ensure timely processing and responses to applicants.

The initiative has also reduced the need for medical and dental professionals to visit PMDC offices in person, enabling them to complete registration-related formalities remotely. The online system has helped save applicants’ time and travel expenses while minimising inconvenience, particularly for doctors serving in remote areas, hospitals and demanding professional settings, the statement said.

The council has processed applications across several categories, including full and provisional licences, licence renewals, Good Standing Certificates, postgraduate qualifications, faculty registrations and experience verification.

The portal statistics show that the PMDC issued 90,683 renewals of full licences against 90,837 applications received. It also issued 54,044 full licences out of 54,620 applications, while 51,702 provisional licences were issued against 51,736 applications.

Similarly, the council issued 40,619 Good Standing Certificates against 40,630 applications and processed 17,158 postgraduate qualification registration applications out of 17,203 received. It also issued 11,065 faculty registrations against 11,308 applications.

Furthermore, 7,343 applications from Pakistani nationals seeking foreign basic provisional licences were issued out of 7,347 received.

The PMDC president said the figures demonstrated the scale of work undertaken by the council, particularly in high-volume registration categories. He stressed the importance of institutional efficiency, transparency, accountability and timely facilitation of medical and dental professionals.

He said the council was continuing to modernise its operational systems, strengthen administrative oversight and address pending applications in accordance with applicable rules and regulatory requirements, while maintaining the standards expected of the country’s national medical and dental regulatory body.

The council has also prioritised the early identification of deficiencies and objections in applications, enabling applicants to address outstanding requirements and avoid unnecessary delays. Timely scrutiny and follow-up, the statement added, were helping improve processing times and make the registration system more transparent and applicant-friendly.

headline: Free hepatitis C programme offers hope to millions
description: ISLAMABAD - The Prime Minister’s National Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C is offering free screening, diagnostic tests and treatment
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Prime Minister’s National Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C is offering free screening, diagnostic tests and treatment to millions of Pakistanis who might otherwise be unable to afford care for the potentially life-threatening disease.

For low-income families, the cost of diagnosis and treatment can be a major obstacle, often forcing patients to delay medical attention until the infection has caused serious liver damage. The government’s initiative seeks to remove this financial barrier and improve access to treatment for a disease that is curable in most cases.

An estimated 60 million people worldwide, including around 11 million in Pakistan, are affected by hepatitis C. Transmitted primarily through infected blood, contaminated syringes and improperly sterilised or shared instruments, the infection can remain undetected for years before leading to complications such as cirrhosis and liver cancer.

Under the programme, patients are being provided free PCR tests, which can otherwise cost around Rs8,000, while treatment worth an estimated Rs34,000 to Rs68,000 is also available without charge. The initiative combines screening and early diagnosis with treatment, public awareness and follow-up to ensure that patients receive appropriate care. Initially launched in Islamabad, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, the programme is envisaged to expand nationwide.

An official of the Ministry of National Health Services said the initiative was intended to ensure that financial constraints did not deprive anyone of essential healthcare.

“The programme is based on the principle that every citizen deserves access to screening and treatment, irrespective of their financial circumstances. No person should lose their life simply because they cannot afford a diagnostic test or medicines,” the official said.

The District Health Office (DHO) Islamabad is also supporting the initiative through screening facilities, awareness activities and coordination with public-sector institutions. Officials said screening was being carried out at designated healthcare facilities and special camps to reach people who might otherwise not seek testing.

On the directions of Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal, the DHO has also extended screening services to parliamentarians and staff of the National Assembly Secretariat. Seventeen screening points have been established in Islamabad, while efforts are under way to broaden coverage. A DHO official said the aim was to identify infections before they progressed and connect patients with treatment services.

“Early diagnosis is the most effective way to prevent the complications associated with hepatitis C. Our objective is to reach people before the disease progresses and ensure that those testing positive are connected with treatment facilities,” the official said.

Medical experts say the programme could significantly reduce the country’s disease burden if screening is sustained and accompanied by public awareness and effective infection-control measures. Dr Maqsood Malik, a senior liver specialist, said hepatitis C was curable in most cases if patients were diagnosed and completed the prescribed course of treatment.

“Modern antiviral medicines can cure the majority of hepatitis C patients, usually through a relatively short treatment course,” he said, adding that early identification remained essential to preventing advanced liver disease.

Dr Tauqeer Ahad, a physician associated with public healthcare services, said free screening and treatment could remove a major obstacle for people from low-income households.

Dr Naila Shamim stressed that treatment alone would not eliminate the disease without preventive measures and greater public awareness. She urged people to avoid sharing needles and razors, ensure that medical instruments were properly sterilised and seek screening after potential exposure.

The programme’s extension to Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir is particularly important for residents of remote mountainous communities, who often face geographical and financial barriers to specialised healthcare. Its proposed nationwide expansion could help reduce disparities in access to screening and treatment.

headline: Compensation for school jeep accident victims sought
description: Shangla - Political and social circles, civil society representatives and prominent figures in Shangla have called for a special financial package
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - Political and social circles, civil society representatives and prominent figures in Shangla have called for a special financial package for the family of a student killed and 17 others injured in a school jeep accident in Shalmanu Peerabad, urging Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi to ensure immediate financial assistance and free medical treatment for the victims.

The demand follows an accident in which a jeep carrying schoolchildren home after classes plunged into a deep ravine in the Shalmanu Peerabad area. One student died at the scene, while 17 others sustained injuries, some of them serious. The injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for treatment.

The incident has triggered widespread grief across the district, with political and social representatives expressing sorrow over the loss of life and concern for the injured children and their families.

Talking to The Nation, representatives of various political and social organisations said the government had a responsibility to support the affected families and ensure that they did not face additional financial hardship in the aftermath of the tragedy.

They demanded that the bereaved family be granted appropriate financial compensation and that the government bear all medical expenses of the 17 injured students.

Drawing a parallel with the financial assistance provided to victims of the Puran Aloch tragedy, which occurred during an anti-encroachment operation in Puran tehsil of Shangla, they called for a similar relief package for the families affected by the school jeep accident. They said equal treatment was essential to ensure that the victims received timely assistance and could meet their immediate needs.

The representatives also appealed to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and Deputy Commissioner Shangla to intervene and coordinate immediate relief efforts. They urged the governor, as the constitutional head of the province, to direct the relevant departments and district administration to extend financial and medical assistance to the affected families.

They further called for quality medical care for the injured students and said arrangements should be made to transfer those requiring specialised treatment to major healthcare facilities, including Saidu Teaching Hospital in Swat and Ayub Teaching Hospital in Abbottabad. All expenses, they stressed, should be borne by the government to spare the families an additional financial burden.

The representatives also called for a transparent and swift compensation mechanism, saying the affected families should not be subjected to lengthy bureaucratic procedures to obtain assistance.

Emphasising the need for preventive measures, they urged the authorities to improve roads in remote mountainous areas, ensure the roadworthiness of vehicles transporting schoolchildren and strictly enforce traffic regulations to prevent similar tragedies.

They expressed hope that the governor and district administration would respond promptly to their appeal and ensure financial assistance for the bereaved family and free medical treatment for all 17 injured students.

headline: Section 144 imposed in Bannu for anti-polio drive
description: PESHAWAR - The authorities on Sunday imposed Section 144 across Bannu district from November 1 to 7 in view of security concerns during the anti-polio
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR - The authorities on Sunday imposed Section 144 across Bannu district from November 1 to 7 in view of security concerns during the anti-polio vaccination campaign.

Under an order issued by Deputy Commissioner Bannu Zia-ur-Rehman, display of weapons, pillion riding on motorcycles and the use of tinted vehicle windows have been banned throughout the district.

According to the notification, District Police Officer Shafiullah Gandapur had informed the administration about security concerns ahead of the November anti-polio campaign, scheduled to run from November 2 to 5. The decision was taken in view of previous terrorist attacks targeting polio teams and police personnel deployed for their security.

However, patwaris and union council secretaries performing official polio campaign duties have been exempted from the restriction on carrying weapons.

Violators of the restrictions will face legal action under Section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

Meanwhile, the anti-polio campaign has formally been launched in Bannu, with Deputy Commissioner Zia-ur-Rehman and DPO Shafiullah Gandapur administering polio drops to children at the inauguration ceremony.

The campaign aims at vaccinating 228,000 children under the age of five across 57 union councils of the district.

A total of 1,412 polio teams, 321 area in-charges and 57 Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) have been deployed to ensure the campaign’s success.

The deputy commissioner urged parents to ensure that all children under five receive polio drops and called on the public to cooperate with vaccination teams.

He said ensuring vaccination coverage for every child was essential in view of the presence of polio cases and the virus in the district.

headline: Robbery suspect shoots policeman, escapes
description: PESHAWAR - A robbery suspect escaped after opening fire on a police constable in the Sherwan police station area of Abbottabad district on Sunday,
author: APP
article_text:
PESHAWAR - A robbery suspect escaped after opening fire on a police constable in the Sherwan police station area of Abbottabad district on Sunday, leaving the officer injured, police said.

The incident occurred in Chamati area when a police constable attempted to stop the suspect, identified as Saleem, son of Siddique, a resident of Kanger Payeen. The suspect allegedly opened fire, hitting Constable Ubaid in the abdomen.

The injured policeman was immediately shifted to hospital for medical treatment.

Police said Saleem was wanted in connection with robbery case No. 239, registered under Section 395 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) on the complaint of Jafar Hussain Shah.

According to the first information report (FIR), the suspects had looted gold jewellery, Rs300,000 in cash and a mobile phone from the complainant’s house.

Police have launched a search operation to arrest the fleeing suspect.

headline: Rescue 1122 handles 787 emergencies in DI Khan in Oct
description: DERA ISMAIL KHAN - Rescue 1122 responded to 787 emergencies in Dera Ismail Khan during October, providing rescue and medical assistance to people in distress,
author: APP
article_text:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN - Rescue 1122 responded to 787 emergencies in Dera Ismail Khan during October, providing rescue and medical assistance to people in distress, while also transferring 72 patients to healthcare facilities for further treatment.

According to the monthly performance report released by Rescue 1122, medical emergencies accounted for the largest share of operations, with 607 cases attended during the month. Rescue teams also responded to 141 road traffic accidents, 18 incidents involving bullet injuries, 13 recovery operations, six fires and two drowning incidents.

In addition to emergency response operations, the service facilitated 72 patient transfers. Of these, 59 patients were shifted to healthcare facilities within the district, while 13 were referred to hospitals in other districts for specialised treatment.

The operations were conducted under the directives of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Rescue 1122 Director General Dr Khateer Ahmad.

Commenting on the performance, Muhammad Arif Khan appreciated the commitment and professionalism of rescue personnel, saying their prompt response played a vital role in providing timely assistance to people facing emergencies.

He said the protection of human lives and property remained the department’s foremost priority and that all available resources and professional capabilities were being utilised to ensure an effective emergency response.

He reaffirmed that Rescue 1122 Dera Ismail Khan would continue providing emergency services with dedication and professionalism.

headline: ‘Reliable data and political will vital for effective water governance’
description: ISLAMABAD - Effective water governance in Pakistan requires reliable data, a sound legal framework, capable institutions and professional expertise, backed by
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Effective water governance in Pakistan requires reliable data, a sound legal framework, capable institutions and professional expertise, backed by strong political commitment to ensure that policies are translated into action, a water governance expert has said.

In an interview with APP, Dr Muhammad Ashraf, Country Representative of the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) in Pakistan, stressed the need to strengthen institutional capacity, improve water resource assessments and introduce systematic water accounting and auditing to ensure the sustainable and equitable use of the country’s water resources.

He said even well-designed policies, laws and institutions could not deliver results without the political will and commitment needed to implement them.

Referring to the National Water Policy 2018, Dr Ashraf said it provided a comprehensive framework comprising 33 objectives and outlined key principles, including the installation of water meters to discourage wastage and the application of the ‘polluter pays’ principle.

However, he said policy provisions alone were insufficient without clear legal responsibilities, designated institutions, practical implementation mechanisms and adequate enforcement capacity. Explaining the division of responsibilities following the 18th Constitutional Amendment, he said the federal government primarily dealt with major hydropower projects, transboundary water matters and the distribution of water among provinces under the 1991 Water Apportionment Accord.

The provinces, he added, were responsible for managing water resources within their respective jurisdictions, including groundwater, floodwater, hill torrents and wastewater. Dr Ashraf said wastewater should not be treated merely as a source of pollution but also recognised as a resource that could be treated and reused for industrial, agricultural and other purposes.

He clarified that the Indus River System Authority (IRSA) was responsible for distributing water among the four provinces in accordance with the 1991 accord and its prescribed formula, taking variations in water availability into account. IRSA did not formulate water policy but implemented the agreed water-sharing arrangements, he added.

Emphasising the importance of evidence-based decision-making, Dr Ashraf said Pakistan needed a comprehensive and consistent system to assess and account for its water resources.

He said reliable assessments were required of water originating from glaciers, rainfall, groundwater, wastewater and hill torrents before decisions could be made about infrastructure development and resource allocation.

Water accounting, he explained, involved systematically recording water inflows, consumption and outflows, enabling authorities to identify losses, inefficiencies and discrepancies through audits.

He said IWMI had consulted federal and provincial stakeholders to develop guidelines for water resource assessment and accounting. The initiative also involved developing and testing water-budgeting tools to help identify losses, excessive consumption and shortages.

Dr Ashraf said water budgeting could help authorities and farmers determine whether crops were receiving adequate supplies, identify inefficient irrigation practices and reduce the risk of crop failure and other long-term consequences of poor water management.

He also referred to work on drought contingency planning and the transfer of a related tool to the Pakistan Meteorological Department, emphasising the need for preparedness and timely action in response to climate-related water challenges. He said coordinated efforts by federal and provincial governments, relevant institutions and other stakeholders were essential to improving water governance, strengthening accountability and ensuring the sustainable management of the country’s water resources.

headline: Tank administration clears encroachments along DI Khan Road
description: Tank - The district administration of Tank has intensified its anti-encroachment campaign, removing illegal structures and obstructions from
author: APP
article_text:
Tank - The district administration of Tank has intensified its anti-encroachment campaign, removing illegal structures and obstructions from commercial areas and along the Tank-Dera Ismail Khan Road to ease traffic congestion and improve access for pedestrians.

On the directives of Deputy Commissioner Jamshed Khan, Additional Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Irfan Khan led an operation at Dera Road Bazaar, where platforms built in front of shops, extended sheds, temporary shelters and other structures occupying public spaces and pedestrian pathways were removed.

The administration said the operation was aimed at restoring the designated road limits and ensuring the unobstructed movement of vehicles and pedestrians.

In a separate operation, the district administration, in collaboration with the anti-encroachment staff of the Tehsil Municipal Administration (TMA), cleared permanent encroachments along both sides of the Tank-DI Khan Road, particularly between Wapda Colony and the DI Khan Bus Stand.

Assistant Commissioner Tank Malik Sajid Ali Khan supervised the operation and directed the relevant staff to remove illegal structures and clear public passageways.

Speaking on the occasion, Additional Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Irfan Khan warned shopkeepers and traders against occupying public spaces, saying that encroachments on roads, footpaths and other public passageways would not be tolerated.

He said the campaign would continue without discrimination and warned that those who rebuilt illegal structures after their removal would face legal action, including heavy fines.

The district administration also urged traders to confine their commercial activities to their legally designated premises and refrain from placing goods or extending shop structures onto public roads and pedestrian walkways.

Officials said encroachments caused traffic congestion, inconvenienced commuters and residents, and could obstruct the movement of emergency services.

The administration called on the business community to cooperate with its staff and the TMA in keeping commercial areas orderly and ensuring smooth traffic flow, adding that enforcement would continue against all forms of illegal occupation of public spaces.

headline: ICT Police nab 175 suspects, conduct 48 search operations in one week
description: ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Police have nabbed 175 suspects, including drug dealers, illegal arms holders and proclaimed
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Police have nabbed 175 suspects, including drug dealers, illegal arms holders and proclaimed offenders, during a week-long crackdown across the federal capital, besides conducting 48 search operations to ensure public safety.

According to an ICT Police official, the operations were carried out on the special directives of Inspector General of Police (IGP) Islamabad Capt (retd) Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry as part of ongoing efforts to curb crime and protect citizens.

Police apprehended 42 suspected drug dealers and recovered 8,566 grams of ice, 5,698 grams of hashish, 4,812 grams of heroin and 1,387 bottles of liquor from their possession. The official said 43 suspects were taken into custody for possessing illegal weapons and displaying firearms. Police recovered 37 pistols of different calibres, six daggers and a large quantity of ammunition.

He said police also apprehended 90 proclaimed offenders, habitual criminals and court absconders during the week. Meanwhile, ICT Police conducted 48 major combing and search operations in different areas of Islamabad to trace criminal elements and strengthen security.

During these operations, police checked 2,257 individuals, 987 households, 92 hotels and 281 shops.

The official said 1,352 motorcycles and 490 vehicles were also checked as part of the security measures.

Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Islamabad Ali Waseem said Islamabad Police were utilising all available resources to protect the lives and property of citizens.

He said action against criminal elements would continue to maintain law and order in the federal capital.

headline: ITP offer students motorcycle licences without 42-day learner waiting period
description: ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP) have introduced a special facility for college and university students, allowing them to obtain motorcycle driving
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Islamabad Traffic Police (ITP) have introduced a special facility for college and university students, allowing them to obtain motorcycle driving licences without completing the mandatory 42-day learner waiting period from November 1 to 30, 2026.

According to an ITP official, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Islamabad Kainat Azhar Khan said the initiative was aimed at making the driving licence process easier and more convenient for students across the federal capital.

She said eligible college and university students could avail themselves of the relaxation in the 42-day learner period and obtain their motorcycle driving licences on the spot after completing the required formalities. The CTO, Kianat, also informed citizens that they could now receive their driving licences at their doorsteps through TCS courier service instead of making repeated visits to traffic police offices.

She said the home delivery facility would save citizens time and make the licensing process more convenient.

Kainat urged students to take advantage of the special facility during November and encouraged citizens to obtain valid driving licences before riding motorcycles or driving vehicles.

headline: Fire at E-11 marquee brought under control after overnight operation
description: ISLAMABAD - A fire that broke out at a marquee in Sector E-11 of Islamabad late Saturday night was brought under control after an emergency
author: The Nation
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A fire that broke out at a marquee in Sector E-11 of Islamabad late Saturday night was brought under control after an emergency firefighting operation by the Capital Emergency Services, while cooling operations continued at the site in the early hours of Sunday.

Firefighting units rushed to the scene shortly after the incident was reported and launched an operation to extinguish the blaze using trained personnel and specialised equipment.

The fire was completely extinguished by around 2am, according to the Capital Development Authority (CDA), but rescue teams remained at the site to carry out cooling operations and prevent the possibility of the fire reigniting.

Firefighters were also inspecting the affected area to ensure that residual heat had been eliminated and the site was safe.

The Islamabad Capital Territory administration, CDA and Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad (MCI) coordinated their efforts during the emergency response.

CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf said all available resources were being utilised to ensure public safety and prevent any further incident.

There was no immediate official information about the cause of the fire, the extent of damage or any casualties.

headline: Bettani elders, admin agree on joint efforts for lasting peace
description: Llakki marwat - The district administration and Bettani tribal elders have agreed to strengthen mutual cooperation to promote lasting peace and
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Llakki marwat - The district administration and Bettani tribal elders have agreed to strengthen mutual cooperation to promote lasting peace and accelerate development in the region.

The understanding was reached at a meeting held at the Deputy Commissioner’s Jirga Hall here on Sunday, attended by Deputy Commissioner Shahid Rafiq Gandapur, ARDC member Qari Muhammad Umar and tribal elders.

During the meeting, the elders apprised the administration of the problems confronting local tribespeople in various sectors. They also discussed the prevailing law and order situation and the pace of development in the region.

The elders put forward proposals to improve public service delivery and strengthen coordination between government officials and tribal representatives to ensure the timely resolution of people’s grievances.

Responding to their concerns, Deputy Commissioner Shahid Rafiq Gandapur assured the participants that the administration would prioritise the provision of basic amenities and improve the delivery of public services at people’s doorsteps.

He said concerted efforts and close cooperation among all stakeholders were essential to achieving peace, development and prosperity in the Bettani region. The government, he added, was taking concrete measures to uplift the area and bring it at par with other developed parts of the country. The deputy commissioner assured the elders that the issues raised at the meeting would be taken up with the relevant departments for their resolution. He also underscored the importance of continued cooperation between the administration and tribal elders in promoting peace, development and public welfare.

description: LAKKI MARWAT - Deputy Commissioner Shahid Rafique Gandapur has imposed a four-day ban on the display and carrying of weapons and several other
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAKKI MARWAT - Deputy Commissioner Shahid Rafique Gandapur has imposed a four-day ban on the display and carrying of weapons and several other activities across Lakki Marwat district ahead of the anti-polio campaign scheduled to begin on November 2, an official of the district administration said on Sunday.

The official said the restrictions had been imposed in response to a letter from the district police officer (DPO), who had expressed apprehensions that miscreants and anti-social elements might attempt to disrupt law and order during the vaccination campaign. The restrictions also include a ban on pillion riding, the use of unregistered motorcycles and vehicles, vehicles with tinted windows, and gatherings of five or more people at public places. The measures were necessary to prevent any untoward incident and maintain peace and public order during the polio eradication campaign, the official said.

Issued under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), the order will remain in force from November 2 to 5.

Violators will be liable to prosecution under Section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), he added.

headline: WHO supports special polio campaign
description: Peshawar - The World Health Organization (WHO) is supporting a special polio vaccination campaign in high-risk areas of Peshawar and Khyber
author: APP
article_text:
Peshawar - The World Health Organization (WHO) is supporting a special polio vaccination campaign in high-risk areas of Peshawar and Khyber districts to protect more than 900,000 children up to 10 years of age against the crippling disease.

Under the campaign, polio drops and a booster dose of the injectable polio vaccine are being administered in 78 high-risk union councils across the two districts.

WHO teams are supporting the vaccination drive to strengthen immunity among children and prevent the transmission of poliovirus in areas vulnerable to the disease. The initiative is part of ongoing efforts to reach every eligible child with life-saving vaccines and accelerate Pakistan’s progress towards polio eradication.

headline: Raag Bhairavicompositions enthral audiences
description: MULTAN - The Multan Arts Council hosted a musical evening titled “Sur Mala Ke Roop Hazar” (A Thousand Shades of Melody) on Saturday,
author: APP
article_text:
MULTAN - The Multan Arts Council hosted a musical evening titled “Sur Mala Ke Roop Hazar” (A Thousand Shades of Melody) on Saturday, featuring performances based on Raag Bhairavi and celebrating the traditions of classical and semi-classical music. The programme brought together male and female vocalists, who entertained the audience with their renditions and interpretations of the traditional compositions.

Among the performers, Sobia Malik, Shamim Ansari, Zaheer Abbas and Zubair Bhapla received appreciation for their vocal performances, which highlighted the expressive range and enduring appeal of Raag Bhairavi.

The evening’s main attraction was renowned vocalist Ustad Nadeem Riaz, who travelled from Lahore to participate in the event. His performance, marked by vocal command and musical expertise, drew warm applause from the audience.

The Piracha Sisters, Shahid Qureshi, Asad Abbas and several other singers also performed. Director Multan Arts Council Saleem Qaisar conducted the proceedings and coordinated the sequence of performances.

The programme highlighted the role of cultural institutions in encouraging artistic expression and preserving traditional musical forms for future generations.

headline: IHC resumes hearing on 50 missing Pakistanis abroad
description: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) will resume hearing on Monday (today) a petition seeking the tracing and safe return of 50 Pakistani
author: Shahid Rao
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) will resume hearing on Monday (today) a petition seeking the tracing and safe return of 50 Pakistani citizens, reportedly missing abroad after travelling through irregular channels in search of employment.

A single-member bench, headed by Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir, will take up the petition filed by Afzaal Hussain Shah through his counsel, Advocate Shafqat Abbas Tarar. The court had previously issued notices to the federal government, seeking its response to the plea.

At the last hearing, the court directed the Assistant Attorney General to submit a report on the matter before the next hearing and adjourned proceedings until November 2.

Through the petition, the petitioner has sought directions to the relevant authorities to trace, identify and verify the whereabouts of the missing citizens, provide them with consular assistance and facilitate their safe return. He has also sought protection for those who may be stranded or otherwise vulnerable abroad, along with time-bound progress reports to their families.

During the previous hearing, the petitioner’s counsel informed the court that more than 50 young men from Mandi Bahauddin, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad and adjoining areas had travelled in separate boats from Mauritania towards Spain between April 2024 and January 2025.

However, they failed to reach their intended destination, leaving their families without reliable information about their whereabouts or immigration status in any country, the counsel submitted.

The court was also informed that the petitioner had approached the prime minister, foreign minister and interior minister through written applications, seeking their intervention in the matter.

The counsel requested the court to direct the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to initiate consular inquiries in the countries concerned and coordinate with Pakistani embassies and consulates to trace the missing citizens.

He also sought directions for the examination of available immigration, travel and other relevant records to establish the whereabouts of the missing Pakistanis and facilitate their safe repatriation. The petition further calls for efforts to determine whether any of the missing citizens are stranded at unidentified locations, have been deported or are being held under any other circumstances abroad.

headline: Shabqadar Fort’s chained gates guard a 186-year-old tale
description: CHARSADDA - For 10-year-old Anaya Khan, history came alive when she stood before the massive wooden gates of Shabqadar Fort on Sunday, fulfilling a
author: APP
article_text:
CHARSADDA - For 10-year-old Anaya Khan, history came alive when she stood before the massive wooden gates of Shabqadar Fort on Sunday, fulfilling a long-held wish after completing her mid-term examinations.

Holding her grandfather’s hand, she gazed at the heavy chains wrapped around the gates, which, according to historical accounts, have remained shackled since 1840.

“I had always imagined visiting this historic fort after reading in history books and newspapers that its main gates had been chained since 1840. Seeing them with my own eyes feels like stepping into another time,” she said.

Built in 1837 under Maharaja Ranjit Singh by Sikh architect Tota Ram, Shabqadar Fort stands on the outskirts of Charsadda and is among Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s notable historical landmarks. Its strategic position between the Peshawar and Kabul valleys made it an important military outpost during the Sikh Empire and later under British rule. However, it is the unusual story of its chained gates that has made the fort particularly intriguing to visitors.

“The gates have remained in chains for nearly 186 years,” said Bakhtzada Khan, Assistant Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, while explaining the fort’s history to APP.

According to historical accounts, a fierce assault by a Mohmand tribal lashkar in 1840 exposed weaknesses in the fort’s defences. Although Sikh forces eventually repelled the attackers, the wooden gates failed to prevent the breach.

Following an inquiry, Prince Sher Singh, son of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, reportedly ordered the gates to face a symbolic court-martial for dereliction of duty. The proceedings were conducted by Generals Maan Singh and Jean-Baptiste Ventura, after which the massive willow gates were chained and sentenced to 100 years in captivity.

Their sentence expired in 1940, but the chains were never removed, Bakhtzada Khan said, describing the unusual tradition as a reminder of the fort’s military past.

Another attraction inside the fort is a room traditionally associated with former British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, who is believed to have stayed there in 1897 while working as a war correspondent covering the tribal uprising in the region.

The room retains a bed associated with his stay, old wooden chairs, a manual fan and black-and-white photographs. A small museum nearby displays historical weapons and military relics, including vintage rifles, binoculars, mortar shells and tribal weapons.

The fort has witnessed successive political and military eras, from the Sikh Empire to British colonial rule and the establishment of Pakistan. Several prominent military figures, including Generals Ventura and Allard, were associated with the region, while Italian General Paolo Avitabile played a significant role in the Sikh administration of Peshawar.

After independence, the fort continued to receive prominent visitors, including President Iskandar Mirza in 1957 and former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in 1970.

Currently under the control of the Federal Constabulary and used for training purposes, the fort has also attracted calls for regulated public access to promote heritage tourism. Similar proposals have been made for other historic sites, including Bala Hisar, Jamrud and Alexandra forts.

headline: Arab League calls for international probe into torture of Gaza detainees in Israeli prison
description: The Arab League called Sunday for an independent international investigation into the torture and systematic abuse of Palestinians from Gaza held in
author: Anadolu
article_text:
The Arab League called Sunday for an independent international investigation into the torture and systematic abuse of Palestinians from Gaza held in Israel’s Ramla Prison, demanding accountability for those responsible.

In a statement, the league condemned the repeated assaults of prisoners in the facility’s Rakevet wing, saying they had left detainees with injuries and burns.

It described the practices as violations of international humanitarian law, including the Geneva Conventions and the Convention against Torture, and said they constituted “crimes against humanity” requiring accountability.

The league demanded an immediate end to the abuse and urged Israel to allow unrestricted access for the International Committee of the Red Cross and independent monitors to document conditions and provide medical care.

It also called for the immediate release of sick and wounded prisoners and an end to arbitrary detention.

The statement followed an Oct. 27 report by the Palestinian Prisoners’ Media Office detailing recurring assaults against Gaza detainees in the Rakevet wing.

The office said the assaults took place on Fridays and Saturdays and involved beatings with batons, pepper spray, gas, rubber bullets and stun grenades.

It also reported that guards entered a cell with police dogs and took detainees to a room without surveillance cameras, where they were assaulted.

The office warned that continued abuse endangered prisoners’ lives, particularly those already ill or injured.

The Arab League urged the international community, the UN Human Rights Council and the UN General Assembly to act to protect Palestinian prisoners and end impunity.

There was no immediate Israeli response to the statement.

Ramla Prison is in central Israel and is administered by the Israel Prison Service.

headline: Bulgaria’s Yotova wins presidential runoff with clear lead in exit polls
description: Bulgaria’s acting President Iliana Yotova was heading for a decisive victory in Sunday’s presidential runoff against her pro-Western challenger,
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Bulgaria’s acting President Iliana Yotova was heading for a decisive victory in Sunday’s presidential runoff against her pro-Western challenger, according to exit polls.

Completed parallel counts by five major polling agencies put Yotova’s share of the vote at between 56.6% and 58.2%, compared with 38.6% to 40.6% for Andrey Gyurov.

“We accept the results, no matter how surprising they are,” Gyurov told a press conference in Sofia, adding that while the campaign is ending, the responsibility is not.

Yotova, a longtime figure within the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), improved on her first-round result from last weekend, when she finished with 34.76% against Gyurov at 31.95%. Her campaign emphasized no additional arms support for Ukraine and instead called for peace through a diplomatic solution, in contrast to her rival.

The election follows April’s parliamentary vote in which Progressive Bulgaria, led by former President Rumen Radev, won 131 of the National Assembly’s 240 seats and an outright majority.

Yotova, who previously served as Radev’s vice president, assumed the acting presidency after he resigned in January. Progressive Bulgaria has backed her bid for a full five-year mandate.

Gyurov, a former deputy governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, had warned during the campaign that a Yotova victory would leave no real counterweight at the top of the state, since Progressive Bulgaria already controls the government.

On the European Union and security policy, he criticized the government’s hesitation, reduced support for Ukraine, and slow coordination with NATO and EU partners, arguing that the approach has left Bulgaria more exposed and turned it into a weak link on the alliance’s eastern flank.

headline: Russia, Ukraine report cyberattacks on emergency alert apps
description: Russia and Ukraine reported cyber incidents affecting their emergency alert mobile applications early Monday, with false warnings sent to users in both
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Russia and Ukraine reported cyber incidents affecting their emergency alert mobile applications early Monday, with false warnings sent to users in both countries.

The Ukrainian Air Force said the country's Air Alert application had likely been subjected to "hostile interference" after false warnings appeared on the app.

"There is no radiation threat," it said on Telegram, urging residents to remain calm and follow official updates.

Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications later blamed Russia for the incident, saying users had received "strange messages," including a Russian-language message referring to the Oreshnik missile.

Hours later, Russia's Emergencies Ministry said its mobile application had been hit by a "massive cyberattack" which allowed attackers to send false information to the public.

The ministry said Russia's broader public warning system was operating normally and had not been affected by the breach.

Citizens continued to receive alerts through sirens and loudspeakers, SMS messages and television and radio broadcasts, it said, adding that the mobile application was only an additional information service.

The ministry said specialists were working to restore the app's normal operation and that the situation was "under control."

Moscow did not say who it believed was responsible for the attack.

It was not immediately clear whether the incidents affecting the Russian and Ukrainian applications were connected.

headline: Lahore tops world's most polluted cities list as AQI crosses 500
description: Lahore tops the world's most polluted cities list as AQI exceeds 500, with Allama Iqbal Town recording 912. Experts urge residents to take precautions.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Air pollution in the provincial capital has reached alarming levels, with the city's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) exceeding 500, posing serious health risks to residents.

According to the Meteorological Department, Lahore has emerged as the world's most polluted city, topping the global list of cities with the worst air quality.

Allama Iqbal Town recorded the highest pollution level in the city, with an AQI of 912, followed by Burki Road at 698, Gulberg at 619, DHA Phase 5 at 569 and Model Town at 471.

The deteriorating air quality has raised serious concerns over public health, as residents remain exposed to hazardous levels of pollution.

Health experts have advised citizens to limit unnecessary outdoor activities and wear protective masks when venturing outside.

They have also urged residents to take additional precautions to protect children, the elderly and people suffering from respiratory illnesses, who are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of air pollution.

headline: FCC says SC rulings not binding, sets strict conditions for review petitions
description: Federal Constitutional Court rules Supreme Court judgments are not binding on it, sets strict review petition conditions and dismisses Balochistan Trading
author: APP
article_text:
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that Supreme Court judgments carry persuasive value but are not binding on it, while laying down stringent conditions for filing review petitions and warning against frivolous litigation.

In its ruling, the FCC clarified that it could seek guidance from Supreme Court judgments and adopt legal precedents established by the apex court, provided they were consistent with the law and the Constitution.

The court observed that its review jurisdiction was extremely limited and could be exercised only in specific circumstances.

According to the ruling, a review petition could be entertained only where an error was apparent on the face of the record or an omission had resulted in a miscarriage of justice. It could not be used to reopen arguments or seek a fresh hearing of a case.

The FCC explained that review proceedings did not involve rehearing an entire case but were confined to examining whether an apparent error existed in the original record.

Discouraging the routine filing of review petitions, the court directed litigants and lawyers to seek a review only where genuine and legally sustainable grounds existed.

It warned that frivolous or malicious review petitions could result in costs of at least Rs25,000, while disciplinary proceedings could also be initiated against an Advocate-on-Record involved in filing such petitions.

The ruling made it mandatory for the Advocate-on-Record or the party concerned to submit a certificate specifying the grounds for seeking a review before filing a petition.

The court also required petitioners to deposit Rs50,000 as security for the hearing of a review petition, which could be forfeited if the petition was dismissed or found to be frivolous or malicious.

It further clarified that, in appropriate cases, review petitions could be decided through circulation without an oral hearing.

The FCC also outlined the procedure for challenging high court judgments delivered under Article 199 of the Constitution.

It ruled that under Article 175F(1)(c), permission from the constitutional court was required before an appeal could be filed against a high court decision issued under Article 199.

The court clarified that leave to appeal was not an appeal as a matter of right, adding that an application acquired the status of an appeal only after the court granted permission.

It further observed that the rejection of a leave-to-appeal application did not necessarily imply endorsement of the high court's judgment.

According to the ruling, the court was not required to provide detailed reasons when declining leave to appeal.

The FCC also held that a non-speaking order, or one issued without detailed reasoning, did not in itself constitute valid grounds for filing a review petition.

It explained that, at the leave-to-appeal stage, the court examined whether a legal question warranted consideration or whether intervention was necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice.

Meanwhile, the FCC dismissed a review petition filed by Balochistan Trading Company and ordered the forfeiture of the security deposited by the petitioner.

The court observed that the company had failed to identify any error apparent on the face of the record that could justify reconsideration of its earlier decision.

It noted that the review petition merely reiterated arguments already presented during the previous proceedings.

Consequently, the court rejected the company's request for the restoration of its lease and possession.

headline: South Korea takes emergency steps to keep $17.5bn Czech nuclear project on track
description: South Korea introduces emergency measures to keep its $17.5bn Dukovany nuclear project on schedule after KHNP's contract talks with a construction consortium
author: Web Desk
article_text:
South Korea on Monday announced an emergency management system to prevent delays to its $17.5 billion nuclear power plant project in the Czech Republic after contract negotiations with a domestic construction consortium broke down, Yonhap News Agency reported.

The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said the government would introduce measures to ensure the Dukovany nuclear power project remained on schedule and prevent similar contractual setbacks.

The announcement came after Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Co. (KHNP) last week terminated negotiations with a consortium comprising Daewoo Engineering & Construction and Doosan Enerbility following a failure to reach an agreement on key contractual terms.

The ministry was scheduled to hold its first emergency meeting on Monday to discuss follow-up measures and address potential disruptions to the project.

KHNP, South Korea's state-run nuclear power operator, will initiate a fresh tender process to select a construction contractor, with plans to finalise an agreement by July 2027.

Construction of the nuclear power plant is scheduled to begin in November 2027.

"The minister and vice minister will personally review key project issues every week and take necessary measures for the time being," Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said.

The project, valued at 25 trillion won ($17.5bn), involves the construction of two 1,000-megawatt APR1000 nuclear reactors at Dukovany in the Czech Republic.

A KHNP-led South Korean consortium secured the project last year and subsequently began negotiations with the Daewoo-Doosan consortium, which had been designated to undertake construction work.

headline: Drone attacks hit 2 power stations in eastern Sudan, trigger widespread outage
description: Drone attacks targeted two electricity substations in the cities of Aroma and New Halfa in Sudan’s eastern Kassala state early Monday, causing widespread
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Drone attacks targeted two electricity substations in the cities of Aroma and New Halfa in Sudan’s eastern Kassala state early Monday, causing widespread power outages across the state, local sources told Anadolu.

The attacks brought to 15 the number of electricity stations targeted by drones across Sudan over the past week, including in Khartoum, Gezira, Sennar, Red Sea, Gedaref, Kassala and River Nile states.

​​​​​​​Drones struck the New Halfa and Aroma electricity substations early Monday, witnesses said.

The two attacks caused widespread electricity outages across Kassala state, according to local sources.

Videos circulated on social media showed fires at the New Halfa and Aroma stations, while Civil Defense teams were seen trying to extinguish the blaze at the Aroma facility.

On Sunday, drones targeted the Abu Hamad electricity substation in River Nile state and the Al-Dabbah substation in Northern state.

Following the attacks, the Sudanese government said Sunday that it had filed complaints against Ethiopia with the UN Security Council and the African Union Peace and Security Council, accusing Addis Ababa of involvement in attacks on civilian infrastructure and power stations in several Sudanese states.

There was no immediate comment from Ethiopia.

Sudanese authorities and rights groups have accused the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of targeting civilian infrastructure. The paramilitary group generally does not comment on such accusations and says it works to protect civilians.​​​​​​​

The Sudanese army and RSF have been fighting since April 2023 in a conflict triggered by disagreements over the integration of the paramilitary group, leaving tens of thousands dead and displacing around 13 million people amid a worsening humanitarian and hunger crisis.

headline: KP governor urges stronger economic ties with China, invites investment
description: KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi urges stronger economic cooperation with China, highlighting investment opportunities in hydropower, mining, agriculture and
author: APP
article_text:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has called for transforming Pakistan's longstanding friendship with China into a stronger economic partnership, highlighting investment opportunities in the province's hydropower, minerals, agriculture, tourism and industrial sectors.

Addressing the inauguration ceremony of the Pakistan-China Research Centre for Party and State Governance, Kundi said bilateral relations were rooted in mutual trust, respect and shared interests.

He appreciated the role of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) in strengthening political and people-to-people ties between the two countries.

Welcoming the establishment of the research centre, the governor expressed confidence that it would provide an important platform for research, policy dialogue and institutional cooperation.

Kundi said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had the potential to generate more than 30,000 megawatts of hydropower, besides possessing abundant mineral resources, agricultural potential and significant tourism opportunities.

He said these resources made the province an attractive destination for Chinese investors seeking opportunities in various sectors.

The governor also highlighted the province's Gandhara heritage and historical sites, including Takht Bhai, saying they offered considerable potential for promoting religious and cultural tourism.

Referring to the province's demographic strength, Kundi said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had a population of more than 40.8 million, including over 10 million young people, whom he described as its greatest asset.

He said Chinese expertise and technology could help create opportunities for technical training, employment and industrial development, particularly for the province's youth.

Inviting Chinese investors to explore opportunities in hydropower, mining, manufacturing, tourism and agriculture, the governor assured them of all possible facilities and support.

"Our vision is a progressive, prosperous and stronger Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It is time to take Pakistan-China friendship into a new era of shared economic growth and development," he said.
