headline: Khawaja Asif accuses TikToker of evading law after deadly Daska stampede
description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif accuses TikToker Patlu of evading legal action after a Daska wedding stampede killed two people and injured dozens.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has accused a TikToker known as Patlu of using his influence to evade legal action following a stampede at a wedding event in Daska that left two people dead and dozens injured.

In a post on social media platform X, the defence minister condemned the incident, saying it could not be denounced strongly enough.

Asif said the TikToker had attracted a large crowd to his wedding ceremony by announcing expensive prizes, including substantial cash rewards.

He alleged that the event had been staged to generate income through social media, with the prizes serving as an investment aimed at securing higher earnings from online engagement.

The minister said the event had made a mockery of the poverty of underprivileged residents, while the large gathering resulted in a stampede that claimed two lives and left dozens injured.

Asif further alleged that the TikToker was absconding and using his influence to obstruct the enforcement of the law.

Expressing concern over the growing influence of social media, the defence minister warned that unregulated online activities could have serious consequences for society and the state.

He stressed the need to hold those responsible accountable and called for greater scrutiny of the activities of social media personalities.

Asif also questioned whether existing tax laws adequately covered social media influencers who, according to him, were earning billions of rupees through online platforms.

He called for an examination of their income and accountability mechanisms, raising concerns over the regulation and taxation of earnings generated through social media.

headline: Attaullah Tarar orders revival of PTV Drama and Film Academy
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution aimed at equipping young people with professional skills in filmmaking, drama production and digital content creation.

He issued the directives while chairing a high-level meeting to review plans for the revival of the academy and revamping of PTV Home through specialised training programmes, modern technical facilities and industry-oriented learning models.

Federal Secretary for Information Ashfaq Ahmed Khalil and senior officials of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting attended the meeting.

The meeting reviewed various training models proposed in collaboration with the private sector, focusing on providing hands-on professional training to young people while creating new revenue opportunities for Pakistan Television.

Tarar said the revival of the academy and revamping of PTV Home were part of the government's commitment to promoting the country's media and creative industries.

He said Pakistan was introducing an advanced training programme in colour grading for the first time, noting that professionals previously had to travel abroad to acquire specialised training and access modern facilities in the field.

He added that locally available advanced colour-grading facilities would provide the film industry and private sector with access to modern technical resources, helping improve the quality of Pakistani filmmaking.

The minister directed officials to launch a transparent and practical pilot project in partnership with the private sector to ensure that training programmes remained aligned with evolving industry requirements.

He said equipping young people with practical skills in filmmaking, drama production, editing, colour grading and digital content creation was among the government's key priorities.

The meeting also reviewed proposals for establishing modern classrooms and studio laboratories, installing student workstations, appointing technical staff and trainers, and developing a comprehensive curriculum.

Tarar said students would receive training in a professional environment equipped with modern editing suites, studio laboratories and technical equipment.

He emphasised that the programmes would go beyond theoretical learning by incorporating practical assignments, project development and portfolio building to enhance participants' professional capabilities.

The minister further said young people's creative projects would be encouraged for PTV News, PTV Home and other Pakistan Television platforms, providing emerging talent with opportunities to showcase their work.

He said the initiatives would help strengthen the country's film and drama industry by developing a skilled workforce, introducing advanced technical expertise and making modern production facilities available locally.

He added that efforts would also be made to ensure the financial sustainability of the PTV Academy as it transformed into an effective professional training centre.

Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution aimed at equipping young people with professional skills in filmmaking, drama production and digital content creation.

He issued the directives while chairing a high-level meeting to review plans for the revival of the academy and revamping of PTV Home through specialised training programmes, modern technical facilities and industry-oriented learning models.

Federal Secretary for Information Ashfaq Ahmed Khalil and senior officials of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting attended the meeting.

The meeting reviewed various training models proposed in collaboration with the private sector, focusing on providing hands-on professional training to young people while creating new revenue opportunities for Pakistan Television.

Tarar said the revival of the academy and revamping of PTV Home were part of the government's commitment to promoting the country's media and creative industries.

He said Pakistan was introducing an advanced training programme in colour grading for the first time, noting that professionals previously had to travel abroad to acquire specialised training and access modern facilities in the field.

He added that locally available advanced colour-grading facilities would provide the film industry and private sector with access to modern technical resources, helping improve the quality of Pakistani filmmaking.

The minister directed officials to launch a transparent and practical pilot project in partnership with the private sector to ensure that training programmes remained aligned with evolving industry requirements.

He said equipping young people with practical skills in filmmaking, drama production, editing, colour grading and digital content creation was among the government's key priorities.

The meeting also reviewed proposals for establishing modern classrooms and studio laboratories, installing student workstations, appointing technical staff and trainers, and developing a comprehensive curriculum.

Tarar said students would receive training in a professional environment equipped with modern editing suites, studio laboratories and technical equipment.

He emphasised that the programmes would go beyond theoretical learning by incorporating practical assignments, project development and portfolio building to enhance participants' professional capabilities.

The minister further said young people's creative projects would be encouraged for PTV News, PTV Home and other Pakistan Television platforms, providing emerging talent with opportunities to showcase their work.

He said the initiatives would help strengthen the country's film and drama industry by developing a skilled workforce, introducing advanced technical expertise and making modern production facilities available locally.

He added that efforts would also be made to ensure the financial sustainability of the PTV Academy as it transformed into an effective professional training centre.

headline: NBP issues major currency exchange rates
description: The National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) on Monday issued the selling and buying rates of major foreign currencies in Karachi.
author: NNI
article_text:
The National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) on Monday issued the selling and buying rates of major foreign currencies in Karachi.

According to the rates released on November 2, the US dollar was available at Rs278.54 for selling and Rs275.54 for buying.

The British pound was quoted at Rs372.84 for selling and Rs368.45 for buying, while the euro stood at Rs311.09 and Rs307.43, respectively.

The Japanese yen was traded at Rs1.7636 for selling and Rs1.7427 for buying.

Similarly, the Saudi riyal was listed at Rs74.22 for selling and Rs73.34 for buying, while the UAE dirham stood at Rs75.84 for selling and Rs74.95 for buying.

headline: Maryam Nawaz vows to protect journalists' rights and press freedom
description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday reaffirmed her government's commitment to protecting journalists' rights and press freedom, describing
author: APP
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday reaffirmed her government's commitment to protecting journalists' rights and press freedom, describing media professionals as the eyes and ears of society and champions of truth.

In her message on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, she said journalists raising their voices for truth and justice must be protected and allowed to perform their professional duties without fear.

She said threats, violence and harassment against journalists were unacceptable and those involved in crimes against media professionals must be brought to justice.

The chief minister said freedom of the press and freedom of expression were essential for a democratic society, while free and responsible journalism played a vital role in strengthening democratic institutions.

She said journalists who exposed injustice, oppression and falsehood served society by highlighting public issues and giving voice to the people, adding that any attempt to silence the truth was an attack on fundamental rights.

Maryam Nawaz reiterated that the Punjab government fully supported press freedom and the protection of journalists' professional rights and dignity.

She also expressed her resolve to help homeless journalists realise their dream of owning homes.

The chief minister maintained that journalists in Punjab were safe and said her government would continue to ensure an environment in which they could work freely and securely.

headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 world champion with 3rd-place finish in Mexico
description: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history on Sunday, securing the 2026 drivers' title with a third-place finish at
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history on Sunday, securing the 2026 drivers' title with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian, who replaced seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025, claimed his maiden championship in only his second Formula 1 season, with four rounds remaining.

Antonelli broke Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest Formula 1 world champion and became the first Italian to win the drivers' title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the 71-lap race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, while Ferrari's Hamilton finished second ahead of Antonelli.

Antonelli entered the race with a commanding championship advantage, needing only a ninth-place finish or better to secure the title regardless of his rivals' results.

Starting fourth on the grid, the Italian maintained his position after a chaotic opening lap in which Ferrari's Charles Leclerc took the lead following an off-track battle with teammate Hamilton.

Antonelli briefly led the race as the frontrunners made their pit stops, extending his opening stint until lap 44 before switching from soft to medium tires.

The Mercedes driver rejoined in fourth place before a crash involving Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas brought out the safety car and subsequently a red flag.

After the race restarted on lap 47, Hamilton overtook Leclerc, while Antonelli held off Lando Norris.

On lap 48, Antonelli made a decisive move on Leclerc at Turn 1, overtaking the Ferrari driver to take third place and put himself on course for the world title.

Antonelli maintained his position through another safety car period triggered by Arvid Lindblad's crash on lap 59, keeping his title hopes firmly on course.

With Verstappen and Hamilton battling ahead, Antonelli controlled his pace in the closing laps and crossed the finish line third to become the 2026 world champion.

"We did it! And I wouldn't be here without Mercedes and without my family. I'm speechless, I'm trying to process what's just happened," Antonelli said after the race.

"It's been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max and Lewis is incredible. I look forward to more battles in the future.

"This weekend, I did feel a little more tense. I'm just so happy I got it done," he added.

Verstappen finished 0.799 seconds ahead of Hamilton to claim victory, while newly crowned world champion Antonelli completed the podium, 4.006 seconds behind the winner.

Charles Leclerc finished fourth, followed by Lando Norris, George Russell, Oscar Piastri, Franco Colapinto, Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly.

headline: French government warns against school blockades as protests resume
description: The French government urged students on Monday not to block schools as student and high school organizations resumed demonstrations after a two-week holiday
author: Anadolu
article_text:
The French government urged students on Monday not to block schools as student and high school organizations resumed demonstrations after a two-week holiday break, despite concessions announced last week to end the protest movement.

Education Minister Edouard Geffray called on protesters to allow students to return to classrooms, describing the resumption of classes as an "absolute priority."

Speaking to France Inter, Geffray acknowledged students' right to demonstrate but stressed that protests should not prevent others from accessing education.

He warned that the ongoing unrest could put the school year at risk and reminded protesters that blocking access to educational institutions was illegal.

"You can't prevent your classmates from going to class," he added.

Geffray said reported blockades were mainly concentrated in the Ile-de-France region, northern France, and the southwestern city of Toulouse.

A blockade was reported early Monday outside Helene-Boucher High School in Paris' 20th arrondissement, one of the main centers of the student protest movement, according to broadcaster BFMTV.

Around 20 students placed trash bins in front of the school's entrance, preventing access to classrooms.

Police are also set to reinforce their presence around schools to ensure security and support the educational community following violence during previous demonstrations.

The renewed mobilization comes despite a series of measures announced last Monday aimed at ending protests that began in mid-September.

headline: IRSA releases 99,700 cusecs of water into rivers
description: The Indus River System Authority (IRSA) on Monday released 99,700 cusecs of water from various rim stations, while total inflows stood at 51,500 cusecs.
author: NNI
article_text:
The Indus River System Authority (IRSA) on Monday released 99,700 cusecs of water from various rim stations, while total inflows stood at 51,500 cusecs.

According to IRSA data, the water level at Tarbela Dam stood at 1,506.20 feet, which was 104.20 feet above its dead level of 1,402 feet. Water inflow and outflow at the dam were recorded at 28,900 and 65,000 cusecs, respectively.

At Mangla Dam, the water level was recorded at 1,194.70 feet, 144.70 feet above its dead level of 1,050 feet. Its inflow and outflow stood at 5,900 and 18,000 cusecs, respectively.

The water releases at Kalabagh, Taunsa, Guddu and Sukkur barrages were recorded at 72,900, 43,800, 31,100 and 11,100 cusecs, respectively.

Meanwhile, 8,600 cusecs of water was released from River Kabul at Nowshera, while River Chenab recorded a release of 2,300 cusecs at Marala.

headline: Second batch of digital skills programme launched in DI Khan
description: The district administration on Monday launched the second batch of its digital skills programme at Government Commerce College following the successful
author: NNI
article_text:
The district administration on Monday launched the second batch of its digital skills programme at Government Commerce College following the successful completion of the first batch.

The programme, titled 'NexGen & Smart Skills Youth Hub', was initiated under the supervision of Deputy Commissioner Hikmatullah to equip young people with modern digital skills and practical training to enhance their professional capabilities.

The launch ceremony was attended by the college principal, youth officer and other relevant staff members.

According to the district administration, the initiative aims to empower young people through market-oriented digital skills, enabling them to access better employment opportunities, improve their career prospects and pursue self-employment.

The administration said efforts were also underway to promote technical and vocational education and expand access to digital skills training, recognising youth development as an important driver of national economic growth.

headline: China's high-tech manufacturing, green technologies draw global business interest
description: China's growing emphasis on advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI) and green technologies is attracting international business interest, as the
author: Web Desk
article_text:
China's growing emphasis on advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI) and green technologies is attracting international business interest, as the 140th China Import and Export Fair, commonly known as the Canton Fair, showcases the country's expanding technological capabilities and innovation-driven industrial development.

The fair, marking its 70th anniversary, reflects China's evolving manufacturing model, with automation, digitalisation and sustainable production becoming increasingly important to global trade. According to media reports, the first phase concluded in Guangzhou with 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions, an increase of 13.3% over the corresponding phase of the previous spring session.

More than 12,000 Chinese companies participated in the first phase, including over 6,000 high-quality enterprises recognised for technological innovation and specialised products. Across the fair, around 64% of exhibitors use technologies such as AI and the industrial internet, while new and green products account for 23.2% and 26% of exhibits, respectively.

The event also featured 22 smart application scenarios, 16 AI applications and plans for more than 700 new product launch events, highlighting the growing integration of advanced technologies into manufacturing and international commerce.

Business and industry leaders say China's industrial transformation is reshaping global supply chains and providing developing economies, including Pakistan, with greater scope for technology transfer, industrial partnerships and participation in higher-value manufacturing.

Nosherwan Khalil Khan, President of the Rawalpindi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (RCCI), told Wealth Pakistan that the Canton Fair was an important platform for promoting international trade, strengthening business-to-business connections and facilitating industrial cooperation.

He said RCCI regularly facilitated the participation of its member companies in the fair, held twice a year in spring and autumn, to connect Pakistani businesses with international markets, emerging technologies and potential investment partners.

Khan said China's transition towards advanced manufacturing, AI, automation and green technologies was reshaping global supply chains and creating greater scope for trade, technology transfer and joint ventures.

For Pakistan and other developing economies, he said, this transformation could help modernise industrial processes, improve productivity, enhance product quality and strengthen export competitiveness.

He emphasised that Pakistani businesses should use the Canton Fair not only to source machinery and advanced technologies but also to establish strategic partnerships, attract investment, promote joint ventures and develop domestic manufacturing capabilities.

Khan also highlighted the importance of supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which require better access to modern machinery, technical expertise, affordable financing and international markets to compete effectively.

He said deeper Pakistan-China business collaboration could help diversify Pakistan's export base, promote value addition and integrate local industries into global value chains.

Converting trade relationships into long-term industrial partnerships could accelerate industrial modernisation, generate employment and support the development of a more sustainable, export-oriented economy, he added.

Omais Khattak, President of the Islamabad Industrial Association, told Wealth Pakistan that China's industrial transformation was fundamentally changing global trade by shifting the emphasis from cost-based competition towards value addition and innovation.

He said the evolution of the Canton Fair demonstrated the growing importance of technology transfer, joint ventures and participation in high-value supply chains for developing economies seeking to expand industrial production and strengthen international competitiveness.

Khattak said Pakistan could capitalise on these developments by connecting its Special Economic Zones under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) with Chinese SMEs exploring green and technology-driven industrial relocation.

He said closer industrial cooperation could support the development of domestic manufacturing capabilities while helping Pakistani enterprises adopt advanced production technologies and improve efficiency.

Promoting local production of high-tech components and upgrading industrial capabilities to meet global environmental, social and governance (ESG) requirements could also help Pakistan diversify its exports and strengthen its position in international markets, he added.

The Canton Fair's increasing focus on advanced manufacturing, AI and sustainable technologies reflects China's broader industrial transformation and its growing influence on international production and trade patterns.

For Pakistan, business leaders said, translating these developments into lasting economic gains would require stronger technology partnerships, greater local value addition and closer integration into high-value global supply chains.

headline: Over 35,000 patients with flu-like symptoms reported at Lahore hospitals
description: More than 35,000 patients with flu-, COVID-19- and influenza-like symptoms have been reported at six major government hospitals in Lahore over the past seven
author: NNI
article_text:
More than 35,000 patients with flu-, COVID-19- and influenza-like symptoms have been reported at six major government hospitals in Lahore over the past seven days as smog intensifies and seasonal viral infections spread across the city.

According to sources, Mayo Hospital reported the highest number of patients, with more than 11,000 people seeking treatment for related symptoms. Services Hospital received over 9,800 patients, while more than 1,000 were reported at Jinnah Hospital.

Thousands of patients with similar complaints also visited General Hospital, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Children’s Hospital.

Sources said rapid testing had also detected positive COVID-19 cases, raising concerns about the spread of viral infections.

The head of the Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) Department at Services Hospital said different COVID-19 variants might be less severe than previous strains, but their symptoms should not be ignored. He advised people experiencing flu-like symptoms to consult qualified doctors rather than resorting to self-diagnosis or treatment.

Professor Shahbaz Ghori said COVID-19, seasonal influenza and smog could cause similar respiratory symptoms, making precautionary measures and timely medical examinations important.

Amid rising air pollution and viral infections, residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary outdoor activities, wear masks and maintain proper hygiene.

headline: Pakistan's remittances expected to exceed $44 billion this fiscal year: Aurangzeb
description: Federal Minister for Finance Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb has said Pakistan's remittances are expected to exceed $44 billion during the current fiscal year,
author: NNI
article_text:
Federal Minister for Finance Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb has said Pakistan's remittances are expected to exceed $44 billion during the current fiscal year, emphasising the need for sustained economic reforms, digital innovation and stronger cybersecurity measures.

Addressing a Pakistan Banks Association event virtually, the finance minister said Pakistan's journey from economic stability towards sustainable growth was continuing, with fiscal discipline, export growth and private investment remaining essential priorities.

He said financial innovation should help reduce business costs, improve access to financial services and bring more people into the formal economy. Digital assets, he added, should be integrated into the financial system based on their genuine economic benefits and potential to facilitate business activities.

Aurangzeb cited the use of deposit tokens for institutional users on blockchain networks as a practical example of digital financial innovation.

He said the Bank for International Settlements' Project Agorá was examining tokenised bank deposits, while the State Bank of Pakistan was reviewing possibilities for cross-border payments through reserves.

The minister stressed that banks had a crucial role in protecting public funds and addressing risks associated with digital technologies while ensuring effective services for consumers.

He said the regulatory framework needed to distinguish between different types of digital assets and their economic activities.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan had established a legal framework under the Virtual Assets Act 2026, with the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) responsible for licensing and supervising virtual asset service providers.

He added that the State Bank of Pakistan and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan also had important roles in developing the regulatory framework for digital assets.

The minister said risks associated with unbacked crypto assets were different and required separate consideration under the regulatory system.

He said Pakistan received $41.6 billion in remittances during the previous fiscal year, with inflows expected to surpass $44 billion in the ongoing fiscal year.

Aurangzeb emphasised that there was no room for complacency in addressing cybersecurity risks alongside the expansion of digital financial systems.

headline: AI models mostly smarter than top scientists, OpenAI's Altman says
description: Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant portions of white-collar work, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said on Monday.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference in the United Arab Emirates, Altman highlighted the dramatic leap in AI capabilities over the past year.

"At the start of this year, AI was mostly not as smart as our smartest scientist, and now it's mostly smarter than them," Altman said.

"AI was mostly not able to do a lot of white-collar jobs, and now it mostly can do a lot of parts of that," he added.

Altman stressed that despite the disruptive impact on global economies and employment, human judgment, creativity and accountability must remain central to the technology's deployment.

"We think it is absolutely critical that people remain in control of the future; there should not be a handoff to AI, there should not be a gradual 'we are going to let AI decide what is best for us,'" he said.

"AI needs to be a tool built for people and needs to serve people, not the other way around," Altman noted.

Addressing concerns surrounding the massive electricity demands of computing infrastructure, he described physical power supply as the single biggest bottleneck for the sector.

"Everything else we're going to make huge progress on, except atoms are still atoms and the physical world that has to power this is going to be the dominant factor of the cost and the abundance," he said.

Altman also noted that global per capita token consumption has surged from near zero six years ago to roughly 100,000 tokens a month, while top institutional users consume about 500 billion tokens monthly.

Highlighting the host nation's rapid adoption of technology, he pointed out that around 80% of young people in the UAE use ChatGPT on a weekly basis.

During the event, OpenAI announced partnerships with Emirati technology group G42 and state oil producer Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, marking the first global deployment of OpenAI's frontier models by an energy company.

headline: Pakistan, South Korea sign MoU to strengthen judicial cooperation
description: Pakistan and South Korea's supreme courts sign an MoU to strengthen judicial cooperation, promote digital justice, AI integration and institutional reforms.
author: APP
article_text:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Supreme Court of South Korea on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) aimed at strengthening bilateral judicial cooperation, promoting institutional exchanges and advancing technological innovation in the justice system.

The agreement was signed during an official visit to Seoul by the Chief Justice of Pakistan, who was received by his South Korean counterpart, Justice Jo Hee-de, at the Supreme Court of Korea.

The two chief justices held discussions on strengthening institutional ties, promoting mutual learning and exploring opportunities for closer cooperation between the judiciaries of the two countries.

The meeting concluded with the signing of the MoU, marking a step towards expanding judicial relations between Pakistan and South Korea.

The agreement establishes a framework for sustained institutional engagement, covering judicial exchanges, professional capacity building, judicial education, collaborative research and the sharing of institutional experiences and best practices.

It places particular emphasis on judicial reforms and modernisation, electronic court systems, digital justice, artificial intelligence and its responsible use in judicial administration, smart courts, judicial analytics and cybersecurity.

Under the agreement, both countries will facilitate reciprocal judicial delegations, professional attachments, study visits, expert exchanges, joint conferences and seminars, along with periodic high-level judicial dialogue.

The MoU also provides an institutional mechanism to coordinate and implement mutually agreed initiatives, ensuring continued engagement between the two judiciaries.

During the visit, the Chief Justice of Pakistan also met Justice Noh Gyeongpil, Minister of the National Court Administration of South Korea.

Their discussions focused on judicial administration, institutional governance and the role of technological innovation in improving court management and the delivery of justice.

The chief justice also visited the Supreme Court of Korea's IT Centre, where he was briefed on technological advancements in judicial administration, digital court systems and technology-enabled justice services.

The visit provided an opportunity to examine South Korea's experience in judicial digitalisation and explore areas of potential cooperation relevant to Pakistan's ongoing judicial reform and digital transformation initiatives.

Pakistan's Ambassador to South Korea, Syed Moazzam Shah, accompanied the chief justice throughout the visit and participated in meetings and other engagements, extending diplomatic support to efforts aimed at strengthening institutional relations between the two countries.

The signing of the MoU forms part of the Supreme Court of Pakistan's efforts to expand international judicial cooperation and draw on global experiences to advance institutional reforms.

The agreement is expected to facilitate knowledge sharing, professional development and the adoption of innovative approaches to judicial administration through structured engagement with South Korea's technologically advanced judiciary.

headline: Maryam Nawaz sets target to train 2,500 rural women under SheThreads programme
description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has set a target of providing textile skills training to 2,500 rural women by June 2027 under the SheThreads
author: APP
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has set a target of providing textile skills training to 2,500 rural women by June 2027 under the SheThreads programme, with 1,150 women already having completed training.

The initiative aims to equip rural women with market-oriented skills and provide them with dignified employment opportunities in the textile industry. Participants will also receive a monthly stipend of Rs15,000 during the training period.

Under the programme, the Women Development Department has started registration of women from rural areas of Lahore for a three-month training course at Shahkam Industries on Multan Road.

The training will focus on industrial sewing machine operation and apparel supervision, combining classroom instruction with practical sessions to prepare participants for employment in the textile sector.

Women aged between 18 and 45 years, holding Punjab domicile and having at least a matriculation qualification, are eligible to apply.

Interested candidates can submit their applications at Shahkam Industries along with their national identity cards and domicile certificates. After initial screening and verification, shortlisted candidates will be required to submit an affidavit before admission.

Further information about registration is available through assistant commissioners, union council secretaries and relevant district offices.

Maryam Nawaz said the initiative aimed to empower rural women through market-oriented skills and enable them to earn a respectable livelihood.

She said the programme would equip participants with skills according to industry requirements and facilitate their employment in the textile sector after successful completion of training.

author: Web Desk
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has given a 15-day deadline to achieve a 100 per cent improvement in cleanliness across the province, directing authorities to take strict measures against poor sanitation and ensure effective waste management.

Chairing a special meeting to review the performance of the Suthra Punjab programme, the chief minister decided to end the contracts of unsatisfactory solid waste management companies and shift to self-operations in Lahore, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Multan and Dera Ghazi Khan.

Expressing concern over dust and dirt on roads across the province, Maryam Nawaz ordered the daily washing of major roads. She directed authorities to impose fines on those found dumping waste on roads after cleaning operations.

She also instructed officials to take measures to penalise people for littering in markets, bazaars, vegetable markets, fruit markets and grain markets. The chief minister directed that villages be cleaned every alternate day.

A target has also been set to ensure adequate human resources and machinery in every district. Deputy commissioners and assistant commissioners were directed to hold weekly meetings with field monitoring officers and establish key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess their performance.

The chief minister ordered timely payment of workers' salaries in every city and locality and sought details from all deputy commissioners about the machinery required for sanitation operations.

She also sought a final record of savings achieved through the shift to self-operations. Authorities are considering imposing fines on owners of vacant plots where garbage is found.

Deputy commissioners from Multan, Rajanpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Hafizabad, Muzaffargarh and other districts presented reports on sanitation arrangements during the meeting.

Maryam Nawaz directed deputy commissioners to physically verify machinery and equipment available in their respective districts.

She has called another meeting after one week to review progress under the Suthra Punjab programme.

headline: Gilani pledges parliamentary support for water security initiatives
description: Senate Chairman Yousaf Raza Gilani on Monday pledged parliamentary support through legislation, oversight and budgetary allocations to advance commitments made
author: APP
article_text:
Senate Chairman Yousaf Raza Gilani on Monday pledged parliamentary support through legislation, oversight and budgetary allocations to advance commitments made at Pakistan Water Week 2026, describing water security as a national priority.

Inaugurating the sixth edition of the five-day conference, being held in Islamabad from November 2 to 6, Gilani said Parliament must ensure that water policies translated into practical improvements for farming communities and people affected by floods and water shortages.

He identified three key areas for parliamentary action: enforceable legislation, effective oversight and sustained funding. He called for full implementation of provincial water laws and stronger governance of groundwater resources.

Gilani said Parliament should assess whether water policies were benefiting farmers at the tail end of irrigation networks and whether flood warnings were reaching villages in time. He stressed that budgets should prioritise disaster prevention alongside relief efforts.

He noted that solar-powered pumps had provided relief to farmers but required regulations to govern groundwater extraction. He also called for careful aquifer management, planned groundwater recharge and the use of floodwater to replenish underground reserves.

Sharing reliable data, he said, could strengthen trust between provinces, while women, young people and farming communities should be involved as partners in water management.

Recalling his tenure as prime minister during the 2010 floods, Gilani said Pakistan faced the twin challenges of devastating floods and declining water availability.

He said the 2022 floods affected around 33 million people and caused more than $30 billion in damage and economic losses, while nearly seven million people were affected by floods last year. At the same time, per capita water availability had declined from more than 5,000 cubic metres to around 1,000 cubic metres.

“Too much water and too little, sometimes in the same districts within the same year,” he said, stressing that response alone did not ensure resilience.

Gilani questioned whether reconstruction efforts were reducing future risks or recreating existing vulnerabilities. He also reiterated Pakistan's position that the Indus Waters Treaty remained valid and binding, saying water must never be used as an instrument of pressure.

He called for a water-secure and flood-resilient Pakistan by the country's centenary in 2047.

IWMI Pakistan Country Representative Dr Muhammad Ashraf said water security was closely linked to food security, climate resilience and economic stability. He stressed that each conference session should produce clear commitments, identify responsibilities and set timelines for action.

In his keynote address, IWMI Strategic Programme Director for Water, Food and Ecosystems Dr Mohsin Hafeez said Pakistan had substantial evidence and ideas but needed a shared commitment to translate them into action. Decisions taken in Islamabad, he said, must bring tangible improvements for farmers.

More than 200 participants attended the opening session of the conference, organised by the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) and the CGIAR Policy Innovations Science Program in collaboration with the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources and the Ministry of Water Resources.

The programme features two thematic tracks, each comprising 13 sessions, along with plenary discussions on development partners' water and climate priorities and water governance in the Indus Basin. The closing ceremony is scheduled for November 5, while the conference will continue until November 6.

Concluding his address, Gilani urged participants to consider how their commitments would improve the lives of a farmer in Thar, a family living along the Ravi or a child in Quetta waiting for clean water.

headline: LPG price reaches Rs600 per kg in Lahore
description: LPG distributors have protested against the alleged overcharging of consumers in Lahore, as the price of liquefied petroleum gas has reportedly surged to Rs600
author: NNI
article_text:
LPG distributors have protested against the alleged overcharging of consumers in Lahore, as the price of liquefied petroleum gas has reportedly surged to Rs600 per kilogram from Rs250 previously.

Chairman LPG Distributors Irfan Khokhar said the last liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessel arrived in Pakistan in July 2026, raising concerns about gas supplies and prices.

Speaking to a private television channel, he attributed the increase in LPG prices to local manufacturers, saying the sharp rise had created difficulties for consumers.

Khokhar urged the government to bring local gas units under its control to regulate prices. He also called for a tax-exemption policy on LPG imports to improve supplies and ensure the availability of gas at affordable rates.

A report citing sources last week warned that LPG prices could reach Rs1,000 per kilogram during winter if the government did not intervene.

Meanwhile, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has announced a significant increase in the prices of gas supplied nationwide by Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and Sui Southern Gas Company.

headline: PM Shehbaz directs banks to expedite loans for priority sectors
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Finance Ministry to take strict action against banks showing sluggish
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and the Finance Ministry to take strict action against banks showing sluggish performance in providing loans to agriculture, housing and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) under government initiatives.

Chairing a review meeting on facilitating financing for priority sectors in Islamabad on Monday, the prime minister said that promoting SMEs, housing and agriculture was among the government's top priorities to strengthen the economy and create employment opportunities for young people.

He appreciated banks demonstrating good performance in extending loans to these sectors and stressed that banks should extend the same level of cooperation to priority-sector financing as the government and its institutions provided to the banking industry.

"Private sector development is critically dependent on banks," he said, adding that SMEs had significant potential to drive economic growth, boost exports and generate employment.

Highlighting the importance of agriculture, the prime minister described it as the backbone of the national economy and said the government was working to increase exports through value addition in agricultural products.

He also observed that the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Scheme would promote the housing and construction sectors and benefit several allied industries.

Shehbaz Sharif directed the finance minister to engage stakeholders from the SME, agriculture and housing sectors, address their financing-related challenges and develop a comprehensive strategy.

He also instructed the SBP and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to jointly resolve tax-related issues faced by SMEs and exporters. The prime minister further called for a comprehensive risk-coverage strategy to facilitate lending to small and medium-sized businesses.

During the briefing, the meeting was informed that the SBP was working on three key pillars to expand financing for priority sectors: improving regulations, sharing risks and costs between the government and banks, and promoting digital financial services.

The recently launched SME Connect digital portal (smeconnect.sbp.org.pk) will enable businesses to apply for loans and track the progress of their applications.

The meeting was informed that, as of October 23, loans worth Rs511 billion had been approved under the Prime Minister's Apna Ghar Programme, covering 86,899 applications. Loans amounting to Rs91 billion had been disbursed to 15,584 applicants.

The overall volume of housing finance had reached Rs455 billion, benefiting 187,317 borrowers.

In the agriculture sector, outstanding financing stood at Rs1,329 billion, benefiting around 3.5 million people. Meanwhile, SME financing had reached Rs1,148 billion, with 342,458 businesses accessing loans.

Targets have been set to increase financing in both the agriculture and SME sectors to Rs1,500 billion by the end of the fiscal year 2027, the meeting was told.

The briefing also highlighted government initiatives involving risk-sharing arrangements and credit guarantees for housing, agriculture and SMEs. Efforts were also underway to simplify loan procedures, reduce documentation requirements and improve access to finance through digital systems.

The performance indicators of commercial banks in all three priority sectors were also presented, with the prime minister appreciating banks that had demonstrated strong performance.

Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Dr Musadik Malik, Mian Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar and Shaza Fatima Khawaja attended the meeting.

Prime Minister's Adviser Haroon Akhtar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad, MNAs Hafizuddin and Chaudhry Iftikhar Nazir, senior officials and heads and representatives of leading commercial banks were also present.

headline: Week-long polio vaccination drive begins across 97 districts
description: Pakistan on Monday launched a week-long sub-national polio vaccination campaign across 97 selected districts, targeting more than 23.9 million children under
author: APP
article_text: Pakistan on Monday launched a week-long sub-national polio vaccination campaign across 97 selected districts, targeting more than 23.9 million children under five years of age to protect them against the crippling disease. According to the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), the campaign will continue until November 8, with vaccination teams administering polio drops to eligible children through door-to-door visits and other designated arrangements. Across Punjab, more than 9.278 million children will be vaccinated in 13 selected districts, while 6.883 million children will receive polio drops in 20 districts of Sindh. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the campaign will cover 27 selected districts, targeting over 4.808 million children, while 2.217 million children will be vaccinated in 31 districts of Balochistan. In Islamabad, more than 447,000 children will receive polio drops. The campaign will also cover three selected districts of Gilgit-Baltistan, targeting over 153,000 children, and two districts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, where more than 183,000 children will be vaccinated. The NEOC has urged parents to ensure that all children under five receive polio drops during the ongoing and every subsequent campaign, emphasizing that repeated vaccination is essential for building strong immunity against the virus. It said providing children with a polio-free future was a shared national responsibility and called on parents and communities to extend full cooperation to vaccination teams to achieve the complete eradication of poliovirus from the country.

The NEOC has urged parents to ensure that all children under five receive polio drops during the ongoing and every subsequent campaign, emphasizing that repeated vaccination is essential for building strong immunity against the virus.

It said providing children with a polio-free future was a shared national responsibility and called on parents and communities to extend full cooperation to vaccination teams to achieve the complete eradication of poliovirus from the country.

headline: Gold prices rise by Rs2,400 per tola
description: The prices of gold witnessed an increase in the local market on Monday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola rising by Rs2,400 to settle at Rs412,136,
author: APP
article_text: The prices of gold witnessed an increase in the local market on Monday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola rising by Rs2,400 to settle at Rs412,136, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold increased by Rs2,058 to Rs353,340, while 10 grams of 22-karat gold rose by Rs1,886 to Rs323,906. In the international market, the price of gold increased by $24 to reach $3,896 per ounce, the association reported. Meanwhile, the price of silver per tola increased by Rs100 to Rs5,488, while the price of 10 grams of silver rose by Rs86 to Rs4,705. The price of silver in the international market also increased by $1 to reach $50.10 per ounce, the association added.

headline: DPM Dar reiterates Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening of strategic, cooperative partnership with China
description: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Monday, reaffirmed Pakistan’s continued commitment to further strengthening the
author: APP
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Monday, reaffirmed Pakistan’s continued commitment to further strengthening the ‘All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership’ with China.

The DPM/FM held a bilateral meeting with Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee (IDCPC), the Foreign Office Spokespersons said in a press release.

The two sides discussed ways to enhance cultural ties and people-to-people exchanges.

Both leaders expressed their resolve to maintain close coordination and carry forward the positive momentum in bilateral relations.

Minister Liu conveyed greetings from Foreign Minister Wang Yi, which the DPM/FM warmly reciprocated.

The DPM/FM also conveyed warm greetings to President Xi Jinping on behalf of Pakistan’s leadership.

headline: Pakistan, Bangladesh explore new avenue for industrial cooperation, economic partnership
description: Advisor to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan on Monday held a meeting with Bangladesh’s Minister for Finance and Planning
author: APP
article_text: Advisor to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan on Monday held a meeting with Bangladesh’s Minister for Finance and Planning Rashid Al Mahmud Titumir and explored new avenues for strengthening bilateral economic ties, with a focus on industrial cooperation, export-led growth, clean energy, technology transfer and investment. The advisor received the Bangladeshi minister along with his delegation and discussed bilateral relations, industrial cooperation, export-led growth and opportunities for strengthening economic ties between the two countries, said a news release. The meeting was attended by Rana Ihsan Afzal, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Industries and Commerce; Humaira Zia Mufti, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Industries and Production; and Freedoon Akram Sheikh, Joint Secretary. Welcoming the delegation, Haroon said that Pakistan and Bangladesh shared brotherly relations rooted in common cultural heritage and historical connections. On behalf of the people of Pakistan, he warmly welcomed the distinguished guests and expressed his desire to further strengthen bilateral engagement. The advisor said that the prime minister attached particular importance to strengthening relations with regional countries and promoting economic cooperation through mutually beneficial partnerships. Highlighting Pakistan’s ongoing industrial transformation, Haroon said the government was introducing regulatory reforms to facilitate investment, accelerate industrial development and improve the business environment. He emphasized that the government’s approach was to replace red tape with a red carpet for investors, ensuring greater facilitation and ease of doing business. The advisor briefed the visiting delegation on Pakistan’s initiatives in the automotive and clean energy sectors, stating that the country had introduced a New Energy Vehicle Policy to facilitate the transition towards sustainable and environmentally friendly technologies. He further informed the delegation that work was underway on the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy to promote the local manufacturing of lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries. He added that the government was also facilitating the rapid expansion of electric vehicle charging infrastructure across the country. Highlighting Pakistan’s progress in solar technology, Haroon Akhtar Khan said that these emerging sectors offered significant opportunities for collaboration between Pakistan and Bangladesh. He identified solar technology, battery manufacturing, electric vehicles and broader industrial development as promising areas for bilateral cooperation. He emphasized that both countries could explore mutually beneficial opportunities through industrial partnerships, technology transfer, joint ventures and greater value addition in products. The advisor also stressed the importance of export-led growth, manufacturing expansion, industrial productivity and value addition as key pillars for strengthening economic cooperation between the two countries. During the meeting, Rashid Al Mahmud Titumir expressed warm sentiments towards Pakistan and its people, describing the relationship between the two countries as brotherly. The visiting minister shared Bangladesh’s economic experience and highlighted the country’s progress in overcoming various economic challenges. He said that Bangladesh had made significant efforts to stabilize its microeconomic and macroeconomic indicators while achieving improvements in industrial growth and manufacturing. He also emphasized the potential for expanding economic and industrial cooperation between Pakistan and Bangladesh, noting that stronger bilateral engagement could create new opportunities for both countries. The meeting concluded with a shared understanding of the need to strengthen economic engagement, explore new avenues of industrial collaboration, and promote mutually beneficial partnerships between Pakistan and Bangladesh.

headline: Islamabad court sentences man to seven years in PECA harassment case
description: An Islamabad court has sentenced Raja Haris Naveed, the main accused in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old student and the recording
author: Web Desk
article_text:
An Islamabad court has sentenced Raja Haris Naveed, the main accused in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old student and the recording of an objectionable video, to seven years of rigorous imprisonment.

Additional Sessions Judge Muhammad Afzal Majoka announced the verdict in the case registered under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA).

The court also imposed a fine of Rs1 million on Naveed. He will face an additional six months in prison if he fails to pay the amount.

However, the court acquitted co-accused Shahzeb Mairaj, extending him the benefit of the doubt after the prosecution failed to establish his role in assisting the crime.

According to the case details, Naveed allegedly lured the 16-year-old matriculation student through deception and confined him in a drawing room. He then harassed the student at gunpoint and recorded an indecent video without his consent.

headline: Water, food and national security closely linked, says IWMI Pakistan representative
description: International Water Management Institute (IWMI) Country Representative in Pakistan, Dr Muhammad Ashraf, has highlighted the close connection between water
author: APP
article_text:
International Water Management Institute (IWMI) Country Representative in Pakistan, Dr Muhammad Ashraf, has highlighted the close connection between water security, food security and national security, urging coordinated action to tackle the country’s growing water challenges.

Speaking at the opening session of the sixth Pakistan Water Week 2026, a five-day international conference, Dr Ashraf drew attention to the mounting pressure of climate change on the country’s water resources.

He said Pakistan Water Week had developed into a key forum where local and international stakeholders could discuss water-related issues and consider sustainable ways to address them.

Reflecting on the lessons learned from previous editions, Dr Ashraf emphasised the need to keep water security among the country’s national priorities. He also called for engagement across different sectors to support the transition towards sustainable water management.

The sixth edition of Pakistan Water Week is being held under the theme, “Commitments to Action: Advancing Water Security and Achieving Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Pakistan.”

IWMI is organising the conference in partnership with the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) and the Ministry of Water Resources.

The event is supported by PCRWR through the Ministry of Water Resources, UNICEF, the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR), the CGIAR Policy Innovations Science Program and the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).

headline: Diamond Paints Launches ‘Pakkay Rishtay Ki Demand’ Campaign Against Jahez Demands
description: As wedding season begins across Pakistan, Diamond Paints is using its voice to address an issue that continues to place unnecessary pressure on families: Jahez
author: Web Desk
article_text:
As wedding season begins across Pakistan, Diamond Paints is using its voice to address an issue that continues to place unnecessary pressure on families: Jahez demands.

With the launch of its new campaign, “Pakkay Rishtay Ki Demand,” Diamond Paints is taking a firm position against the expectations and material demands that can become attached to marriage.

Launching across television and digital platforms, the nationwide campaign asks society to reconsider what should truly matter when two families come together.

The Only Demand Should Be a Strong Relationship

Weddings should mark the beginning of a relationship built on respect, understanding and mutual support. Yet for many families, marriage can also bring expectations surrounding furniture, appliances, money and other material possessions to be provided by the bride’s family.

These expectations are often normalised as part of wedding tradition. But when something is expected, requested or made a condition of marriage, it stops being simply a gift.

That is the distinction at the heart of “Pakkay Rishtay Ki Demand.”

The campaign does not question what parents may voluntarily choose to give their children as they begin a new chapter of their lives. Instead, it challenges the culture of demanding Jahez and the financial and emotional pressure such expectations can create.

A marriage should not begin with a list of material requirements.

Challenging an Expectation That Has Become Normalised

Through the campaign, Diamond Paints is encouraging parents, young people and families on both sides of a marriage to question expectations that may have gone unchallenged for generations.

For parents of sons, it is an opportunity to reject the idea that marriage entitles a family to expect material goods from the bride’s side.

For young men and women, it is a reminder that the foundation of a marriage should be the relationship they are choosing to build together.

And for parents of daughters, marriage should not become an obligation to meet demands to secure their daughter’s future.

Changing a deeply embedded social expectation requires more than placing responsibility on one group. It requires families, particularly those in a position to make or reject such demands, to make a conscious choice.

Diamond Paints Uses Its Platform to Start a Wider Conversation

For Diamond Paints, a brand closely associated with homes and the lives built within them, the campaign provides an opportunity to speak about what should form the foundation of a new home in the first place.

A home may be filled with furniture, appliances and possessions over time. But none of those things should determine the value of a marriage or become the price attached to beginning one.

With “Pakkay Rishtay Ki Demand,” Diamond Paints is moving beyond simply acknowledging the problem and using its national platform to make its position clear: relationships should come without Jahez demands.

The campaign will continue across the wedding season through television, digital content and wider conversations around the issue, encouraging more families to question a practice that has too often been accepted as simply “the way things are.”

Because when a rishta is built on respect, there should only be one demand: a strong relationship.

Pakkay Rishtay Ki Demand.

#EndJahezDemands

headline: Ahsan Iqbal proposes five political corridors between CPC and Pakistani parties
description: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal has proposed creating five political corridors between the Communist
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal has proposed creating five political corridors between the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Pakistani political parties to expand institutional cooperation and ensure continuity in national development policies.

Speaking at the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Iqbal said the proposed initiative would include exchanges involving young people and political leaders.

He said Pakistan could draw important lessons from China’s development model, particularly its emphasis on public service, organisational discipline, self-reform, effective governance and long-term planning.

The minister noted that Pakistan had suffered setbacks whenever established development policies were discontinued following changes in government. He stressed that national plans should extend beyond electoral cycles to maintain progress over the long term.

He added that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) was committed to promoting these principles within the country’s democratic system.

Referring to the launch of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) during former prime minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif’s tenure, Iqbal said its first phase had converted a memorandum of understanding into around $25 billion in investment. He said the projects had added more than 8,000 megawatts of electricity to the national grid, built 888 kilometres of highways and motorways, and created approximately 236,000 direct and indirect jobs.

Reaffirming the longstanding relationship between the two countries, Iqbal said Pakistan-China friendship remained above political differences and changes in government, enjoying broad support among their people.

Discussing URAAN Pakistan and CPEC 2.0, he said the five proposed political corridors would complement the five economic corridors. They would focus on strategic dialogue, governance and development learning, youth and leadership development, cultural links, and regional peace and cooperation.

The minister placed particular emphasis on engaging young people, proposing reciprocal exchanges between emerging leaders from the CPC and Pakistani political parties. The programme could begin with an initial group in 2027, offering participants structured learning opportunities at China’s Central Party School.

Congratulating Chinese President Xi Jinping and the CPC on the conclusion of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, Iqbal said the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China offered an opportunity to deepen political and institutional ties.

He said leadership should be judged not only by what is achieved during a term in office, but also by the lasting institutions, policies and foundations established for coming generations.

Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal has proposed creating five political corridors between the Communist Party of China (CPC) and Pakistani political parties to expand institutional cooperation and ensure continuity in national development policies.

Speaking at the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Iqbal said the proposed initiative would include exchanges involving young people and political leaders.

He said Pakistan could draw important lessons from China’s development model, particularly its emphasis on public service, organisational discipline, self-reform, effective governance and long-term planning.

False rape cases emerge as new challenge for south Punjab police

The minister noted that Pakistan had suffered setbacks whenever established development policies were discontinued following changes in government. He stressed that national plans should extend beyond electoral cycles to maintain progress over the long term.

He added that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) was committed to promoting these principles within the country’s democratic system.

Referring to the launch of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) during former prime minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif’s tenure, Iqbal said its first phase had converted a memorandum of understanding into around $25 billion in investment. He said the projects had added more than 8,000 megawatts of electricity to the national grid, built 888 kilometres of highways and motorways, and created approximately 236,000 direct and indirect jobs.

DIG Prisons inspects Bahawalnagar District Jail

Reaffirming the longstanding relationship between the two countries, Iqbal said Pakistan-China friendship remained above political differences and changes in government, enjoying broad support among their people.

Discussing URAAN Pakistan and CPEC 2.0, he said the five proposed political corridors would complement the five economic corridors. They would focus on strategic dialogue, governance and development learning, youth and leadership development, cultural links, and regional peace and cooperation.

The minister placed particular emphasis on engaging young people, proposing reciprocal exchanges between emerging leaders from the CPC and Pakistani political parties. The programme could begin with an initial group in 2027, offering participants structured learning opportunities at China’s Central Party School.

Man kills former mother-in-law over divorce dispute

Congratulating Chinese President Xi Jinping and the CPC on the conclusion of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, Iqbal said the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China offered an opportunity to deepen political and institutional ties.

He said leadership should be judged not only by what is achieved during a term in office, but also by the lasting institutions, policies and foundations established for coming generations.

headline: PHP police arrest 60 wanted criminals
description: FAISALABAD -The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) Police on Sunday intensified its crackdown against criminal elements in Faisalabad region during October
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: FAISALABAD -The Punjab Highway Patrol (PHP) Police on Sunday intensified its crackdown against criminal elements in Faisalabad region during October 2026,arresting 38 proclaimed offenders and 22 court absconders,recovering 599 liters of liquor and safely reuniting seven missing children with their families. According to SP Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region Muhammad Tariq Malik,the force registered 692 cases during the month as part of its efforts to maintain law and order,prevent crime,ensure highway safety and provide timely assistance to commuters. He said Faisalabad district accounted for 271 cases,followed by Jhang with 213,Toba Tek Singh 135 and Chiniot 73. During operations against criminal elements, PHP personnel arrested 60 wanted suspects,including 38 proclaimed offenders and 22 court absconders. In its drive against drug-related offenses,the force registered 34 cases and recovered 599 liters of liquor to curb illegal activities and prevent the circulation of intoxicating substances in the region,he added.The PHP also intensified action against illegal weapons,registering five cases and recovering three 30-bore pistols, one 12-bore gun and 12 rounds and cartridges. In other recoveries,the force seized a stolen motorcycle bearing registration number ARR-9274 and cash amounting to Rs.21,100. During a separate operation in Faisalabad district,PHP personnel also confiscated 595 kilograms of hazardous meat from dead animals,preventing its potential supply to consumers. Alongside law enforcement operations,the force continued providing public assistance and emergency support to highway users. Malik said PHP personnel assisted 2,091 people across the region by providing guidance and timely help to commuters facing difficulties during their journeys. To ensure smooth traffic flow and improve road safety, the personnel also removed 61 encroachments from highways,facilitating motorists and helping ensure safer movement of traffic. In a significant humanitarian initiative,the force recovered seven missing children from different locations and safely reunited them with their parents and relatives. Reviewing the monthly performance,SP Muhammad Tariq Malik said the Punjab Highway Patrol Faisalabad Region was diligently performing its professional responsibilities to prevent crime on highways,protect the lives and property of citizens and provide commuters with a safe,secure and peaceful travelling environment. He reaffirmed that the force would continue its operations against criminal elements while maintaining its focus on public safety,highway security and timely assistance to road users. He added that public service and protection of citizens would remain a priority with patrol personnel continuing to utilize their professional capabilities to ensure safer highways and improved security throughout Faisalabad region.

headline: Farewell ceremony held in honour of two transferred DSPs in Muzaffargarh
description: MUZAFFARGARH - District Police Officer (DPO) Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah hosted a farewell ceremony in honour of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) City Circle
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - District Police Officer (DPO) Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah hosted a farewell ceremony in honour of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) City Circle Zafar Wattoo and DSP Alipur Circle Allah Yar Saifi, who have been transferred from Muzaffargarh district. According to Police Media Coordinator Nawab Umar Khan Sherwani, the ceremony was attended by DPO Syed Ghazanfar Ali Shah, SP Investigation Nasir Mahmood and ASP Nabeel Ahmed Langrial. DSPs from across the district, heads of various branches, DSP Investigation Malik Akbar Mahmood, DSP Safe City Tariq Sattar and his staff were also present. During the ceremony, the DPO presented honorary shields to both outgoing officers in recognition of their professional services and contributions to the district. He also extended his best wishes to them for their new assignments.

headline: Faisalabad police arrest thousands of suspects in major crime crackdown
description: FAISALABAD - Under the leadership of City Police Officer (CPO) Tanveer Hussain, Faisalabad Police have arrested thousands of suspects involved in serious
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: FAISALABAD - Under the leadership of City Police Officer (CPO) Tanveer Hussain, Faisalabad Police have arrested thousands of suspects involved in serious criminal activities during the current year. According to police, a total of 434 suspects involved in murder cases have been arrested and sent to jail during the current year. Furthermore 43 suspects involved in blind murder cases were traced and arrested with the help of modern technical resources. Police also arrested 691 suspects involved in attempted murder cases, while 75 suspects wanted in robbery cases were apprehended and legal proceedings were initiated against them. In addition 3,380 suspects involved in street robbery incidents were arrested as part of the ongoing crackdown against criminal elements. Police officials stated that modern technology and technical resources are being utilized to trace and apprehend suspects involved in serious criminal activities. CPO Faisalabad Tanveer Hussain stated that all legal requirements would be fulfilled to ensure that suspects involved in serious crimes receive punishment in accordance with the law.

headline: Khawaja Farid University, college face decline amid mismanagement
description: RAHIM YAR KHAN - Two major educational institutions named after renowned regional Sufi saint Khawaja Ghulam Farid are reportedly losing their academic standing
author: IHSAN UL HAQ
article_text:
RAHIM YAR KHAN - Two major educational institutions named after renowned regional Sufi saint Khawaja Ghulam Farid are reportedly losing their academic standing amid prolonged mismanagement, internal politics and the absence of permanent heads, forcing students to seek quality education in other major cities. Khawaja Farid College, established in 1952 as the first college in the district, and Khawaja Farid University, established in 2014 as its first university, were both named after the celebrated saint. However, residents say both institutions have witnessed a steady decline in academic standards due to alleged favouritism in appointments and administrative affairs. The university, established during the tenure of former chief minister Shehbaz Sharif, has allegedly been operating under ad hoc arrangements even 12 years after its establishment. Key positions, including registrar, controller of examinations and treasurer, have reportedly not been filled on a permanent basis. The prolonged absence of a permanent controller of examinations has caused serious difficulties for students, particularly delays in degree verification. According to reports, some students have even lost foreign scholarship opportunities as a result. Successive vice chancellors have also been accused of appointing people from their own groups to key positions. The university is reportedly facing a shortage of faculty members, including the absence of a pro-vice chancellor, affecting its academic and administrative affairs. Allegations have also surfaced that classes were launched in certain departments without proper approval for faculty positions and new disciplines during the tenures of its first two vice chancellors, damaging the institution’s reputation. Former vice chancellors have also faced allegations of making appointments in violation of merit and awarding contracts to favoured individuals, compromising the quality of construction work. Around three years ago, a newly constructed building on the campus reportedly collapsed shortly after its completion, allegedly due to substandard construction. However, no action was reportedly taken against those responsible. The university’s international ranking has also allegedly declined sharply. The vice chancellor appointed around two years ago reportedly attempted to address these problems but could not overcome powerful internal lobbies and administrative differences. He resigned a few days ago, citing personal reasons. In 2022, a principal was removed following a written complaint against a teacher who allegedly used inappropriate language. The college subsequently remained under acting principals for three years. In February 2025, a newly appointed principal reportedly lost his position following a controversy involving the showering of currency notes on female performers during a welcome party.

His successor was also reportedly removed over allegations, leaving the college once again under an acting principal. Citizens have appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Governor Sardar Saleem Haider to appoint permanent heads of both institutions without further delay. They called for the appointment of capable administrators committed to merit, transparency and institutional reforms to restore the lost prestige of the university and college and prevent students from having to move to other cities for quality education.
