headline: FIC schedules live cardiac surgeries during PHC inspection
description: FAISALABAD - The administration of Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology (FIC) has adopted an unusual approach by scheduling live cardiac surgeries from the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
FAISALABAD - The administration of Faisalabad Institute of Cardiology (FIC) has adopted an unusual approach by scheduling live cardiac surgeries from the hospital’s operation theatres for participants attending a PACVTS conference during the period of Punjab Healthcare Commission inspections, raising questions about the arrangement. The FIC Medical Superintendent Dr. Nadeem Akhtar issued an official order (No.30419-25) on October 29, 2026, stating that teams from the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHC) would conduct inspections at the hospital from November 2 to November 7, 2026. In this regard all heads of departments, doctors, nurses, paramedical staff and other employees were directed to perform their duties according to their respective duty rosters, avoid negligence in their work and refrain from taking leave. The order further stated that strict departmental action would be taken against those who failed to comply with the instructions. On the other hand a two day cardiac surgery conference is being organised at a private hotel by the Pakistan Association of Cardiovascular Surgeons in collaboration with FIC. According to the conference programme, live cardiac surgeries will be broadcast directly from FIC’s operation theatres to participants at the private hotel on Friday 06, November from 8:30 am to 12:30 pm so that young and newly doctors can benefit as much as possible from the professional experience of senior doctors.

However according to the order issued by the MS PHC inspection teams will examine staff attendance, hospital records, emergency services, routine operations and other related matters. Under these circumstances it would become difficult for the operation theatre, anaesthesia, perfusion, nursing and other relevant staff to arrange live surgeries during the inspections. As a result hospital staff is reportedly concerned over the arrangement. When FIC MS Dr Nadeem Akhtar was contacted for his comments on the matter, he stated contrary to the inspection period mentioned in his own official order, that the PHC teams would visit the hospital from November 2 to November 5, while live surgeries would be shown to conference participants on November 6.

headline: Man kills former mother-in-law over divorce dispute
description: Mailsi - A woman was killed and a man critically injured when her former son-in-law, along with his accomplices, allegedly stormed a house and opened fire over
author: Peer Abdul Razaq Qureshi
article_text: Mailsi - A woman was killed and a man critically injured when her former son-in-law, along with his accomplices, allegedly stormed a house and opened fire over a divorce dispute in Chak No. 204/WB, within the jurisdiction of Tibba Sultanpur Police Station. The deceased was identified as Amina Bibi, while Ghulam Shabbir sustained serious injuries and was shifted to Nishtar Hospital Multan in critical condition. According to police, the incident occurred near Danish School, where accused Naveed Iqbal, accompanied by Muhammad Shahbaz and another unidentified person, allegedly entered the house under the cover of darkness and opened indiscriminate fire. The complainant, Muhammad Rafaqat, son of the deceased, told police that his sister was previously married to Naveed Iqbal but the couple had subsequently divorced. He alleged that the accused, along with his accomplices, entered their house over the divorce dispute and shot his mother dead. Following the incident, Tibba Sultanpur police reached the scene, took the body into custody and initiated legal proceedings. SHO Rana Saqib Nazir said a case had been registered on the complainant’s application and raids were being conducted to arrest the nominated suspects. He added that all aspects of the incident were being investigated.

headline: DIG Prisons inspects Bahawalnagar District Jail
description: BAHAWALNAGAR - DIG Prisons Qazi Muhammad Aslam visited District Jail Bahawalnagar and inspected various departments to review facilities provided to inmates,
author: Ali Raza
article_text: BAHAWALNAGAR - DIG Prisons Qazi Muhammad Aslam visited District Jail Bahawalnagar and inspected various departments to review facilities provided to inmates, security arrangements and administrative affairs. Accompanied by Superintendent District Jail Bahawalnagar Syed Hassan Mujtaba, the DIG conducted a detailed inspection of the jail hospital, kitchen, visitors’ shed and other sections. He reviewed cleanliness, food quality, medical facilities, security arrangements and the overall conditions of prisoners. Speaking on the occasion, Qazi Muhammad Aslam said providing the best possible facilities to prisoners was a top priority under the special instructions of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and Inspector General Prisons. He said all available resources were being utilised to ensure proper cleanliness, quality food, medical facilities and effective security arrangements in prisons. He added that treating prisoners humanely and in accordance with the law was a fundamental responsibility of the jail administration. The DIG expressed satisfaction with the administrative affairs and arrangements of various departments at District Jail Bahawalnagar and appreciated the efforts of the jail administration.

headline: False rape cases emerge as new challenge for south Punjab police
description: MUZAFFARGARH - Allegations of the misuse of stringent anti-rape laws to implicate rivals in fabricated cases are emerging as a new challenge for law
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text: MUZAFFARGARH - Allegations of the misuse of stringent anti-rape laws to implicate rivals in fabricated cases are emerging as a new challenge for law enforcement agencies across South Punjab, with a growing number of complaints raising concerns about the credibility of criminal proceedings and the protection of genuine victims. Police records indicate that Muzaffargarh reported the highest number of allegedly fabricated cases among major cities in South Punjab last month, with 27 such cases reported. In October alone, 11 FIRs were reportedly registered in attempts to implicate individuals in false rape cases. Lodhran recorded six similar cases, according to available figures. In a separate development in Multan, an allegation of sexual assault reportedly made after a woman returned from a birthday celebration was also found to be false during the subsequent proceedings, according to police sources. Meanwhile, legal proceedings have been initiated against four individuals, including two women, in Muzaffargarh over allegations of filing false cases. Police have invoked provisions of the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021, and initiated further legal action, including proceedings for penalties where applicable. The first such cases in the area were reportedly registered at Sanawan Police Station, within Sanawan police circle, followed by another case in Qasba Gujrat. In one of the cases, FIR No. 288/26 was registered on the complaint of a woman identified as Bakhtu against a man named Jumma on allegations of rape. Police said the complainant subsequently made a statement before a court in favour of the accused and expressed willingness to compromise. A subsequent review of police records reportedly raised questions about similar complaints allegedly lodged by the woman at different police stations, followed by statements that benefited the nominated accused. Following the review, the SHO of Qasba Gujrat Police Station and SDPO Sanawan Malik Akbar initiated legal proceedings under the Anti-Rape Act 2021. Police case No. 625/26 was reportedly registered at Sanawan Police Station under Sections 22(2)(a) and 22(2)(b) of the Act. The reported action by SDPO Malik Akbar has been welcomed by political, social, business and civil society representatives in Qasba Gujrat, who described the move as an important step towards preventing the misuse of legal provisions and strengthening public confidence in the justice system. They stressed that stringent laws intended to protect women and children must not be exploited to settle personal scores or target opponents. At the same time, they emphasised that genuine survivors of sexual violence must receive protection, dignity and timely justice. The representatives called for impartial investigations, evidence-based prosecutions and strict adherence to due process, saying that accountability must extend to anyone found guilty of deliberately filing fabricated complaints. They also praised SDPO Malik Akbar’s reported initiative, urging law enforcement authorities to ensure that the law is applied without fear or favour across Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu and Layyah. The allegations of false reporting remain subject to independent investigation and judicial determination. Registration of a case does not, by itself, establish guilt.
